job.title: Senior Android Engineer
job.description:
Join our team at the Guardian and be a part of a diverse and inclusive global organisation that delivers fearless, investigative journalism and holds power to account. Our team of award-winning journalists, cutting-edge commercial professionals and industry-leading digital experts are committed to making a difference and represent a wide range of backgrounds and perspectives. We offer a challenging and exciting environment for career development, with a focus on training, growth and fostering an inclusive culture.

 

We are now looking for a Senior Android Developer to join our Apps Experience team. Development of digital products is central to the Guardian. We create our award-winning Android app primarily in Kotlin and Java using Android Studio. We're focussed on providing a fast and stable experience to our users, and our Play Store rating of 4.7 stars is testament to that.

 

You'll work on major new features, as well as improving and maintaining existing functionality for The Guardian’s Android app. As a Senior Developer you’ll take the lead on projects and offer encouragement and guidance to help others to grow. 

 

About the role

 

  • Building and testing major new features, as well as improving and maintaining existing functionality for the app.
  • Working  90%+ in Kotlin, but you may be required to work with Java too.
  • You won't be coding in isolation - our culture is strongly collaborative, whether pair programming with other developers or working closely with other stakeholders. 
  • You can expect to work closely with iOS, server-side, and web engineers, and designers, product managers, editorial and commercial colleagues.
  • You'll take on a leadership role in some of the teams projects
  • You’ll be encouraged to help others grow - you will pass on your expertise to other developers, whilst continuing to grow yourself.
  • Sometimes deciding what code to write is as hard as writing the code itself. As an engineer you'll be involved in product decisions as well as technical ones.
  • You'll strive to be innovative on a daily basis, as well as at our regular hack days.

 

About you

 

  • You have demonstrated expertise in Android development and you have a strong interest in growing your skills.
  • You have strong competence in one or more of modern Android development tools, including Jetpack Compose, Coroutines/Flow, MVVM, Webviews, other Jetpack libraries, and modular app architectures.
  • You test your code and promote a culture of testing. Demonstrate experience with some of JVM unit testing, instrumented testing, and UI regression testing
  • You are comfortable working with both cutting edge technologies as well as legacy code
  • You have experience of, or are willing to take on a leadership role in some team projects
  • You have a rough idea of how iOS development works and you'd like to know more, perhaps even try it yourself.
  • Familiarity with Swift and ObjectiveC for iOS, or Scala and Typescript for server side development is useful. 

 

We actively encourage applications from groups traditionally underrepresented in the UK media

 

Our developers operate in a hybrid environment working 1 day a week from our offices in Kings Cross and 4 days remotely. If you’d like to come in more than that, that’s great too. 

 

We strive for transparency in remuneration where possible. The salary for new Senior Android Developers at the Guardian is £82,000 per year. 

 

We value and respect all differences (seen and unseen) in all people. We aspire to have inclusive working experiences and an environment that reflects the audience we serve, where our people have equal access to career development opportunities, their voices are heard and can contribute to our future. We actively encourage applications from people of all backgrounds. Many of our staff work flexibly and we will consider all requests for flexible working arrangements.

 

How to apply

 

To apply, please upload your latest CV. We don’t require a cover letter but we’ll ask you a question about our android app as part of the application questionnaire. This question should take no longer than 5 minutes to answer, so please factor in the extra time when applying. 

 

We appreciate the time taken to prepare each application we receive. We do not use AI-assisted technology to review applications; every application is reviewed by a member of our recruitment team. Thank you for bearing with us during the screening process. 

 

The closing date for applications is Monday 26th October 2026.

 

All roles at the Guardian are open for everybody to apply. It is important to us that you feel supported and comfortable throughout your recruitment process, in order to perform your best. Please let us know if there are any changes we could make to help your application, this includes providing documents in accessible formats or personalising the process to better support your needs. Please contact Anna Vipers on anna.vipers@theguardian.com to discuss further so we can work with you to support you through your application.

 

Benefits at the Guardian

You'll have 30 days of annual leave per year (plus bank holidays) with the option to purchase an additional 5 days. Our pension scheme is generous; if you contribute 5% then we will contribute 8-12% (depending on your age). We believe in giving back, which is why employees are given 2 volunteering days annually and the option of payroll giving. Season ticket loans are also available.

 

You are entitled to private healthcare, life cover, income protection, and eye tests. You can also opt in to dental insurance.

 

We have enhanced maternity, paternity, adoption and shared parental leave policies in place. We also support our employees by offering an IVF, menopause, baby loss, and trans equality policy.

 

Culture and wellbeing

We want everyone to feel like they belong at the Guardian and we champion diversity of thought. Our various employee forums provide a platform to use their voice to foster an inclusive workplace. We became the first major media organisation to achieve B Corp status.

 

We offer tools to help you prioritise your wellbeing including access to our employee benefits platform which provides tailored support for health and wellbeing. In addition, we also offer free yoga and pilates classes. These run alongside our corporate gym membership and cycle to work scheme.

 

Our canteen has views overlooking the Regents Canal and caters for breakfast, lunch and dinner.

 

Learning and development

We encourage personal and professional growth. Employees have access to a broad range of tools and solutions, and we are happy to support the pursuit of professional qualifications through vocational courses and apprenticeships.

You've owned growth at a high-growth consumer or subscription business, you've seen what works and what doesn't across the funnel, and you'll arrive with a point of view on what we should do. A big part of this role is bringing that experience with you and helping the rest of the company get better at growth.

You'll partner with our staff marketing engineer to direct a small, diligent cross-functional team, and work with them while working across product, marketing, data, and design. This role reports into product and treats marketing as an equal partner in setting priorities. You'll shape a single growth backlog, balancing measurable wins against the longer-term bets worth protecting. You'll build the framework that sizes every growth opportunity on the same terms, so prioritization performs on evidence and expected impact. Ideas and market intelligence come from across the company; you turn the greatest of them into instrumented experiments tied to the product roadmap.

What You’ll Do:

  • Use AI tooling to compress the loop from idea to shipped experiment, multiplying what a small, nimble team can ship
  • Keep the executive team clear on what you're doing, why, and what you're trading off
  • Bring what you've learned on the consumer growth teams you've worked on (and keep learning from the best ones), and adapt it to how artists find and use DistroKid
  • Raise the growth bar across the company, helping PMs and marketers surface and clear their own growth blockers
  • Use and iterate on the artist tools and promo assets we already have to build organic and viral growth loops.

What We're Looking For:

  • 7+ years in product, including 5+ years working directly in growth
  • 3+ years owning a growth number (paying members, conversion, retention, or self-serve revenue) and the metrics that drive it, at a high-growth consumer or subscription business
  • Experience across several parts of the funnel (acquisition, conversion, activation, engagement, retention and churn), not just one step

Our commitment is to be an employer role model, grounded in inclusion and fairness for all.We want every application to receive fair and thoughtful consideration; therefore, all applications are reviewed by a member of our recruitment team, not by AI.

About you

You are an experienced engineering leader with strong knowledge of ERP or similarly complex enterprise platforms and a track record of leading teams responsible for business-critical technology.

You combine people leadership with credible technical judgement. You are comfortable setting direction, making engineering decisions and working with your team on complex technical problems, while creating the ownership and autonomy for engineers to succeed.

You understand that enterprise platform engineering goes beyond implementing configuration or coordinating vendors. You think about the entire technology capability: the core platform, integrations, data flows, extensions, operational processes, security, resilience and how the platform evolves over time.

You are comfortable working closely with Finance and other business stakeholders, translating priorities and requirements into sustainable technology solutions and constructively challenging approaches that create unnecessary complexity or risk.

You are also interested in building capability. You can identify gaps in skills and knowledge, develop engineers and create a team that understands and genuinely owns its technology rather than relying disproportionately on individual specialists or external partners.

About the team

ERP Services sits within Corporate Technology, part of Internal Products, and owns the engineering capabilities supporting critical Finance and enterprise business processes across the FT.

The team is responsible for the engineering, operation and continuous evolution of our ERP technology estate, including Oracle Fusion and the integrations, data flows and supporting capabilities that connect it to the wider FT technology landscape.

ERP Services works closely with Finance, Product, Architecture, Integration & Engineering Services, Security and other Corporate Technology teams to ensure these critical enterprise capabilities remain reliable and can evolve as the needs of the organisation change.

We are strengthening the engineering leadership and platform expertise within ERP Services as part of a wider evolution of the Corporate Technology operating model. The Engineering Lead will establish clear platform and team ownership, reporting to the Principal Engineer – Corporate Technology.

What you’ll work on

As Engineering Lead – ERP Services, you will own the engineering, operation and continuous evolution of the FT’s ERP technology capability.

You will lead the ERP engineering team, providing people leadership, technical direction and clear accountability for the health and performance of the platforms and services the team owns.

A key part of the role will be strengthening our internal ERP engineering capability. You will develop the technical knowledge of the team, establish clear ownership of platforms and services and ensure we have the skills and understanding required to operate and evolve our ERP estate effectively.

You will work closely with Product and Finance stakeholders to understand business priorities and translate them into engineering plans, balancing new capabilities and business change with platform health, technical debt and operational investment.

You will also work with the Principal Engineer and Architecture to ensure decisions within ERP Services support the longer-term direction of Corporate Technology and the wider FT technology estate.

Your responsibilities will include

Engineering & Platform Ownership

  • Owning the engineering, operation and continuous evolution of the ERP technology capability.
  • Providing clear technical direction for the platforms, integrations and supporting services owned by ERP Services.
  • Ensuring ERP platforms remain secure, resilient, scalable, maintainable and appropriately supported.
  • Establishing clear ownership across the team for systems, integrations and technical capabilities.
  • Ensuring engineering decisions consider reliability, security, operability, maintainability, cost and long-term sustainability.
  • Maintaining visibility of platform health, technical debt, lifecycle risks and significant dependencies.
  • Working with the Principal Engineer and Architecture on material technical decisions and longer-term platform direction.
  • Ensuring the team maintains sufficient technical understanding of its platforms to make informed decisions and challenge external recommendations.

People & Engineering Leadership

  • Leading, supporting and developing the engineers within ERP Services.
  • Setting clear expectations and providing regular coaching, feedback and career development.
  • Building a team culture based on ownership, accountability, collaboration and constructive technical challenge.
  • Developing ERP and enterprise platform expertise across the team rather than allowing critical knowledge to remain concentrated in individuals.
  • Identifying capability and skills gaps and developing plans to address them through development, recruitment or appropriate external expertise.
  • Creating opportunities for engineers to take greater technical ownership and develop their leadership capability.
  • Supporting recruitment and building a resilient team with the skills required for the future ERP technology landscape.
  • Ensuring appropriate succession and knowledge sharing across critical areas.

Delivery & Planning

  • Working with Product to translate business priorities and technology strategy into clear engineering plans and deliverable outcomes.
  • Owning engineering planning and resource allocation within ERP Services.
  • Ensuring engineering capacity appropriately balances business change, platform improvement, operational work and technical debt.
  • Identifying technical dependencies, risks and constraints early and ensuring these are visible in planning and prioritisation.
  • Ensuring delivery commitments are realistic and supported by appropriate technical understanding.
  • Working across teams where initiatives involve multiple platforms, integrations or engineering capabilities.
  • Providing clear visibility of engineering progress, risks and trade-offs to Product, technology leadership and relevant stakeholders.

ERP Platform Evolution

  • Developing a clear understanding of the current ERP estate and identifying opportunities to simplify, modernise and improve it.
  • Working with Product, Architecture and the Principal Engineer to shape the longer-term evolution of ERP technology.
  • Evaluating platform capabilities and determining when requirements should be addressed through standard functionality, configuration, integration or other engineering approaches.
  • Challenging unnecessary customisation and complexity where more sustainable solutions are available.
  • Ensuring platform upgrades, new capabilities and significant changes are introduced safely and sustainably.
  • Understanding vendor roadmaps and assessing their implications for the FT's technology direction and investment decisions.
  • Ensuring technical debt and lifecycle concerns are actively managed rather than accumulating through incremental business change.

Integration & Enterprise Technology

  • Ensuring the team understands and owns the integrations and data flows connecting ERP with the wider FT technology estate.
  • Working closely with Integration & Engineering Services and other platform teams to establish clear ownership of cross-system capabilities.
  • Ensuring integrations follow appropriate FT engineering and architectural standards.
  • Identifying opportunities to simplify interfaces, reduce duplication and improve reliability.
  • Supporting technical decisions that span ERP, Tax, People and other Corporate Technology capabilities.
  • Ensuring changes within ERP appropriately consider downstream and upstream impacts.

Operational Excellence & Risk

  • Owning the operational performance of ERP Services and ensuring critical services are appropriately monitored and supported.
  • Establishing effective approaches to observability, incident management, problem management, change management and operational readiness.
  • Ensuring recurring incidents and operational problems are investigated to their underlying causes and addressed sustainably.
  • Maintaining appropriate approaches to resilience, disaster recovery and business continuity.
  • Ensuring relevant security, data governance, compliance and technology standards are met.
  • Maintaining visibility of material operational and technical risks and ensuring appropriate mitigation plans are in place.
  • Using operational insight to inform engineering priorities and platform investment.

Vendors & Technology Partners

  • Managing the technical relationship with ERP vendors, implementation partners and specialist service providers.
  • Ensuring external partners are used effectively while maintaining clear internal engineering ownership.
  • Providing informed technical challenge to vendor recommendations and proposed solutions.
  • Ensuring externally delivered work meets FT engineering, security and operational expectations.
  • Building internal knowledge from vendor and partner engagements rather than allowing expertise to remain externally concentrated.
  • Contributing technical input to vendor performance, technology selection and investment decisions.

Stakeholder & Cross-Team Collaboration

  • Building strong working relationships with Product, Finance and other business stakeholders.
  • Translating business requirements and priorities into clear engineering implications, options and trade-offs.
  • Helping stakeholders understand platform constraints, technical risks and investment requirements.
  • Partnering with the Principal Engineer, Architecture, Security and other engineering leaders on decisions that cross platform or organisational boundaries.
  • Working constructively with specialist engineers, including Tax and Compliance engineering, on shared capabilities and dependencies.
  • Representing ERP Services in relevant engineering and technology forums.
Technical and leadership experience we’re looking for
  • Significant experience leading engineering teams responsible for complex, business-critical enterprise technology.
  • Strong experience with ERP platforms or similarly complex enterprise SaaS ecosystems.
  • Experience with Oracle Fusion or comparable enterprise ERP platforms would be highly advantageous.
  • Experience providing both people leadership and technical leadership to engineering teams.
  • Strong understanding of enterprise platform engineering, including integrations, APIs, data flows and system dependencies.
  • Experience owning technology through its full lifecycle, from change and delivery through to production operation and continuous improvement.
  • Experience developing engineering capability and strengthening technical ownership within teams.
  • Experience working with Finance or other complex enterprise business domains.
  • Strong understanding of reliability, security, observability, operational risk and technology lifecycle management.
  • Experience translating business priorities into engineering plans and balancing feature delivery with platform health and technical investment.
  • Experience leading technical decisions involving enterprise SaaS platforms, integrations and supporting services.
  • Experience working with vendors, implementation partners and managed service providers while maintaining internal technical ownership.
  • Experience identifying and addressing technical debt, platform lifecycle concerns and key-person dependencies.
  • Ability to communicate complex technical considerations and trade-offs clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Experience working effectively with Principal Engineers, architects, Product Managers and other engineering leaders.
  • Experience of major ERP transformation, implementation or modernisation would be advantageous.
Characteristics we value
  • Strong engineering judgement and a willingness to remain close to the technology.
  • A strong sense of ownership and accountability for both the team and the platforms it operates.
  • The ability to develop people while setting clear expectations for engineering quality and delivery.
  • Pragmatism when balancing business priorities, technical quality and operational risk.

  • An appreciation for simplicity, resilience and long-term platform sustainability.

Lifecycle strategy and planning

  • Own lifecycle plans and a portfolio of programmes focused on renewal, retention, cross-sell and upsell, translating the overall B2B lifecycle strategy into quarterly priorities and measurable commercial outcomes.

  • Share successful approaches, insight and innovation across the Experience and Lifecycle Centre of Excellence to help build organisational capability.

  • Coach and support junior lifecycle colleagues, helping develop lifecycle marketing capability and a culture of continuous improvement.

job.title: Podcast Summer Intern
job.description:
About Us 

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading business news organisations, recognised internationally for its authority, integrity, and accuracy.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.

The FT has a record paying readership of 1.6 million, more than 1.4 million of which are digital subscriptions. It is part of Nikkei Inc., which provides a broad range of information, news, and services for the global business community. We have offices in more than 35 countries, including London, New York, Hong Kong, Beijing, Manila, Sofia, San Francisco, and Tokyo.

 

Our Internships

We are looking for passionate and motivated students who are interested in pursuing a career in audio journalism and production to join our team! We expect our interns to be in the office a minimum of three days a week. 

This program is a paid, ten week summer internship and offers the opportunity to connect and collaborate across the FT — in the US and globally. You’ll develop ideas that help drive our growth, present your work to US leadership, and gain valuable insights from across the business. Plus, you’ll be paired with a dedicated Buddy to provide mentorship and support throughout your experience.

This internship pays $22 per hour for 40 hours per week and runs from June 7, 2027 - Aug 13, 2027. Before applying, please ensure you will be available on these dates.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the US.

Role overview

The internship will offer hands-on experience pitching, reporting and producing audio stories for the FT’s flagship daily podcast, the FT News Briefing.We are looking for candidates with a proven interest in multimedia journalism and some experience in podcast production. Knowledge of business, economics and financial markets is an advantage, and having the ideas and initiative to propose stories and execute them is a must. 

 

Key responsibilities

  • Researching and pitching audio story ideas which draw from the full range of FT coverage: business, finance and culture
  • Gathering tape and archive audio to bring stories to life 
  • Coordinating and recording interview with FT journalists and other guests
  • Producing and editing elements of the FT News Briefing, with guidance from its team leader

 

Required skills/experience

  • Journalism degree preferred
  • Audio or podcast experience preferred (Internship or other courses)
  • Good writing and editing skills
  • Strong communication and organisational skills
  • Interest in finance and business news
  • Must have experience working with Descript or similar editing software

 

Please submit your application by November 2nd by 5pm Eastern Time and be sure to include the following documents in your application:

  • Resume
  • A cover letter explaining why you would be a good fit, explaining your interest in joining our team and why you’re interested in making financial news and  concepts accessible to a broad audience.

Any application submitted after the deadline will not be considered.

The use of AI

Original reporting, great writing and intelligent commentary lie at the heart of FT journalism. Our readers trust us to produce quality journalism that is accurate, fair and insightful. For this reason, FT editorial staff do not use AI tools to write articles or create reader-facing content.

AI may be used in specific, pre-approved cases to assist with research, such as in data investigations. We expect internship applicants to refrain from using AI in writing tests or written materials submitted during the application process. All submissions must reflect your own knowledge, skills, and experiences.

Candidates may use AI to assist with research and interview preparation. However, the use of AI throughout the application process is monitored to ensure fairness and transparency for all applicants.

Our Product & Tech teams drive us forward in an ever-evolving digital landscape, delivering cutting-edge products to over one million digital subscribers daily. Our growth relies on a diverse, dedicated and dynamic group of product, tech, delivery and data specialists.

With a supportive culture, entrepreneurial spirit and opportunities at every turn, there are no limits to where your FT career can take you.

Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

Our commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion

We believe in the power of unique perspectives and want all voices in our organisation to be heard, respected and valued. A supportive workplace is one where employees feel they can be themselves and operate to their full potential. We are committed to removing barriers for everyone, with a focus on addressing those faced by underrepresented groups.

About you

You are an experienced Principal Engineer or senior engineering leader with a strong background in enterprise integration, shared engineering services or platform capabilities.

You have experience working across multiple teams and technology domains, with the judgement to distinguish between capabilities that should be centrally owned and standardised and those that should remain within individual engineering teams.

You are comfortable operating at both strategic and technical levels. You can define a direction for shared integration and engineering capabilities while still engaging deeply enough with architecture, engineering practices, reliability and delivery to make credible technical decisions.

You are also an experienced people leader who can build and develop senior engineers and create a high-performing team around a new capability. You are able to influence teams without relying solely on formal authority and can establish common approaches where responsibilities have historically been distributed.

You understand that shared services succeed only when they are useful to the teams that depend on them. You therefore approach platform and integration engineering pragmatically, balancing standardisation and reuse with the needs of individual products and domains.

About the team

Integration Services sits within Internal Products and provides shared engineering capabilities that enable connectivity, automation and engineering quality across the organisation.

The capability spans enterprise integrations, reusable engineering services and quality engineering practices that support multiple products, platforms and teams across Internal Products.

As the FT continues to evolve its enterprise technology landscape and undertake significant transformation, the need for consistent, reusable and reliable integration capabilities is increasing.

Two major programmes are currently running in parallel and both depend heavily on shared integration capabilities across multiple platforms and teams. At present, responsibilities are distributed across different parts of the organisation, creating risks around fragmented ownership, duplicated solutions, inconsistent approaches and limited reuse.

The Principal Engineer – Integration Services will establish and lead this capability, creating clear ownership for shared services while ensuring the team remains closely connected to the engineering teams and domains it supports.

What you’ll work on

As Principal Engineer – Integration Services, you will establish and lead the Integration Services capability across Internal Products.

You will own the technical direction, engineering capability, people leadership, delivery and operational performance of shared integration and engineering services.

A key part of the role will be defining what should become a reusable Internal Products capability and what should remain owned within individual domains. You will establish common integration approaches, reusable services and engineering patterns that reduce duplication and make it easier for teams to connect systems safely and reliably.

You will provide senior technical leadership across major transformation programmes, including the Commercial Technology Programme, ensuring integration decisions made within individual programmes contribute to a coherent and sustainable technology estate.

You will also build and develop the team itself, establishing the engineering capability, operating model and ways of working required for a successful shared service organisation.

Your responsibilities will include

Integration Strategy & Technical Direction

  • Defining the technical direction for integration services across Internal Products.
  • Establishing principles, standards and reusable patterns for enterprise integration.
  • Developing a clear strategy for shared integration capabilities, balancing centralisation, reuse and domain autonomy.
  • Identifying opportunities to simplify integration architecture, reduce duplication and improve interoperability.
  • Providing technical leadership on significant integration decisions spanning multiple platforms, teams and domains.
  • Ensuring integration approaches consider security, resilience, scalability, observability, operability and long-term maintainability.
  • Working with Architecture and senior engineering leaders to align integration direction with wider FT technology strategy.
  • Establishing a clear view of the integration landscape, including major interfaces, dependencies, ownership and technical risks.

Shared Services & Platform Engineering

  • Defining and building reusable integration services and engineering capabilities that solve common problems across Internal Products.
  • Establishing clear ownership for shared services and ensuring they have sustainable operational and engineering models.
  • Ensuring shared capabilities provide genuine value to consuming teams rather than becoming additional layers of complexity.
  • Setting appropriate expectations for reliability, performance, scalability, security and service availability.
  • Establishing effective lifecycle management for shared platforms and services.
  • Identifying opportunities for standardisation, consolidation and reuse.
  • Ensuring teams have clear guidance on when to use shared services and when to build capability within their own domains.

Engineering Quality & Automation

  • Establishing and evolving quality engineering capabilities that improve the reliability and confidence of software delivery across Internal Products.
  • Promoting consistent engineering practices around testing, automation, CI/CD and quality assurance where appropriate.
  • Identifying recurring quality problems across teams and developing reusable approaches to address them.
  • Working with engineering leaders to improve automated testing, release confidence and software quality.
  • Encouraging engineering teams to treat quality as part of engineering ownership rather than a separate activity.
  • Using metrics, operational insight and engineering feedback to identify opportunities for continuous improvement.

Strategic Programmes & Transformation

  • Providing senior engineering leadership to major transformation programmes, including the Commercial Technology Programme.
  • Working across programme teams to establish coherent integration strategies across multiple platforms and workstreams.
  • Challenging programme-specific solutions where they create unnecessary duplication, complexity or long-term dependency.
  • Ensuring integration decisions made during transformation can be sustainably operated and evolved after programme delivery ends.
  • Supporting technology and vendor evaluations where integration architecture is a material consideration.
  • Helping programmes distinguish between capabilities that should be delivered as reusable Internal Products services and those that are specific to an individual initiative.

People & Engineering Leadership

  • Leading and developing the engineers within Integration Services.
  • Establishing a high-performing team with clear responsibilities, strong engineering standards and appropriate technical ownership.
  • Coaching senior engineers and developing technical leadership capability within the team.
  • Building an environment that encourages collaboration, constructive technical challenge and knowledge sharing.
  • Recruiting and developing the specialist skills required to build a sustainable integration capability.
  • Creating succession and reducing key-person dependency across critical integration knowledge.
  • Establishing clear expectations for engineering quality, operational performance and delivery.
  • Building strong relationships with engineering leaders across Internal Products so the shared capability is embedded rather than operating as a separate silo.

Delivery & Planning

  • Establishing a roadmap for the development and evolution of shared integration services.
  • Prioritising investment across reusable capabilities, programme commitments, operational work and technical improvement.
  • Working with Product and engineering leaders to understand demand for shared services and translate this into realistic delivery plans.
  • Managing capacity and ensuring the team can support both strategic initiatives and ongoing operational responsibilities.
  • Identifying dependencies and delivery risks across consuming teams and programmes.
  • Providing clear visibility of progress, risks, trade-offs and technical constraints.

Operational Excellence & Reliability

  • Owning the operational performance of shared integration services.
  • Establishing appropriate approaches to monitoring, observability, incident management, problem management and operational readiness.
  • Ensuring critical integrations have clear ownership, appropriate resilience and effective recovery mechanisms.
  • Leading the response to significant incidents affecting shared services and coordinating resolution across dependent teams.
  • Using operational data and incident learning to identify systemic improvements.
  • Ensuring operational responsibilities are sustainable and do not depend disproportionately on individual engineers.

Cross-Domain Collaboration

  • Building strong working relationships with Principal Engineers, Engineering Managers, architects and senior engineers across Internal Products.
  • Establishing effective mechanisms for teams to engage with Integration Services early in the lifecycle of significant initiatives.
  • Helping teams understand integration trade-offs and select appropriate patterns and capabilities.
  • Coordinating decisions where integration ownership crosses domain boundaries.
  • Encouraging reuse and consistency without imposing unnecessary central control.
  • Representing Integration Services in relevant architecture, engineering and technology forums across the FT.

Vendor & Technology Partner Management

  • Providing technical leadership in relationships with integration technology vendors and implementation partners.
  • Challenging vendor-led solutions where they conflict with long-term FT engineering direction or create unnecessary dependency.
  • Ensuring external partners complement rather than replace internal engineering capability.
  • Contributing to technology evaluation, procurement and platform selection decisions.
  • Ensuring partner-delivered work meets FT engineering, security, quality and operational expectations.

Technical and leadership experience we’re looking for

  • Significant experience in a Principal Engineer, senior engineering leadership or comparable technical leadership role.
  • Strong experience designing, building and operating enterprise integration capabilities at scale.
  • Deep understanding of integration architecture, APIs, event-driven systems, messaging, data flows and distributed systems.
  • Experience establishing reusable engineering services or shared platform capabilities across multiple teams.
  • Experience defining technical standards, engineering patterns or platform strategies across organisational boundaries.
  • Experience leading significant transformation programmes involving multiple platforms, teams and integrations.
  • Strong understanding of cloud technologies and modern engineering practices, preferably AWS.
  • Experience with enterprise SaaS ecosystems and integrating them with internally developed applications.
  • Experience with quality engineering, test automation, CI/CD and engineering productivity practices would be advantageous.
  • Experience leading and developing senior engineers and technical specialists.
  • Experience establishing new teams, capabilities or operating models would be highly advantageous.
  • Strong experience influencing teams and senior stakeholders without relying solely on formal authority.
  • Experience identifying and addressing duplicated capabilities, technical debt and fragmented ownership across complex technology estates.
  • Strong understanding of reliability, observability, security and operational excellence.
  • Experience working with vendors and implementation partners while maintaining clear internal technical ownership.
  • Ability to communicate complex technical concepts and trade-offs clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Experience balancing strategic technical direction with practical delivery realities.

Characteristics we value

  • Strong technical judgement and the confidence to make decisions across organisational boundaries.
  • A strong sense of ownership and accountability.
  • Pragmatism when balancing standardisation, reuse and the needs of individual engineering teams.
  • The ability to influence without relying solely on hierarchy.
  • A collaborative approach to building shared capabilities that teams want to use.
  • Curiosity and a willingness to understand problems across the wider technology estate rather than optimising a single domain.
  • Strong coaching and mentoring skills, particularly when developing senior engineers.
  • An instinct for reducing unnecessary complexity and duplication.
  • Confidence challenging established approaches constructively.
  • Calm and clear decision-making during complex delivery and operational situations.
  • An appreciation for reusable, sustainable and well-engineered technology capabilities.

What’s in it for you? Our benefits

Our benefits vary by location, but we are committed to providing best-in-class perks across all our offices. These include generous annual leave, medical cover, inclusive parental leave packages, subsidised gym memberships and opportunities to give back to the community. Full details of our benefits are available on the FT Careers website.

We’ve embraced a 50% hybrid working model (averaging two to three days onsite) that fosters trust and remote adaptability while encouraging in-person camaraderie and peer learning. Additionally, we are open to accommodating specific flexible working pattern requests for all roles where feasible.

Accessibility

job.title: Senior Process & Knowledge Specialist (Customer Care)
job.description:
About Us:

The FT has an uncompromising mission: delivering independent, quality information, news and services to individuals and companies around the globe. It’s the cornerstone of our reputation and the heart of our ambitions for the future. But for our people, the FT offers so much more than what we do. FT people come from all kinds of backgrounds and work across a huge range of disciplines and locations, and find empowering, warm and welcoming culture that values curiosity and rewards smart, ambitious thinking. Those who are willing to unite around our mission and live our values will find plenty to challenge, inspire and interest them. Like the audiences we serve, no two FT people are the same; but together we help our audience be better informed and understand the world around them. It’s a job that’s never mattered more, and a career that can take you anywhere you want to go. 

Our commitment to diversity and inclusion in the workplace:

At the FT, we give all employees a voice so that diverse perspectives are heard and valued. We believe that a supportive workplace is one where employees feel they can be themselves at work. We'll continue to remove barriers for all, and in particular, barriers facing employees from underrepresented groups. 

About the role:

The Senior Process & Knowledge Specialist (internal business title) is responsible for driving the strategic development, governance, and continuous improvement of Customer Care operational processes and knowledge management practices. The role designs and governs the operational knowledge and process ecosystem, ensuring workflows, operational guidance, and knowledge assets are structured, scalable, and aligned to support consistent, efficient, and customer-focused service delivery across agent, self-service, and AI-assisted support experiences.

Working collaboratively across Customer Care and key business functions, the role plays a key part in enhancing operational efficiency, agent and customer experience, process consistency, and knowledge effectiveness. The role also oversees the ongoing optimisation of the Customer Care knowledge base, ensuring content remains accessible, compliant, and aligned with evolving operational and business needs.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Define, manage, and continuously improve the structure, governance, usability, and discoverability of the Customer Care knowledge base, ensuring the content is intuitive, accurate, scalable, and effectively supports agent, self-service, and AI-assisted Customer Care experiences.
  • Design and optimise operational workflows, process guidance, policies, and decision-making tools that simplify complex processes, improve agent experience, and support Customer Care teams in fast-paced operational environments.
  • Ensure knowledge content and operational guidance are designed with both agent and customer experience in mind, balancing usability, compliance, and operational efficiency.
  • Define and oversee standards for operational knowledge content, workflows, and guidance, ensuring information is structured, scalable, operationally effective, and aligned across internal, customer-facing, and AI-assisted support channels.
  • Manage and optimise the Customer Care knowledge base platform, including Salesforce Knowledge, ensuring content governance, change requests, updates, approvals, and standards supporting AI-assisted support experiences are effectively administered and prioritised.
  • Analyse operational workflows, customer journeys, and knowledge content to identify inefficiencies, gaps, risks, inconsistencies, and opportunities to enhance customer experience, self-service effectiveness, operational efficiency, and scalable service delivery.
  • Collaborate with stakeholders across Customer Care and other business functions to gather requirements, align processes, and deliver continuous improvements across workflows, knowledge management practices, and supporting tools.
  • Champion knowledge management best practices, industry trends, and continuous improvement initiatives, and promote the adoption of knowledge base tools, content standards, and process improvements across Customer Care.
  • Ensure all operational guidance, policies, and process documentation are accurate, compliant, and regularly reviewed in alignment with legal, regulatory, and business requirements.
  • Lead and facilitate process review discussions, workshops, and stakeholder sessions to support operational alignment and improvement initiatives.
  • Utilise QM data, AI-driven insights, analytics, user feedback, and content performance metrics to improve knowledge structure, discoverability, content effectiveness, process usability, operational efficiency, and overall Customer Care and customer experience.
  • Maintain a strong understanding of Customer Care products, services, policies, systems, and operational processes to ensure knowledge content remains accurate and relevant.
  • Provide support to the Quality Manager as required for improvements across the Customer Care team.

Core Competencies

Experience

  • Proven background in knowledge management, process improvement, operational excellence, business process analysis, or similar roles within Customer Care, Customer Service, or Contact Centre environments.
  • Design, documentation, and optimisation of operational workflows, policies, process maps, and agent-facing guidance using formats such as written guidance, visual workflows, and quick-reference materials.
  • Identification of operational gaps, inefficiencies, risks, and opportunities for improvement, with the ability to recommend and support effective solutions.
  • Management of knowledge management platforms, content governance processes, and knowledge base administration, including Salesforce Knowledge or similar systems.
  • Structuring and governance of knowledge content to support consistent experiences across agent, self-service, and AI-assisted support channels.
  • Collaboration with Global teams across Customer Care and other business functions to support operational alignment and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Utilisation of operational data, customer or user feedback, and performance trends to support decision-making, process optimisation, and content improvements.
  • Support of operational change, continuous improvement initiatives, and process optimisation activities.
  • Use of AI tools, analytics, or technology solutions to support knowledge management, operational efficiency, or process improvements.
  • Understanding of process improvement and continuous improvement methodologies, including familiarity with frameworks such as Lean, Six Sigma, or Kaizen.
  • Proficiency with Google Workspace with a solid command of its core features.

Skills & Behaviours

  • Strategic mindset with the ability to balance customer experience, operational efficiency, scalability, and business objectives when designing processes and knowledge solutions.
  • Excellent writing, editing, communication, presentation, and facilitation skills, with the ability to translate complex operational information into clear, structured, and user-friendly guidance for diverse audiences.
  • Strong capabilities in workflow, process design, and information architecture, creating logical, intuitive, and operationally effective experiences for Customer Care teams and customers.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical-thinking skills, with the ability to identify trends, gaps, risks, inefficiencies, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Strong understanding of operational usability and agent experience, ensuring guidance is practical and effective within fast-paced customer service environments.
  • High attention to detail, ensuring accuracy, consistency, compliance, and reliability across operational processes and knowledge content.
  • Strong stakeholder management, collaboration, and influencing skills, working effectively across teams, functions, and seniority levels.
  • Leadership mindset with the ability to drive alignment, support operational change, champion continuous improvement initiatives, and challenge the status quo through a proactive and solutions-focused approach.
  • Data-driven mindset, confidently using analytics, AI tools, operational insights, and performance trends to inform recommendations and improve knowledge effectiveness, operational efficiency, and user experience.
  • Strong organisational and prioritisation skills, effectively managing multiple projects and requests amid changing priorities.
  • Adaptable and collaborative team player, motivated by continuous learning and improving customer, agent, and business outcomes.
  • Schedule flexibility, with a willingness to work UK hours, ability to adapt to shifting timelines, and support during public holidays.

Customer Care Values 

  • Customer-Centric: We put the customer at the heart of everything we do, going above and beyond to deliver the gold-standard service our customers expect and deserve.
  • Collaborative: We believe in the power of individuals and teams working together across different roles and responsibilities in a respectful and open-minded way so that we can deliver the best customer outcomes.
  • Accountable: We act with integrity, whilst taking responsibility for our performance and personal growth, to ensure that we give our best to both customers and colleagues.
  • Resilient: We are adaptable, flexible and brave, maintaining a positive attitude during times of challenge and change, so that we can respond to the needs of our customers and the FT.
  • Effective: We are creative and productive whilst remaining focused on our goals with a results-driven approach so that we deliver the right outcomes for our customers and for the FT.

What’s in it for you? Our Benefits:

Our benefits vary depending on location, but we are committed to providing best-in-class perks across all our offices as well as an inclusive environment to develop your career. Examples of our benefits include: generous annual leave, flexible working (including working from home), health coverage (medical & dental), company match and enhanced family leave packages. Full details of our benefits can be found here.

Further Information:

The FT is committed to providing an inclusive working environment for all. We are an equal opportunities employer who seeks to recruit and appoint the best talent regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion and/or belief. We also promote flexible working and will consider specific requests around flexibility for all roles where it can be accommodated. Please let us know if you require any adjustments as part of the application process or to enable you to attend an interview. If you would like to discuss your requirements or have any questions, please contact a member of our HR team, who will be happy to help.

job.title: Senior Talent Acquisition Specialist (9 month parental leave cover)
job.description:
About us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.

In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing.

Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and inspire you. With no fixed path, you’ll discover new skills and forge a career that can take you anywhere.

Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

Our commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion

We believe in the power of unique perspectives and want all voices in our organisation to be heard, respected and valued. A supportive workplace is one where employees feel they can be themselves and operate to their full potential. We are committed to removing barriers for everyone, with a focus on addressing those faced by underrepresented groups.

The Role

The Financial Times is looking for an experienced Senior Talent Acquisition Specialist to join our global Talent Acquisition team on a 9-month fixed-term contract.

This is a hands-on recruitment delivery role managing a varied and fast-moving portfolio of vacancies across the FT. Working across multiple business areas, including commercial, corporate support, GTM and technology. You will manage recruitment at a range of levels, including senior, specialist and business-critical appointments, while partnering with stakeholders across our global organisation.

You will take ownership of the full recruitment lifecycle, from initial role briefing and market assessment through sourcing, screening, interview management and offer. You will independently manage approximately 15–18 live requisitions at any one time, including the associated scheduling and candidate communication.

While the role will primarily support UK hiring, you will also recruit across other regions, particularly the US and APAC, according to business demand.

This is an opportunity for an experienced in-house recruiter who enjoys being close to recruitment delivery and can move confidently between different functions, levels and geographies, build credibility with senior stakeholders and personally drive searches through to successful appointments.

Key Responsibilities

  • Independently manage a portfolio of approximately 15–18 concurrent requisitions, taking ownership from initial briefing through to accepted offer.
  • Deliver recruitment across a broad range of functions adapting your approach to different roles and talent markets.
  • Manage recruitment across a range of levels, including senior, specialist and business-critical appointments.
  • Lead detailed role briefings with hiring managers to establish requirements, assessment criteria, recruitment strategy and realistic hiring timelines.
  • Write and optimise job adverts and determine appropriate attraction and sourcing strategies for each vacancy.
  • Proactively identify and engage passive candidates through LinkedIn Recruiter, direct headhunting, talent mapping, referrals and other appropriate channels.
  • Screen and assess candidates against agreed requirements and provide hiring managers with clear, evidence-based recommendations.
  • Design and manage effective interview and assessment processes in partnership with hiring managers.
  • Own interview scheduling and candidate communication, providing a responsive and high-quality candidate experience throughout.
  • Manage offer delivery and negotiation, working with People colleagues and hiring managers to secure successful appointments.
  • Deliver recruitment through direct sourcing and attraction channels without reliance on recruitment agencies.
  • Build trusted relationships with hiring managers and senior leaders, advising and constructively challenging recruitment strategy, candidate quality, market conditions, assessment and hiring decisions.
  • Provide clear updates on recruitment progress, pipeline health, risks and recommended actions, and lead structured interview wash-ups and selection discussions.
  • Partner with HR Business Partners and other People colleagues to understand priorities and anticipate recruitment requirements.
  • Manage recruitment across UK, US and APAC markets according to business needs, working effectively across different locations and time zones.
  • Develop proactive sourcing strategies and build strong and diverse pipelines for specialist and hard-to-fill vacancies.
  • Champion fair and inclusive recruitment practices and advise hiring managers on structured and inclusive assessment approaches.
  • Maintain accurate and timely recruitment data in Greenhouse and Workday, monitor pipelines and take proactive action to keep recruitment moving.
  • Use recruitment data and market insight to inform search strategies and stakeholder conversations.

Required Skills and Experience

  • Significant end-to-end talent acquisition experience, ideally within a complex, international organisation and/or fast-paced in-house recruitment environment.
  • Demonstrable experience independently managing a high-volume portfolio of concurrent vacancies while maintaining a strong candidate and stakeholder experience.
  • Broad recruitment experience across multiple functions, including GTM, commercial and corporate support. Technology recruitment experience is desirable. 
  • Experience recruiting at a range of levels, including senior and specialist appointments, with confidence partnering directly with senior stakeholders.
  • Experience managing recruitment across multiple countries or regions, ideally including exposure to UK, US and/or APAC hiring.
  • Strong direct sourcing and headhunting capability, including identifying and engaging passive candidates for difficult-to-fill roles.
  • Confidence managing recruitment independently from sourcing and screening through interview management, candidate communication and offer negotiation, without dedicated coordinator or sourcer support.
  • Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the confidence to advise, challenge and manage expectations constructively.
  • Excellent organisation and prioritisation skills, with the ability to maintain momentum across multiple competing recruitment processes.
  • Strong judgement and assessment skills, including the ability to understand unfamiliar roles and identify the capabilities required for success.
  • Experience applying inclusive recruitment practices and supporting fair, structured candidate assessment.
  • Confidence using recruitment data and market insight to inform hiring strategies and stakeholder conversations.
  • Experience using an Applicant Tracking System, ideally Greenhouse or similar. 
  • A proactive, pragmatic and delivery-focused approach, with the ability to work autonomously and remain effective in a fast-moving environment.

What's in it for You?

Our benefits vary by location but we are committed to providing best-in-class perks across all our offices. These include generous annual leave, medical cover, inclusive parental leave packages, subsidised gym memberships and opportunities to give back to the community. Full details of our benefits are available here.

We currently operate a hybrid model which requires staff to work onsite 50% of the time, subject to role requirements & regular review. While flexible working requests will be considered, not all patterns are suitable for all roles. We believe this balanced approach supports flexibility and protects our culture, making collaboration and communication easier, building stronger relationships and team cohesion, and supporting peer learning. We reserve discretion on reasonable notice to change this approach either generally or for specific individuals or teams.

Accessibility

We are a disability confident employer and Valuable 500 signatory.

Please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments/personalisation as part of the application process or to enable you to attend an interview. If you would like to discuss your requirements or have any questions, email talent@ft.com and a member of our team will be happy to help.

Further Information

At the FT, we embrace innovation and the use of technology and appreciate that individuals may leverage AI tools as part of their job application process. Whilst we are happy for you to use AI to assist with your application, it is essential that all information provided is authentic and accurately represents your skills, experience, and qualifications.

Candidates should be aware that the use of AI throughout the application process may be monitored to ensure a fair and transparent hiring process for all.

Please beware of fraudulent job postings and offers claiming to be from the Financial Times. All legitimate opportunities will direct you to apply through the official Financial Times careers site, and the FT will never ask for financial information, payments, or referrals to third parties during the hiring process. If you have any concerns about the legitimacy of a job posting or suspect any scam activity, please contact talent@ft.com.

job.title: US Data Journalist
job.description:
About us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.

In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing.

Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and inspire you. With no fixed path, you’ll discover new skills and forge a career that can take you anywhere.

Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

 

The role

The FT’s visual and data journalism team is looking for an experienced data journalist to cover US politics, economics and financial news. This is a full-time staff position.

The successful applicant will collaborate with US-based news editors and correspondents across North America as well as colleagues in London, Hong Kong and beyond. You’ll help us deliver compelling journalism on our core coverage areas of trade, economics and financial markets, as well as US electoral politics and campaign finance. 

You will have a record of working self-sufficiently, from story pitch to final product, and an interest in providing a global perspective for both US and overseas readers. You will also collaborate with the wider Visual & Data Journalism team, and reporters and editors from across the FT’s network who need support applying data-driven methods to their work. 

We are happy to consider candidates wishing to be based in Washington DC or New York City. External applicants must be eligible to work in the US.

Occasional weekend/flexible working may be required as part of covering fast-moving news.

 

Essential skills

You will have a strong portfolio of work in data journalism, ideally focused on business, finance, economics or politics in North America. In addition, we are looking for:

  • Experience using data journalism or data science techniques to find and tell news stories
  • Confidence using R or Python for data sourcing (including web scraping, APIs and large databases), cleaning and analysis
  • Excellent communication skills, particularly the ability to explain your quantitative analysis work simply to non-specialist audiences
  • A passion for continuously learning in order to keep your skills at the forefront of current practice
  • The ability to pitch, write and deliver original data driven stories

 

Desirable Skills

While this is not a graphics-production role, experience of using data visualisation effectively in reporting would be a distinct advantage. 

In addition, while we don’t expect you to have all of these skills, any of the following would be beneficial, so please mention them in your cover letter and résumé:

  • Training in statistics, data science or quantitative social science methods
  • Experience building, maintaining or working with pipelines for continuously acquiring and processing data
  • Experience applying data analysis in financial or business journalism
  • Knowledge of working collaboratively with others on coding projects using version control systems such as Git
  • Familiarity with Adobe Illustrator 

 

Please submit your application by the end of the day, Friday 6th November 2026. 

 

Salary range

A reasonable estimate of the salary range for this role is $85,000 to $115,000. To ensure pay fairness, the successful candidate will be offered a salary within the estimated salary range based on a number of considerations including but not limited to: skill set; experience and training; certifications; and other business and organisational needs. This position is represented by the News Guild.

 

The use of AI

Original reporting, great writing and intelligent commentary lie at the heart of FT journalism. Our readers trust us to produce quality journalism that is accurate, fair and insightful. This is why FT editorial staff do not by default use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to write articles or create other reader-facing content. For specific and pre-approved cases, AI can be harnessed for certain tasks, such as assisting data research for investigations.  

We expect applicants to the FT newsroom to refrain from using AI in their test submissions, and any written materials should be a genuine reflection of their own knowledge, skills and experiences. We encourage candidates only to employ AI as a tool to help with research and interview readiness for a role. 

Candidates should be aware that the use of AI throughout the application process is monitored to ensure a fair and transparent hiring process for all.

 

Our commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion 

We believe in the power of unique perspectives and want all voices in our organisation to be heard, respected and valued. A supportive workplace is one where employees feel they can be themselves and operate to their full potential. We are committed to removing barriers for everyone, with a focus on addressing those faced by underrepresented groups.

 

What’s in it for you? Our benefits

Our benefits vary by location but we are committed to providing best-in-class perks across all our offices. These include generous annual leave, medical cover, inclusive parental leave packages, subsidised gym memberships and opportunities to give back to the community. Full details of our benefits are available here.

FT Newsroom staff are expected to work onsite a minimum of three days per week, subject to role requirements and regular review. While flexible working requests will be considered, not all patterns are suitable for Editorial roles.

 

Accessibility
