job.title: US Summer Newsroom Intern
job.description:
About us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading business news organisations, recognised internationally for its authority, integrity, and accuracy.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.

In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing. 

The FT has a record paying readership of 1.6 million, more than 1.4 million of which are digital subscriptions. It is part of Nikkei Inc., which provides a broad range of information, news, and services for the global business community. We have offices in more than 35 countries, including London, New York, Hong Kong, Beijing, Manila, Sofia, San Francisco, and Tokyo.

Our Internships

We are looking for passionate and motivated students who are interested in pursuing a career in media to join our team! We expect our interns to be in the office a minimum of three days a week. 

This program offers the opportunity to connect and collaborate across the FT — in the US and globally. You’ll develop ideas that help drive our growth, present your work to US leadership, and gain valuable insights from across the business. Plus, you’ll be paired with a dedicated Buddy to provide mentorship and support throughout your experience.

This internship pays $22 per hour for 40 hours per week and runs from June 7, 2027 - Aug 13, 2027. Before applying, please ensure you will be available on these dates.

Applicants must be authorised to work in the US.

Role Overview

The FT’s US newsroom internship offers aspiring journalists a front-row seat to the fast-paced world of global news. This is your chance to learn from and contribute to a dynamic multimedia newsroom that values curiosity, creativity, and sharp storytelling.

No two days are the same. From breaking stories and in-depth research to innovative digital projects, you’ll work alongside editors and reporters to bring ambitious journalism to life. We’re looking for versatile, driven interns who are eager to dig into stories that matter and help shape how the world understands the news.

Key responsibilities

  • Pitching, reporting, and writing original news stories
  • Conducting interviews and developing sources
  • Assisting senior correspondents with research, document analysis and reporting
  • Curating newsletters and contributing to digital projects
  • Collaborating with staffers on special projects

Required skills / experience

  • Proven interest in journalism
  • Some experience or knowledge of financial journalism, business, economics, or related areas
  • Curiosity about global markets, companies, and economies
  • Initiative to pitch and complete story ideas
  • Ability to work independently and meet deadlines
  • Excellent research and analytical skills
  • Strong communication and writing skills across platforms
  • Sound news judgment and high ethical standards

Please submit your application by November 2nd by 5pm Eastern Time and be sure to include the following documents in your application:

  • Resume
  • A cover letter explaining why you would be a good fit, and explaining your interest in joining our team
  • Three writing samples or published clips

Any application submitted after the deadline will not be considered.

The use of AI

Original reporting, great writing and intelligent commentary lie at the heart of FT journalism. Our readers trust us to produce quality journalism that is accurate, fair and insightful. For this reason, FT editorial staff do not use AI tools to write articles or create reader-facing content.

AI may be used in specific, pre-approved cases to assist with research, such as in data investigations. We expect internship applicants to refrain from using AI in writing tests or written materials submitted during the application process. All submissions must reflect your own knowledge, skills, and experiences.

Candidates may use AI to assist with research and interview preparation. However, the use of AI throughout the application process is monitored to ensure fairness and transparency for all applicants.

Our commitment to a fair and inclusive workplace

At the FT, we are committed to creating a fair and inclusive workplace where everyone has equal opportunity to succeed. We welcome and value different perspectives and strive to ensure all employees are heard and supported. We believe people do their best work when they can be themselves and have the flexibility they need to balance their work and personal lives. We are an equal opportunity employer and align with all applicable laws prohibiting discrimination.

Accessibility

We are a disability confident employer and Valuable 500 signatory.

Please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments/personalisation as part of the application process or to enable you to attend an interview. If you would like to discuss your requirements or have any questions, email talent@ft.com and a member of our team will be happy to help.

job.title: Senior Workday Financial Reporting Manager
job.description:
This is a remote US position that must be worked within Pacific Time core business hours.

 

 

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 

The Senior Workday Financial Reporting Manager is responsible for overseeing the preparation and distribution of financial statements in compliance with regulatory requirements and company policies. You will ensure the accuracy and integrity of financial reporting, assist with external audits, and implement best practices in financial disclosure. You have a strong background in GAAP/IFRS, SEC reporting (if applicable), and financial analysis.

 

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 

  • Report Development: Design, build, test, and maintain custom Advanced, Matrix, Composite, and standard Workday reports using calculated fields and Business Objects.
  • System Maintenance & Upgrades: Test, review, and update existing reports during Workday's bi-annual releases to maintain functionality.
  • Dashboard Creation: Design and manage operational dashboards, Discovery Boards, and Report-as-a-Service (RaaS) outputs, partnering with the Financial Analyst, to track key performance indicators (KPIs) for leadership.
  • Prepare and update financial statement templates.
  • Oversee internal financial reporting processes and implement controls to maintain accuracy and efficiency.
  • Manage the preparation of quarterly and annual reports.
  • Participate in monthly, quarterly, and year-end closing process.
  • Collaborate with internal teams to gather report parameters.
  • Lead process improvements in financial reporting systems and procedures.
  • Ensure compliance with internal policies.

 

 

SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

 

  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, information systems, business, or a related field, providing the technical foundation for Workday reporting responsibilities. MBA or CPA is valued.
  • 3-5 years of experience in financial reporting, accounting, and/or auditing roles.
  • Demonstrated, hands-on experience building reports in Workday Report Writer including calculated fields and advanced, matrix, and composite reports.
  • Workday Report Writer Certification or be willing and able to successfully complete a Workday Report Writing proficiency assessment as part of the interview process.
  • Deep understanding of Workday Finance.
  • Workday Adaptive Planning experience including Adaptive Dashboards, HTML Reports, and OfficeConnect reporting packages highly preferred.
  • Experience with Workday Dashboards, Scorecards, and Workday Hubs preferred.
  • Experience gathering, documenting, and translating business requirements into reporting solutions, with working knowledge of data integration/ETL concepts and reporting governance practices.
  • Knowledge of GAAP.
  • Non-profit experience highly preferred.
  • Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and data analytics skills.
  • Proficiency in Excel.
  • Excellent problem-solving, communication, and leadership abilities.

 

 

PHYSICAL DEMANDS FOR CERTAIN ROLES

 

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

 

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally required to stand, walk, and sit for long periods of time, and work at a computer for long periods of time.

 

 

SALARY AND BENEFITS

 

The starting salary for this position is $108,900 to $122,000 per year, benchmarked against industry standards. Salaries for positions required to be in specific geographic locations reflect the corresponding labor market. 
 
The actual offer extended will depend on the candidate's experience, qualifications, and the role's requirements. Positions working 20+ hours per week also receive our comprehensive benefits package (with medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, generous paid time off, and more). Click here for an overview of our company benefits.


Explore our career opportunities to join a team that values creativity, innovation, and diversity. 

 

 

ABOUT THE RECORDING ACADEMY AND ITS AFFILIATES

 

RECORDING ACADEMY

The Recording Academy represents the voices of performers, songwriters, producers, engineers, and all music professionals. Dedicated to ensuring the recording arts remain a thriving part of our shared cultural heritage, the Academy honors music's history while investing in its future through the Grammy Museum, advocates on behalf of music creators, supports music people in times of need through MusiCares, and celebrates artistic excellence through the Grammy Awards—music's only peer-recognized accolade and highest achievement. As the world's leading society of music professionals, we work year-round to foster a more inspiring world for creators.

 

LATIN RECORDING ACADEMY

The Latin Recording Academy is an international, membership-based organization comprised of Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking recording artists, musicians, songwriters, producers and other creative and technical recording professionals. The organization is dedicated to improving the quality of life and cultural condition for Latin music and its makers. In addition to producing the Latin Grammy Awards to honor excellence in the recorded arts and sciences, The Latin Recording Academy provides educational and outreach programs for the Latin music community either directly or through its Latin Grammy Cultural Foundation.

 

LATIN GRAMMY CULTURAL FOUNDATION

The Latin Grammy Cultural Foundation is a charitable organization established by the Latin Recording Academy in 2014. The organization is dedicated to creating opportunities for the next generation of Latin music creators through scholarships, educational programs, grants, and access to creators and industry executives.

 

MUSICARES

A friend and ally of the music community, MusiCares was established by the Recording Academy to safeguard the health and well-being of all music people. A four-star charity and safety net in times of need, MusiCares offers confidential preventative, recovery, and emergency programs to address financial, medical, and personal health issues. Through the generosity of our donors and volunteer professionals, our dedicated team works across the country to ensure the music community has the resources and support it needs.

 

GRAMMY MUSEUM

The Grammy Museum is a nonprofit organization dedicated to celebrating and exploring music from yesterday and today to inspire the music of tomorrow through music preservation, education, exhibitions, and public programming and aims to create a world in which shared love of music sparks curiosity, creativity, and community. Programs include Grammy in the Schools education programs that are offered year-round for students, teachers, and schools throughout the United States. 

 

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

The Recording Academy, its affiliates, and the music industry have a strong culture of inclusion and respect for everyone. The Recording Academy makes intentional, courageous, and principled decisions for stronger business outcomes and ensures that all creators and professionals live and work in a fair and safe environment. It is the Recording Academy's policy to provide equal employment opportunities for all applicants and employees. The Recording Academy does not discriminate on the basis of race (nor traits historically associated with race, including, but not limited to hair texture and protective hairstyles), color, religion (including religious dress and grooming), creed, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth or related medical conditions), national origin, ancestry, age, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, family care status, military or veteran status, marital status, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information or any other characteristic protected by law. The Recording Academy will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities unless doing so would result in an undue hardship to the Recording Academy. This policy governs all aspects of employment, including selection, job assignment, compensation, promotion, discipline, termination, access to benefits and training, recruitment, hiring, transfer, and social and recreational programs.

The Audience Intelligence intern will have many responsibilities including the mining of data sets for insights, automation, facilitating predictive analytics, and supporting research. The intern will also have the lead on a project allowing them to complete the internship with a deliverable that can be used in their future job search.

KQED envisions a public media organization with a culture that centers on human dignity, equity, and belonging. This will enable us to better serve and reflect the Bay Area through diverse and inclusive storytelling.

KQED provide citizens of Northern California with a community-supported alternative to commercial media.   We provide citizens with the knowledge they need to make informed decisions; convene community dialogue; bring the arts to everyone and engage audiences to share their stories. We help students and teachers thrive in 21st-century classrooms, and take people of all ages on journeys of exploration- exposing them to new people, places and ideas.

Essential Functions:
  • Help develop new insights and analyses that inform organizational decisions and help us continue to engage our audiences

  • Execute quantitative analyses that translate data into actionable insights
  • Build visualizations that expose the health and performance of our products
  • Presentation building for a variety of stakeholders
  • Other Duties as assigned

Knowledge/Experience Required:

  • Intellectual curiosity for data-driven products
  • Experience with data analysis and/or visualization
  • Excellent writing, research, and communication skills
  • Strong attention to detail
  • Problem-solving acumen
  • Capacity to balance multiple responsibilities
  • Ability to work independently
  • At least some knowledge of SQL

Knowledge/Experience Desired:

  • Bonus points for knowledge of Python or another programming language, dashboarding tools (e.g., Looker, Tableau, etc.), ETL tools, or databases.

Growth & Development Opportunities:  

Audience Intelligence interns have a huge impact on what we do. They are a full-fledged member of our team and their life experience, opinions, and ideas bring fresh approaches to the work we do and are incredibly valuable. job.description:
Title: Director of Membership Programs

Schedule Format - Location: Hybrid - San Francisco

Pay Information: Salary Range: $125,547 - $137,000

Position SummaryThe Director of Membership Programs leads the strategy and growth of KQED’s on-air, third-party, and emerging membership fundraising channels. This role manages a portfolio that includes on-air fundraising, matching gifts, vehicle and real estate donations, and other third-party programs, while identifying and testing new opportunities to grow membership revenue.This is a strategy and growth role with responsibility for evaluating the performance and potential of each fundraising channel, determining where KQED should invest, improve, scale, or shift resources, and building a disciplined pipeline of new tests and initiatives. The Director develops business cases, establishes goals and measures of success, manages key vendor relationships and contracts, and uses performance data to make recommendations about the future of the portfolio.

The Director supervises the Fundraising Manager, who leads the day-to-day planning and production of KQED’s radio membership drives and year-round on-air fundraising calendar, as well as a NABET-represented staff member who manages the day-to-day operations of KQED’s current third-party fundraising programs. The Director sets strategy, priorities, and revenue goals across both areas and is accountable for overall performance.

This role works closely with colleagues across Membership, Development, Product, Data and Analytics, Programming, Content and Donor Services to ensure fundraising channels work together to grow revenue, acquire new members and strengthen long-term donor relationships.

The ideal candidate is analytical and entrepreneurial, with experience growing or improving fundraising programs. They are comfortable testing new ideas, making decisions with imperfect information, managing external partners, and translating data into clear recommendations. They are also a collaborative leader with a strong commitment to public media and KQED’s mission.

KQED envisions a public media organization with a culture that centers on human dignity, equity, and belonging. This will enable us to better serve and reflect the Bay Area through diverse and inclusive storytelling. 

We value the contributions of marginalized people in society — including Black, Indigenous, and all people of color,  people with disabilities, and LGBTQIA+ people — and we believe that these communities must be centered in the work we do, and we strongly encourage members of these communities to apply.

KQED Code of Ethics  https://www.kqed.org/about/code-ethics

The mission that drives us:

KQED provide citizens of Northern California with a community-supported alternative to commercial media.   We provide citizens with the knowledge they need to make informed decisions; convene community dialogue; bring the arts to everyone and engage audiences to share their stories. We help students and teachers thrive in 21st-century classrooms, and take people of all ages on journeys of exploration- exposing them to new people, places and ideas.

This role will work hybrid between working in KQED's newly renovated headquarters and working remotely.

Essential Functions:

Fundraising Channel Strategy & Growth

  • Own the strategy, growth, and performance of KQED’s portfolio of third-party and emerging membership fundraising channels.
  • Supervise and support the NABET-represented staff member responsible for the day-to-day management and administration of KQED’s existing third-party fundraising programs.
  • Manage key vendor and partner relationships, including contracts, performance expectations, and service levels.
  • Evaluate existing programs, including vehicle and real estate donations, to identify opportunities to grow, improve, restructure, or discontinue programs.
  • Develop a pipeline of new fundraising channel opportunities and establish a disciplined process for testing, evaluating, and scaling them.
  • Identify trends, technologies, partnerships, and fundraising models that could create new revenue opportunities for KQED.
  • Work closely with Donor Services, Finance, Legal, Marketing, and other teams to ensure programs operate efficiently and provide a strong donor experience.

On-Air Fundraising Leadership

  • With the department lead, set the annual strategy, revenue goals, and overall approach for KQED’s radio fundraising and year-round broadcast membership promotion.
  • Supervise and support the Fundraising Manager, who leads the planning, production, and execution of radio membership drives and the on-air fundraising calendar.
  • Partner with Programming, News, Content and Membership leadership on drive strategy, campaign timing, messaging and major promotional opportunities.
  • Review performance across drives and on-air campaigns and identify opportunities to improve revenue, donor acquisition, recurring giving and audience experience.
  • Ensure on-air fundraising strategies are coordinated with digital, direct marketing and other membership efforts.

Cross-Departmental Collaboration

  • Partner with acquisition and retention teams to ensure new fundraising channels complement existing donor strategies rather than operate in isolation.
  • Coordinate with Development on opportunities that connect membership fundraising with major donor and philanthropic initiatives.
  • Work with Product and digital teams to ensure donor journeys from broadcast, third-party, and emerging channels connect effectively to KQED’s digital donation experience.
  • Bring audience, donor, and channel insights into broader Membership planning and strategy.
  • Build alignment across teams around priorities, investment decisions, and measures of success.

Team Leadership & Culture

  • Manage, coach and develop the Fundraising Manager and NABET-represented third-party fundraising staff member, providing clear priorities, feedback and support while respecting the roles, responsibilities and requirements of represented staff.
  • Foster a collaborative, creative and mission-driven environment within the Membership team.
  • Encourage experimentation while creating clear expectations for how tests are structured, evaluated, and learned from.
  • Champion continuous improvement and a culture where teams use data and audience insight to make stronger decisions.

Other Job Functions

  • Serve as a leader for new strategic initiatives within the Membership department as assigned by the VP of Membership.
  • Represent Membership in cross-functional planning and organizational initiatives when appropriate.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Candidate Qualifications

Professional Background

  • 7+ years of experience in fundraising, membership, revenue growth, business development, direct-to-consumer programs, or a related field.
  • Demonstrated success launching, growing, or improving revenue-generating programs.
  • Experience managing a portfolio of programs or channels and making decisions about where to invest, scale, or shift resources.
  • Experience developing business cases, setting revenue goals, managing budgets, and forecasting performance.
  • Experience managing external vendors, partners, or contracts.
  • Experience managing and developing staff.
  • Ability to operate effectively in an environment where not every opportunity has a clear roadmap or established playbook.

Strategic & Analytical Skills

  • Strong analytical skills and experience using data to evaluate opportunities and make decisions.
  • Ability to move from broad strategy to clear priorities, tests, and action plans.
  • Experience establishing success metrics and evaluating performance against them.
  • Comfort balancing short-term revenue goals with longer-term growth opportunities.
  • Strong judgment and the ability to make recommendations with incomplete information.
  • Ability to clearly communicate the rationale behind investment and prioritization decisions.

Collaboration & Partnership

  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively as a peer partner across teams and functions.
  • Strong relationship-building skills and experience bringing together stakeholders with different priorities.
  • Ability to influence without relying solely on direct authority.
  • Skilled at managing external partners and holding vendors accountable for results.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate strategy, performance, and recommendations clearly to a range of audiences.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience in public media, nonprofit membership, subscription, direct response, or another audience-supported business.
  • Familiarity with on-air fundraising, broadcast fundraising, or public media membership programs.
  • Experience with third-party fundraising programs such as vehicle donations, planned giving lead-generation programs, or other external fundraising partnerships.
  • Familiarity with CRM and donor data systems; ROI Solutions experience is a plus.
  • Experience testing and launching new revenue or acquisition channels.

Mission Alignment

  • Deep commitment to the values and mission of public media, including service to diverse communities and audiences.
  • Commitment to fostering a workplace culture rooted in collaboration, equity, inclusion, and respect

Title: Social Video Producer

The Social Video Producer is a multimedia journalist responsible for identifying, developing, and producing original vertical video content for KQED’s social and digital platforms. Working within the Newsroom and under the direction of the Manager, Video Content Development, this role will develop stories and repeatable video formats specifically designed for platforms including TikTok, Instagram, YouTube Shorts, and other emerging social platforms supporting KQED’s Food, Guides, and Technology editorial verticals.

The ideal candidate is an experienced journalist and visual storyteller with a strong understanding of social video audiences and the ability to recognize what makes a story compelling in a vertical, mobile-first environment. They will be capable of taking an idea from initial concept through research, reporting, scripting, field production, and delivery to post-production, while working closely with video editors to bring the final story to life.

This role requires strong editorial judgment, journalistic integrity, and the ability to work quickly and creatively in a newsroom environment. The Social Video Producer should be comfortable developing original story ideas, collaborating with reporters and editors, conducting interviews, producing one-person and small-crew shoots, directing talent, and creating production approaches that can be repeated and scaled across KQED’s social video portfolio.

The Social Video Producer will also work closely with Audience Development to understand audience behavior, platform trends, and performance data, applying those insights to story development, format development, and production decisions.
This is a full-time, limited term position reporting to the Manager, Video Content Development.

KQED envisions a public media organization with a culture that centers on human dignity, equity, and belonging. This will enable us to better serve and reflect the Bay Area through diverse and inclusive storytelling.

  • Demonstrated ability to develop stories and video treatments specifically for mobile-first and social audiences.
  • Experience developing repeatable video formats or series designed for social platforms.
  • Strong understanding of journalistic principles, ethics, accuracy, fairness, attribution, and editorial standards.

  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple assignments and deadlines in a fast-paced newsroom environment.

  • Develop and maintain repeatable editing approaches, templates, workflows, and visual formats that improve the efficiency and consistency of KQED News vertical video production.
  • Manage project media and maintain organized edit projects in accordance with KQED post-production, media management, and archival workflows.
  • Meet tight publishing schedules and communicate proactively about potential production or post-production issues that could affect delivery.
  • Work with animators, illustrators, photographers, reporters, and other creative collaborators to incorporate additional visual elements as needed.
  • Work with the Senior Video Editor to develop, adopt and implement post-production standards, workflows, technical requirements, and best practices across News vertical video.
  • Help establish and maintain a distinctive visual language for KQED News vertical video while ensuring consistency with KQED’s broader brand and editorial standards.
  • Work quickly and efficiently on breaking and developing news while maintaining KQED’s standards for accuracy, fairness, attribution, context, and editorial integrity.
  • Work with reporters and editors to clarify or resolve editorial questions that arise during the editing process.Work closely with the Social Video Producer, reporters, editors, and newsroom stakeholders to translate reporting and story concepts into compelling visual narratives.
  • Collaborate with the News Social Video Producer from story development through final delivery, providing creative and editorial input on story structure, visual approach, pacing, graphics, sound, and platform execution.
  • Collaborate with Audience Development to understand audience behavior, performance data, and platform trends and apply those insights to future edits and storytelling approaches.
  • Participate in editorial and production meetings and contribute ideas for improving KQED’s vertical video strategy and storytelling.

Other Job Functions:
  • Perform other video and organizational duties as assigned.

Knowledge/Experience Required:
  • Minimum of three years of professional video editing experience, with demonstrated experience creating content for digital and social platforms.
  • Strong proficiency in Adobe Premiere Pro and familiarity with Adobe After Effects, Photoshop, Illustrator, and Media Encoder.
  • Demonstrated experience editing short-form, vertical video specifically for platforms such as TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts.
  • Strong understanding of mobile-first and social-first storytelling, including hooks, pacing, visual sequencing, captions, graphics, and audience retention.
  • Excellent editorial judgment and a strong understanding of journalistic principles, ethics, accuracy, attribution, and standards.
  • Demonstrated ability to work with reporters, producers, editors, and other editorial stakeholders to shape stories during the editing process.
  • Strong storytelling instincts and the ability to identify the most compelling narrative within interviews, field footage, archival material, and other source materials.
  • Ability to edit quickly and accurately under tight deadlines, including the ability to respond to breaking or developing news.
  • Strong sound editing and mixing skills, including dialogue cleanup, music, sound effects, and overall audio balancing.
  • Experience with color correction and basic motion graphics.
  • Strong understanding of video codecs, resolutions, frame rates, aspect ratios, audio formats, and technical requirements for digital and social video.
  • Ability to create accessible video content, including accurate captions and clear audio.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, including the ability to manage multiple projects and maintain organized media and edit projects.
  • Ability to work independently while also collaborating closely with a multidisciplinary newsroom and video team.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to respond constructively to editorial feedback and iterate quickly.
  • Commitment to KQED’s mission and journalistic standards.

Knowledge/Experience Desired:
  • Experience working in a newsroom or other journalistic environment.
  • Experience editing breaking news, current affairs, documentary, explanatory, or other journalism-focused video.
  • Experience developing repeatable social video formats, templates, or post-production workflows.
  • Advanced After Effects and motion graphics skills.
  • Experience incorporating animation, data visualization, maps, screenshots, social posts, and other visual journalism techniques into video.
  • Experience working with user-generated content and third-party video materials.
  • Familiarity with rights, licensing, releases, and editorial considerations related to third-party media.
  • Experience using audience analytics or performance data to inform editing and storytelling decisions.
  • Familiarity with KQED, public media, or mission-driven journalism.
  • Familiarity with digital asset management and post-production systems.
  • Bachelor’s degree in journalism, film, media production, communications, or a related field preferred.

NOTE: This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive. Employees may be required to perform other related duties as necessary to meet the ongoing needs of this organization.

this is an in-person position that requires periodic travel to Hearst Television locations and participation in an on-call rotation supporting critical technology operations.

job.title: Sales and Marketing Specialist
job.description:
This Job Description May Cause Extreme Excitement and Career Growth 

At AMP Sales & Marketing Solutions, we believe a great workplace isn't just something we say — it's something you can feel when you join the team. Here, it's all about great collabs, ambition, and results but most importantly, we grow here, and we enjoy here.  We're searching for that special someone — a driven, talented individual to join our innovative media sales team. In this role, you'll engage with new and existing clients and show them how our innovative media solutions can amplify their brands and deliver measurable success. If you're energized by building relationships, closing deals, and making an impact, we'd love to hear from you. 


Sound like the right fit? Check out the checklist below and if it sounds like you, hit "Apply Now" and let's chat. 


Your Day-to-Day (aka the Playbook) 

Help Brands Thrive: 

Join our media sales team and play a pivotal role in helping brands and companies grow. By identifying new opportunities, building strong client relationships, and delivering impactful solutions, you'll showcase how our multi-media content platforms and digital assets can drive meaningful results for our partners. 


Your focus will be on helping clients achieve their goals, ensuring that every campaign is a success. When our clients win, we win—and we believe in celebrating those victories together! 

  

Make Connections: Embrace your powers of persuasion and make every handshake and meeting count! Every interaction is a chance to build a genuine connection and show clients how we can help them succeed. You're not just selling; you're building partnerships. You're helping businesses find the right audience in the right place at the right time. When we say One Partner, Endless Possibilities, we mean it! 

 

Be A Trusted Guide: In this role, you'll connect with clients on a human level, understand their unique needs, and craft tailored sales and marketing solutions that deliver results. As their trusted advisor, you'll help them navigate the ever-evolving marketing landscape, ensuring every step of the journey is planned with care and precision.  

 

Shake Things Up: Bring your creativity and fresh ideas to the table! We're looking for someone who challenges the status quo, embraces innovation, and finds new ways to connect with our audience. Your contributions will help elevate our brand and drive meaningful results for your clients.  

 

Join us and Conquer the Media Landscape: You'll be part of a dedicated team of A1 media sales professionals, committed to achieving market leadership. Together, we amplify our impact, deliver exceptional outcomes, and help our clients succeed in ways that truly matter. 

 

Identify Emerging Opportunities: It's about being able to see what others can't, anticipating market shifts, analyzing data and predicting the next big thing. Your insights will position our clients and AMP for long-term success.  

  

What We're Looking For 

Proven Sales Ability (or an Unstoppable Desire to Learn) 

Whether you're a seasoned sales professional or just getting started, we value your drive, energy, and passion for achieving results. 

 

Strong Communication Skills: You're a natural at building relationships and communicating effectively. Proficiency with digital tools and applications is a must. 

 

A Passion for helping Others: You're committed to understanding clients' needs, providing top-notch customer service and making a difference. You're not just selling a product; you're providing a solution.  


A Competitive Spirit: Do you get a little boost when you achieve a goal (especially if it was a tough one)? We love that for you (and us)!  We want someone who's driven to excel but also knows how to celebrate the victories (big and small) with their team. That drive makes you a valuable part of our organization.  


A Willingness to Grow: Do you thrive in environments where you're always learning something new? Excellent, you'll fit right in! The media world is constantly evolving, and the ability to learn, adapt, and embrace challenges in a fast-paced, digital-first environment is key.  

 

The Practical Stuff 

A valid driver's license, up-to-date insurance, and reliable transportation are necessary for connecting with clients in your community. 

 

Why Join AMP Sales & Marketing Solutions? / The Reasons You Should Hit "Apply Now" 

 

Serious Work, Seriously Cool People: Be part of a dynamic team that values creativity, collaboration, and fun! We are all for work that is rewarding.  

 

The Compensation Package: We offer a base salary, commission structure, and benefits package designed to support your success and well-being. Happy employees don't stage rebellions! ;) 

 

We Make a Real Difference (Not Just Talk About It): At AMP, we help local businesses thrive through advertising strategies that create tangible impacts. Our media sales specialist isn't just selling ads; they're the boots on the ground, making a real difference where it counts. (And yes, it feels pretty good.) 

 

Top-Notch Training and Support: We're not the kind of company that hires you and then disappears into the corporate abyss. We carefully select candidates for a cohort-based training program, where you'll join a group of sales professionals from all over the country. From onboarding to ongoing mentorship, we invest in your success with training programs that set you up for long-term growth. 

 

Career Growth Opportunities: We believe in investing in you. That's why you'll have access to training, mentorship, and career advancement opportunities to help you thrive. We are a leader in our industry, flexing our local charm and national muscle, providing you with options to amplify your career in your local market or join one of our AMP Sales & Marketing Solutions teams in another city.  

 

Comprehensive Media Education (We Are Your Power Source!): New to the industry? We've got you covered with training programs that turn curiosity into expertise.   

 

AMP is us. It's you. It isn't just a name; it's a mission. A promise to amplify our reach, amplify our innovation, and most importantly, amplify you. If you're ready to grow your career and help businesses achieve their goals, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: Senior Union Payroll Associate
job.description:
The Senior Union Payroll Associate performs a variety of functions necessary for the accurate and timely processing of multi-state, multi-company, weekly and bi-weekly payrolls for union and non-union freelance employees. The Senior Union Payroll Associate coordinates, validates, and implements work procedures that require comprehensive operational knowledge of union collective bargaining agreements and federal and state regulations related to wage garnishment, taxation and wage‐hour law.


While there are no direct people responsibilities, the Senior Union Payroll Associate will coordinate independently with other associates, leaders, and teams outside of Payroll Shared Services to accomplish tasks, meet deadlines, champion process improvement initiatives, and enhance the employee experience.


A SNAPSHOT OF YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Perform all duties necessary to ensure timely and accurate processing of multi-state, multi-company weekly and bi-weekly payrolls for union and non-union freelance employees in accordance with collective bargaining agreements and other contracts and in compliance with applicable FOX policies and federal, state, and local regulations
  • Process on demand payments, retroactive payments, one-time payments, tax adjustments, stop payments, void checks, direct deposit reversals, and overpayment collections in accordance with FOX policies, collective bargaining agreements, and in compliance with federal, state, and local regulations
  • Interpret and set up withholding orders for levies, garnishments, child support, and other involuntary wage assignment orders in the payroll system within the regulated period
  • Understand union pay and paid time off rules and the timekeeping system and address employee questions as needed
  • Provide testing support during the implementation of the new timekeeping system and assist with team training
  • Perform detailed pre-payroll processing audits of earnings, deductions, benefits, garnishments, and tax setups to prevent pay-impacting errors when payroll is processed
  • Audit and reconcile union-related inputs, including union dues, initiation fees, and retirement contributions, to ensure accuracy and strict adherence to collective bargaining agreements
  • Understand proper taxation of all employee payments, including employer paid union benefits, and address employee questions as needed
  • Review, test, and update Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) regularly to ensure operational accuracy, compliance, and continuous process efficiency
  • Provide subject matter expertise on union timekeeping rules and processes, to include paid time off plans. This requires the ability to interpret rules outlined in collective bargaining agreements (CBAs) and other union related documents
  • Assist employees and management with questions, concerns, or requests regarding union payroll. This includes properly applying technical knowledge and skills, communicating, and listening effectively
  • Serve as a go-to expert for union payroll questions, managing the timely resolution of customer issues, including handling customer escalations, performing and documenting Root Cause Analysis, and implementing remedial procedures to close gaps identified
  • Ensure compliance with all company policies, internal controls, and SOX controls

WHAT YOU WILL NEED

  • 4+ years hands-on union payroll processing experience, preferably with IBEW, IATSE, AFTRA, and/or NABET collective bargaining agreements
  • Experience with interpreting and setting up withholding orders for levies, garnishments, child support, and other involuntary wage assignment orders
  • Experience and knowledge of automated time and attendance systems
  • Experience with initiating and leading standardization and process improvement initiatives
  • Strong working knowledge of FLSA, federal, state, and local wage and hour and tax regulations. 
  • Ability to interpret collective bargaining agreements for pay and paid time off rules.
  • Strong interpersonal skills – you are approachable, responsive, and team focused
  • Intermediate Excel using VLOOKUP and pivots.
  • Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written
  • Excellent judgment, analytical and problem-solving skills
  • High degree of professionalism and solid ability in delivering high quality customer service and establishing/maintaining effective and collaborative working relationships

NICE TO HAVE BUT NOT A DEALBREAKER

  • Fundamental Payroll Certification (FPC) or Certified Payroll Professional (CPP) designation
  • Experience with Workday Payroll

job.title: Regional Streaming Director
job.description:
FOX Television Stations is growing its streaming operation, and the Florida region is a critical part of that growth. This role sits at the center of that effort — serving as the streaming authority for FOX Tampa (WTVT) and FOX Orlando (WOFL), responsible for building and evolving a high-performing local streaming operation across both markets.

Reporting to the News Director(s) at WTVT & WOFL, this position works in close partnership with FTS Streaming and weather leadership to align regional execution with broader FTS strategy and the Executive Producers of both FL stations. As the streaming team grows and the business evolves, so will this role — expanding in scope, team size, and responsibility. The right candidate is someone who is ready to grow with it.

This is a role for a streaming-first leader who understands where the industry is heading, knows how to bring a newsroom along on that journey, and has the editorial instincts, technical fluency, and analytical rigor to drive measurable growth across the full streaming universe — CTV, FAST channels, and social video.

A Snapshot of Your Responsibilities - Editorial & Content Leadership

  • Lead with a streaming-first mindset across both newsrooms, driving editorial vision, cultural adoption, and a commitment to continuous content improvement.
  • Make fast, sound editorial decisions in breaking news environments, balancing urgency with accuracy.
  • Manage and evolve streaming programming schedules across Tampa and Orlando, working toward expanded hours and a long-term 24/7 weather and streaming operation at both stations.
  • Elevate content quality at every level — from live breaking news to long-form storytelling — with an eye toward what works for a streaming-native audience.
  • Operate fluidly across digital and streaming, shaping content intentionally for each format and platform.

Team Development & Newsroom Adoption

  • Motivate, coach, and develop a team of streaming journalists and producers in Tampa, and support alignment with the Orlando & Tampa Executive Producers of Streaming.
  • Serve as the leading voice in both newsrooms for streaming adoption — building buy-in, growing participation, and helping teams evolve their workflows and mindset to support expanded streaming output.
  • Partner with the station and FTS Executive Director of Streaming to identify opportunities to grow the team and the operation over time.

Analytics & Performance Reporting

  • Own streaming performance data and reporting for the FL region across all platforms — including FOX Local CTV, FAST channels, YouTube, social video, and weather.

JOB TITLE: Executive Producer of Investigations

Vibe: Driven, strategic, organized, and obsessed with high-impact journalism across every platform.

The Mission FOX6 Milwaukee is looking for a detail-oriented, creative, high-caliber journalist to lead our investigative team and our Contact 6 consumer advocacy unit. We need an Executive Producer who can manage major investigative projects, oversee our investigative podcast, and reimagine how deep-dive stories reach modern audiences on streaming, digital, and broadcast.

This isn't a role spent sitting in an office waiting for project updates. We need a hands-on leader who is in the middle of our daily news operation—working alongside reporters and producers every day to bring investigative thinking, public records digging, and relentless follow-up into our everyday coverage. You'll lead with curiosity, courage, accountability, and empathy while coaching journalists to move beyond traditional package formats, guiding the team through complex ethical calls, and lifting the investigative standards across the entire newsroom.

Clear communication is essential in this position. Beyond being organized, you must proactively connect employees across all departments so everyone clearly understands available elements, expectations, and deadlines needed to deliver a seamless, high-quality product. 

What You’ll Do

  • Lead and inspire seasoned investigative journalists to conceive, execute, and deliver multi-platform investigative projects and consumer advocacy coverage.
  • Work directly with daily news reporters and producers to bring an investigative lens, public records strategies, and deeper context into daily enterprise reporting.
  • Collaborate with news managers to build a high-trust newsroom culture through open communication and clear feedback.
  • Keep momentum going on major stories across all platforms.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor on complex journalistic ethics, legal vetting, public records requests, and investigative standards.
  • Work across departments to drive new strategies for distributing investigative work beyond packageable content.

What You Bring

  • Proven track record producing or managing investigative journalism, enterprise reporting, or long-form investigative units.
  • Sharp project management skills with the ability to juggle multiple initiatives, keep cross-department teams aligned, and keep long-term investigations on schedule while staying involved in daily newsroom needs.
  • Ability to coach journalists past standard TV package formats into dynamic visual storytelling built for modern audiences.

  • Debug and resolve complex engine‑level issues involving multithreading, memory, platform integration, and Unreal system interactions.
  • Guide Unreal Engine upgrades, custom engine changes, and long‑term technology decisions.
  • Stay current with Unreal Engine advancements, engine architecture trends, and low‑level performance techniques.

À titre de Programmeur ou programmeuse moteur Lead, vous êtes responsable de définir, développer et orienter les systèmes centraux fondés sur Unreal Engine qui soutiennent la jouabilité, le rendu, la physique, les outils et les pipelines d’un titre AAA. Vous fournissez un leadership technique pour l’architecture moteur et les systèmes de bas niveau tout en collaborant étroitement avec les équipes Gameplay, Rendering, Tools, Pipeline et Production afin de garantir qu’Unreal Engine est étendu, optimisé et maintenu pour répondre aux besoins du projet. RESPONSABILITÉS

  • Diriger la conception et l’implantation des systèmes centraux, des frameworks et de l’architecture de niveau moteur d’Unreal Engine.
  • Définir et maintenir les normes du moteur en matière de performance, de stabilité, d’évolutivité et de maintenabilité dans Unreal Engine.
  • Fournir un leadership technique et contribuer directement au développement de fonctionnalités moteur complexes et de systèmes Unreal transversaux.
  • Collaborer avec les autres responsables techniques afin de garantir que les systèmes Unreal Engine soutiennent la jouabilité, les outils, le pipeline et les flux de travail de contenu.

  • Établir des normes de codage, des pratiques de documentation et des processus de débogage pour le développement sous Unreal Engine.
  • Soutenir la production en identifiant les risques techniques, en évaluant l’ampleur des travaux et en planifiant l’évolution d’Unreal Engine au fil des jalons.
  • Déboguer et résoudre des problèmes complexes de niveau moteur liés au multithreading, à la mémoire, à l’intégration des plateformes et aux interactions entre les systèmes Unreal.
  • Orienter les mises à niveau d’Unreal Engine, les modifications personnalisées du moteur et les décisions technologiques à long terme.
  • Se tenir à jour quant aux avancées d’Unreal Engine, aux tendances en architecture moteur et aux techniques de performance de bas niveau.

QUALIFICATIONS

Basic Requirements:

  • Expert proficiency in C++, with extensive experience developing low‑level engine or systems code in Unreal Engine.
  • At least 8+ years of professional experience in game programming, with shipped AAA titles using Unreal Engine.
  • Deep, hands‑on experience working with Unreal Engine at the engine‑systems level.

  • Demonstrated experience leading, mentoring, or technically guiding programmers on a production team.
  • Excellent problem‑solving skills and the ability to design robust systems under production constraints.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively across disciplines.
  • Experience with version control systems such as Perforce or Git.

Desired Characteristics:

  • Experience supporting multiple platforms within Unreal Engine (PC, console, mobile).
  • Experience modifying or extending Unreal Engine source.
  • Strong understanding of gameplay and content pipeline requirements from an Unreal Engine perspective.
  • A passion for building scalable, high‑performance engine technology.

We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to own the CDP product domain within the Customer Experience Platform (CXP) Martech team. This is a high-ownership IC (Individual Contributor) role responsible for the Customer Data Platform (CDP) as a shared global platform: the identity and audience data layer that serves Peacock, SkyShowtime, and NOW.

You'll be the primary intake point for CDP-related requirements from MarTech local teams across all three propositions, own and prioritize the backlog, and drive delivery in close partnership with Engineering (platform instrumentation) and Decision Science (data pipelines and attributes). A core operating principle for this role: solutions must be designed globally first, scalable across all applications, not built for a single product.

In this role you will:
Stakeholder Intake & Prioritization

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for Peacock, SkyShowtime, and NOW MarTech and Marketing teams, owning all incoming CDP requests and proactively identifying data quality and data collection opportunities to scale our product customer lifecycle and marketing operation efforts.
  • Translate those needs into well-structured platform requirements, always with a global lens; solutions need to work across all three products, not just the one making the request.
  • Manage and prioritize the backlog, balancing urgency against platform impact and engineering capacity.
  • Keep documentation and roadmap status visible and current across all partners.

Platform Delivery & Cross-Functional Execution

  • Partner closely with Decision Science and Engineering teams to define business requirements for platform instrumentation (e.g., event schemas, platform events, and data capture), ensuring alignment with global standards and prioritizing delivery based on business needs.
  • Partner with Decision Science on pipeline requirements, new attribute builds, and feed delivery to make sure data flows correctly into downstream systems.
  • Own the coordination of delivery milestones, testing, and QA sign-off, acting as the connective tissue between marketing stakeholders and the technical teams who build and operate the platform.

What You Have

  • Ability to intake, synthesize, and prioritize requirements from multiple marketing stakeholders across competing products and timelines
  • A platform-first mindset — instinct to design solutions that are global and scalable across multiple products rather than solving for one at a time
  • Empathy for marketing and growth teams as your primary customers, with curiosity to uncover the underlying need behind every request
  • Strong business judgment to balance short-term delivery needs against longer-term platform health and scalability
  • Comfort operating in a matrixed environment, building alignment across engineering, data, and marketing stakeholders at various levels of seniority
  • Technical curiosity and fluency to engage meaningfully with engineering and data engineering teams without owning the platform directly
  • Flexibility to adapt quickly to shifting priorities across a global, multi-product organization
  • Self-motivation to manage multiple workstreams simultaneously with tight schedules
  • Enthusiasm to be positive, collaborative, and energetic in a fast-moving streaming environment
  • 5–8+ years of product management experience, with at least 3 years working within a CDP, data platform, or martech infrastructure environment in a requirements, product, or delivery coordination capacity
  • Working knowledge of one or more enterprise CDPs (mParticle, Segment, Adobe CJA, Tealium, or equivalent) sufficient to translate business needs into platform requirements and engage effectively with technical teams
  • Strong understanding of platform event schemas, identity resolution, audience segmentation, and data feed architecture
  • Proven ability to partner with engineering on instrumentation requirements and with data engineering teams on pipeline and attribute delivery
  • Familiarity with downstream activation tools (Braze, Branch, Adtech) and data warehouse environments (Snowflake) is a strong plus
  • Experience with Agile/SCRUM software development environments
  • Streaming, subscription, or B2C consumer product background preferred
  • BS/BA required; technical or data-adjacent background a plus
  • Must have the legal right to work in the United States

Hybrid: This position currently has a hybrid schedule, which requires contributing from the office a minimum of four days per week. The Company reserves the right to change in-office requirements at any time.

  • Works in tandem with Account Executives, Marketing Director, Research Director, and Creative Services to support client needs.
  • Attend sales meetings and sales trainings to gain sales, product and process information and keep abreast of company products and services to articulate to client, when appropriate.
  • Partner with designated Account Executives in identifying new/incremental revenue based on campaign results.
  • Assist designated Account Executives with maintenance of contracts, generating avails, traffic, make-goods, collection and overall customer service.

job.description:
OVERVIEW

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide. 

Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Application Instructions

  • Application Deadline: Monday, October 26th, at 5:00 pm ET.
  • Submission Instructions: Please include a cover letter with your application. In your letter, detail a specific instance where you made a judgment call on behalf of your executive, including the circumstances and the ultimate outcome.

Intro to Position

The Executive Assistant, Marketing and Communications serves as the central operational backbone for senior leadership across NPR's Marketing and Communications divisions. In this role, you will provide high-level administrative partnership to departmental leaders, managing complex calendar logistics, coordinating cross-functional communications, and facilitating key stakeholder engagements across the NPR network.

Acting as a primary administrative liaison for the department, you will ensure seamless day-to-day operations while handling sensitive and confidential information with discretion, sound judgment, and precision.

Responsibilities

  • Manage complex, dynamic daily schedules and executive calendars, proactively resolving scheduling conflicts and aligning time allocations with division priorities.
  • Coordinate end-to-end travel arrangements and logistics for departmental leadership; assemble detailed itineraries and ensure timely reconciliation of expense reports and vendor invoices.
  • Prepare, organize, and proofread briefing materials, agendas, presentations, and background documentation for executive leadership meetings, NPR Board of Directors sessions, and Member station engagements.
  • Track and monitor division email correspondence and workflow queues; triage urgent inquiries, synthesize incoming requests, and route action items to appropriate team leads.
  • Orchestrate logistical planning for internal and external meetings, conferences, division retreats, and Network fly-ins, managing room reservations, audio/visual setup, and catering.
  • Record minutes, track deliverables, and maintain organized digital filing systems across Google Workspace and departmental directories.
  • Serve as the division's administrative point of contact, coordinating office supply inventory, facilities requests, and miscellaneous administrative questions.
  • Support departmental people operations, including scheduling onboarding sessions for new team members and assisting leadership with team retreats, culture initiatives and communications.

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 3+ years of progressive administrative experience supporting senior-level leadership.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage complex scheduling, travel itineraries, and expense reporting with minimal supervision.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with proven proofreading accuracy and attention to detail.
  • Demonstrated track record of exercising strict confidentiality, discretion, and tact when handling sensitive leadership information.
  • Proven ability to organize, prioritize, and track multiple simultaneous administrative deliverables under firm deadlines.
  • Demonstrated commitment to supporting workplace diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives. 

Preferred Qualifications

  • Professional experience supporting C-Suite executives.
  • Prior administrative experience within public media, journalism, broadcasting, or mission-driven nonprofit organizations.
  • Familiarity with Salesforce, Concur, or comparable enterprise CRM and expense management systems.

Education Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.

Work Location & Requirements

  • Hybrid Permitted: This is a hybrid permitted role. Some aspects of this role include duties that are better performed at an NPR facility. The employee will be required to be in the office at the Washington, D.C. location at least 2 days a week but is variable. The employee must also reside in an NPR-supported location based on the number of on-site days they choose.

Job Type

  • This is a full-time, non-exempt position.

Compensation

Hourly Rate: The U.S. based anticipated hourly rate for this opportunity is $36.06 - $38.46 per hour. The range displayed reflects the minimum and maximum hourly rate NPR expects to provide for new hires for the position across all US locations.

job.title: Information Security Analyst
job.description:
About ONErpm

ONErpm strives to establish its legacy as a global brand that makes an impact on the artistic community, the music business, and society as a whole. We are an inclusive company driven by innovation, music, and technology. We believe in mutual respect and recognize that different perspectives drive innovation, accelerate growth, and lead to more sustainable decisions and results.

If you join us, regardless of your location or position, we will support you in doing your best and reaching your full potential.

As a pioneering company, ONErpm has captured more than 20% of Brazil’s digital music market in less than 16 years. Today, we operate in Mexico, the United States, Colombia, Argentina, Peru, Chile, Jamaica, Spain, Nigeria, Vietnam, and many other countries.

As of May 2026, ONErpm has more than 46 offices across 32 countries, with a presence on nearly every continent.

Responsibilities

  • Security in Design: Integrate security requirements and perform threat modeling/project risk analyses in the early stages of system design and feature development (Security by Design)
  • Pipeline & Code Security (AppSec): Implement, operate, and maintain automated security tooling (SAST, DAST, SCA) in CI/CD pipelines; assist software engineers in remediating vulnerabilities using OWASP Top 10 guidelines and secure coding frameworks.
  • Cloud Security Posture: Evaluate, monitor, and improve the security posture of cloud infrastructure and technology environments based on recognized benchmarks such as CIS Controls and cloud security best practices.
  • Privacy & LGPD Compliance: Establish and manage operational workflows for data subject access requests (DSARs), maintain the continuous data mapping lifecycle, and evaluate privacy risks in new product features.
  • Penetration Testing Coordination: Coordinate regular external/internal pentesting procedures, including environment provisioning, scoping requirements between vendors and internal development teams, and managing remediation tracking.
  • Vendor & Third-Party Risk Management: Implement and oversee IT vendor security assessments to evaluate and mitigate the aggregate risks introduced by third-party tools, services, and partners.
  • Security Awareness & Culture: Plan and execute continuous security awareness programs, phishing simulations, and training sessions to build a proactive security mindset across the organization.
  • Incident Management & Root Cause Analysis: Monitor, respond to, and investigate information security and privacy incidents, analyzing root causes and implementing preventative controls.
  • Due Diligence & Audit Response: Conduct and respond to security and privacy due diligence assessments from customers, vendors, and regulatory auditors
  • Metrics & Indicators: Develop, track, and report Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) for Information Security and Privacy maturit
  • Compliance & Regulations: Ensure adherence to internal company policies, compliance regulations, industry standards, and workplace health and safety rules pertinent to the position.

Requirements

  • Higher Degree (Bachelor’s) in Information Security, Computer Science, Software Engineering, Systems Analysis, or related technology fields.
  • Desirable Certifications: CompTIA Security+, AWS/Azure Security Specialty, Certified AppSec Practitioner (CAP), EXIN Privacy & Data Protection (LGPD/GDPR), or ISO 27001 Lead Implementer/Auditor.
  • Proficiency in SAST, DAST, and SCA tools and their integration into CI/CD pipelines (e.g., GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure DevOps).
  • Solid understanding of the OWASP Top 10, CIS Controls, and cloud security architecture (AWS, GCP, or Azure).
  • In-depth knowledge of the General Data Protection Law (LGPD), data mapping, and DSAR management workflows.
  • Familiarity with third-party risk management (TPRM) frameworks and pentest scoping/vendor management.
  • Solid fundamentals in networking, protocols, identity and access management (IAM), and technology infrastructure.

Benefits

  • Health and Dental Insurance

  • Meal Allowance (Groceries)

  • Meal Allowance (Restaurants)

  • Life Insurance

  • TotalPass

  • Birthday Day Off

About Sony Music Entertainment

At Sony Music Entertainment, we fuel the creative journey. We’ve played a pioneering role in music history, from the first-ever music label to the invention of the flat disc record. We’ve nurtured some of music’s most iconic artists and produced some of the most influential recordings of all time.

Today, we work in more than 70 countries, supporting a diverse roster of international superstars, developing and independent artists, and visionary creators. From our position at the intersection of music, entertainment, and technology, we bring imagination and expertise to the newest products and platforms, embrace new business models, employ breakthrough tools, and provide powerful insights that help our artists push creative boundaries and reach new audiences. In everything we do, we’re committed to artistic integrity, transparency, and entrepreneurship.

Sony Music Entertainment is a member of the Sony family of global companies.

Ceremony of Roses is an agile creative practice built to solve the commercial and creative challenges of the world’s top artists. As Sony Music’s merchandise partner, we serve a roster of global talent—both within and beyond the Sony ecosystem. We’re defined by our commitment to product excellence, delivering products that are made to be kept, worn, and loved for years to come. Our best-in-class creative team delivers culture-leading, artist-specific collections that build artist brands beyond their music. Most importantly, we deliver customer excellence, embedding ourselves as an extension of each client’s team, bringing transparency, accountability, and tailored support to every partnership

As an Account Manager you will be responsible for the coordination, management and execution of merchandising projects across multiple clients. Though the role’s responsibilities are wide ranging and ever changing, this predominantly includes facilitation and oversight of the design, manufacture, sale and fulfilment of product, as well as the coordination of merchandise for artist tours, retail sales, events, pop-ups and ecommerce opportunities.

What you'll do:

  • Oversee a roster of managed accounts, tasked with meeting and exceeding expectations to foster account growth against specific Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).
  • Demonstrate effective communication with internal team members by proactively setting timelines, maintaining clear and concise cross-functional communication channels, and fostering a positive work environment through collaboration and support.
  • Develop, refine, and execute a comprehensive 12-18 month roadmap for each managed account, ensuring alignment with client objectives and company strategy.
  • Provide timely responses to internal team members & client inquiries within a 24-hour window via email, teams, or text, ensuring prompt and effective communication.
  • Dedicated to implementing and refining processes aimed at minimizing errors and mitigating potential issues that could lead to customer dissatisfaction or revenue loss for the company.

Who you are:

  • 3-5 years of experience in merchandising, sales or brand management, or equivalent experience in a lateral industry (artist management, booking agency or record label)
  • Excellent communicator with the ability to prepare and confidently present business plans, strategic insights, and difficult news to internal and external stakeholders
  • Experience in an apparel production environment, including an ability to effectively communicate with our production team and manage production process with partners
  • First-hand tour or merchandise sale experience, as well as experience in advancing merchandise and partnering with venues and venue staff
  • Familiarity with D2C strategies, including familiarity with the Shopify platform
  • Proven experience in a role that required strict confidentiality, outstanding organizational skills, and ability to maintain composure and effectiveness in stressful situations
  • Proven track record of successfully managing client relationships and delivering results against aggressive growth targets
  • Strategic thinker who can see the big picture as well as the small details required to win. Motivated to develop systems and processes that can improve performance and scale results
  • Dynamic problem solver with an expert-level understanding of relevant business practices and track-record of efficiently resolving client issues
 

What we give you:

It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. The New York Times advertising department's mission is to create work that helps brands make their mark in the world, and our canvas is the full breadth of The New York Times and its associated media platforms, including digital, mobile, audio, print, events and more.

The Director, Strategy will bring experience working cross-category and possess a passion for uncovering how different categories intersect with media and culture to spark inspiring creative ways-in and ideas. Strategy is a team sport, and you will be an expert collaborator with experience leading versatile teams, including creative, program management, sales, and planning, toward a common goal. Success within the advertising strategy team requires the ability to uncover human and cultural truths across multiple categories like finance, media, entertainment, healthcare, and consumer goods as well as a passion for big ideas expressed through media, a love of The New York Times, and a high standard for creating visual presentations.

Although you will not be responsible for writing media plans, you are comfortable and expert in guiding internal teams as well as clients in making smart and creative media choices.
  • Client Deliverable Development: You are experienced in owning and creating client-ready visual proposals that are polished and inspiring.
  • Category Fluency: You are constantly learning and reading about macro trends in business and culture.

  • Manage 3-6 strategists across 2-3 Categories
  • Co-lead resourcing across the Strategy Team

  • Use research and data to articulate and support sales stories
  • Author and deliver creative briefs on sometimes-tight turnarounds
  • Create and guide others in the creation of powerful proposals with effective storytelling that responds to client needs and telegraphs the value of NYT media offerings
  • Develop a broad understanding of all New York Times assets
  • Lead and project manage across relevant departments (including Sales, Ad Product, T Brand Studio, Ad Operations, Research, Marketing, Events) to create integrated programs for clients
  • Develop, articulate and share innovative programs, partnerships, innovations and opportunities
  • Research, write, and guide others in the creation of content strategy briefs
  • Attend key sales calls to pitch advertising and media ideas to mid/senior-level executives
  • Manage internal senior team members, communicating proposal and program status to management
  • Educate and keep the Strategy team/department abreast of trends and what opportunities or challenges they might present for our business
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Executive Strategy Director

Basic Qualifications:

  • 12+ years of cross-platform Advertising experience in brand and media strategy
  • Interest in managing high-volume categories
  • Experience working on RFPs
  • Experience working in collaborative sales and marketing processes, including working with sales teams or in a sales environment
  • An understanding of the current social, branded content, digital, audio and mobile media landscapes

job.title: Senior Counsel, Commercial
job.description:
The big picture: Axios is a digital media company focused on breaking news and invaluable insights across business, technology, politics, and media. We are hiring a Senior Counsel, Commercial to join our collaborative legal team and serve as a key legal partner to our revenue, product, and operations teams. 

Why it matters: This is a high-visibility, broad-scope role. You will independently counsel senior business leaders, own significant commercial matters end-to-end, and help shape practical solutions as Axios develops new products, partnerships, and growth opportunities.

Go deeper: We are looking for a pragmatic, self-directed attorney with strong commercial judgment who will: 

  • Commercial Transactions & Workflow
    • Draft, review, and negotiate a variety of commercial agreements, including advertising sales, sponsorships, events, customer subscriptions, content licensing, vendor, technology, and strategic agreements.
    • Own commercial legal intake and workflow: prioritize and delegate work, improve playbooks and templates, and help implement self-service tools and automation to handle volume efficiently.
  • Commercial, Product, Sales & Marketing Counseling
    • Provide practical, business-focused advice that balances legal risk with commercial objectives and helps teams reach workable solutions.
    • Advise on new products and features, sales and marketing initiatives, advertising and sponsorships, new revenue opportunities, and day-to-day business matters.
    • Identify legal implications across privacy, IP, regulatory, and operational issues.
    • Provide practical privacy and data-use counseling, including DPAs, privacy policy updates, and data-use questions, and exercise judgment about when specialized support is warranted.
    • Handle routine commercial disputes and other business issues and escalate significant or high-risk matters thoughtfully.
  • Legal Team Leadership
    • Scope and manage outside counsel efficiently and translate legal advice into clear, actionable recommendations for business leaders.
    • Stay current on legal developments relevant to digital media and technology 
    • Contribute to cross-functional and Legal team initiatives as needed. 

Worthy of your time: Ideal candidates will embody an entrepreneurial spirit and passion for Axios’ mission. This position requires the following:

  • 6+ years of relevant legal experience, including significant in-house commercial experience; law firm experience a plus.
  • Experience advising on product, sales, marketing, advertising, sponsorships, and digital media matters; digital media experience strongly preferred.
  • Strong contract drafting and negotiation skills, with a track record of independently leading sophisticated commercial transactions.
  • Broad issue-spotting skills and experience to identify and advise on legal and business risks beyond the contract.
  • Pragmatic risk assessment that balances legal protection with business agility and avoids over-lawyering.
  • Proven ability to operate independently, own matters end-to-end, and advise senior business leaders with sound judgment and confidence.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills and a collaborative, solution-oriented approach.
  • Ability to move quickly, prioritize competing demands, and communicate clearly and succinctly.
  • AI aptitude and comfort using AI-enabled tools and workflows to work more effectively.
