job.title: Senior Product Manager
job.description:
AccuWeather is seeking a strategic and results-oriented Senior Manager, Digital Subscriptions to grow our subscription offerings across mobile, web, and connected platforms. This role is instrumental in defining the roadmap for our digital subscription services, driving audience growth and revenue, and ensuring competitiveness in a fast-evolving landscape. Reporting directly to the SVP of Digital Strategy, the successful candidate will bring deep expertise in subscription ecosystems, customer segmentation, product packaging, pricing strategy, and cross-functional leadership.

 

Key Responsibilities:

· Define and execute end-to-end product and go-to-market strategies for digital subscription offerings across all consumer segments.

· Conduct assessments of Total Addressable Market (TAM), perform customer segmentation and needs analysis, and develop pricing models and packaging strategies to drive business growth.

· Collaborate with cross-functional teams—including design, engineering, marketing, sales, operations, and business development—to ensure a unified approach to product development and market execution.

· Monitor market trends, competitive landscape, and emerging technologies to identify strategic opportunities and potential threats.

· Build and maintain robust financial models to support decision-making, forecast performance, and prioritize investment opportunities.

· Analyze user behavior and business performance using quantitative and qualitative data to inform product roadmap and feature prioritization.

· Serve as a key voice in business development efforts, providing product insight and support for partnership and audience acquisition opportunities.

· Communicate key findings, strategic recommendations, and performance updates to senior leadership and stakeholders.

 

Qualifications:

· 7+ years of experience in digital product management, with at least 5 years developing and executing go-to-market strategies.

· Bachelor's degree in Business, Engineering, Digital Media, or related field; MBA preferred.

· Proven success in managing consumer-facing digital subscription products across multiple platforms.

· Deep understanding of the digital subscription ecosystem and associated business models.

· Experience across product marketing, pricing, sales enablement, and communications, with a strong ability to resolve complex internal and external challenges.

· Strong strategic thinking, analytical rigor, and creative problem-solving abilities.

· Demonstrated experience in cross-functional leadership and stakeholder management.

· Exceptional communication and presentation skills, with the ability to influence and inspire across all levels of the organization.

· Skilled in financial analysis and scenario modeling to support strategic initiatives.

· Ability to interpret complex business documents such as financial statements and legal agreements.

 

 

 

ABOUT ACCUWEATHER   AccuWeather, recognized and documented as the most accurate and most used source of weather forecasts and warnings in the world, has saved over 12,000 lives, prevented injury to over 100,000 people, and saved companies tens of billions of dollars through better planning and decision-making.   Billions of people around the world rely on AccuWeather’s proven Superior Accuracy™ across our consumer digital platforms. AccuWeather.com is the #1 weather destination and one of the top 100 most-visited websites in the world, and our award-winning AccuWeather app delivers detailed real-time forecasts to tens of millions of smartphones.   AccuWeather forecasts also appear on digital signage, in 700 newspapers, are heard on over 400 radio stations, and viewed on 100 television stations. The AccuWeather Network and AccuWeather NOW® reach an audience of over 225 million on cable and streaming platforms including DirecTV, Charter Communications - Spectrum, Verizon, Samsung, Vizio, Philo, Frndly TV, Comcast’s Xfinity X1 and Xfinity Stream, Roku, Xumo, Rockbot, LG, and Amazon Freevee.   AccuWeather For Business serves more than half of the Fortune 500 companies and thousands of other businesses and government agencies globally.   Dr. Joel Myers, Founder and Executive Chairman, established AccuWeather in 1962 and is considered the “father of modern commercial meteorology.” Myers is a visionary entrepreneur and has been called “the most accurate man in weather” by The New York Times. He has been recognized in Entrepreneur Magazine’s Encyclopedia of Entrepreneurs as one of the greatest entrepreneurs in American history. Myers received the American Meteorological Society’s 2018 Award for Outstanding Contributions to the Advancement of Applied Meteorology and the National Weather Association’s 2017 Lifetime Achievement Award, in addition to numerous other accolades.   COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY & INCLUSION   AccuWeather is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity to all applicants and existing employees and we evaluate qualified applicants without regard to race, creed, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy and gender identity/expression), sexual orientation, age, ancestry, physical or mental disability, marital status, political affiliation, religion, citizenship status, genetic information, veteran status, or any other basis protected under applicable federal, state, or local law.   AccuWeather is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation because of a disability for any part of the employment process, please send an e-mail to human.resources@accuweather.com and let us know the nature of your request and your contact information.

job.title: Senior Producer, Reporter Video
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times is continuing to expand its video journalism, identifying compelling visual stories across the depth and breadth of our reporting. We showcase the expertise of Times journalists on camera, share urgent news updates, produce on-the-ground reporting, and pioneer Visual Investigations.

The Video department is looking for a Senior Producer to work on the multi-disciplinary Reporter Video team of video journalists who create powerful videos featuring the expertise of our world-class journalists. Based in London, this role will focus on covering breaking news and major international developments in short-form video, producing a mix of quick-turnaround videos, explanatory and analysis pieces, as well as major enterprise and investigations. 

The Senior Producer will report to a London supervisor and work with the rest of the Reporter Video team in New York and other video hubs, becoming the key manager of the department’s content during the hours that London acts as the main Times hub. 

We are looking for a strong leader who is eager to motivate, inspire teams and innovate. Attention to detail, impeccable organization and effective communication with reporters and editors in the International Desk are a must.

You should also be an excellent storyteller with an eye for visual short-form digital formats, able to work autonomously to identify critical stories outside the U.S. and make sound, quick editorial decisions on world news. You will be expected to produce engaging stories through original reporting, on-the-ground filming, motion graphics and studio-based recordings.

You must have deep experience reporting on stories from Europe, the Middle East and Africa, including managing teams in conflict zones, devising security plans and making risk assessments.

This is a hybrid position based in London and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week.

Responsibilities will include:

  • Drive innovative Reporter Video delivering on a range of formats.

  • Build and strengthen relations with colleagues on the International Desk, including mentorship of reporters, photographers and fellow editors on the reporter video storytelling format.

  • Lead story development and story edits.

  • Review, assign and provide feedback on productions.

  • Support and guide script writing and visual approaches for effective short-form video.

  • Oversee production across multiple projects.

  • Guide interviews and shoots as needed, both in studio and field.

  • Foster experiments with new video approaches and editorial strategies.

  • Manage video journalists and video editors in the newsroom and field.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • This role reports to the Supervising Producer in London.

Basic Requirements:

  • Proven experience producing digital news videos.

  • Experience managing video journalists, also during field deployments, including in hostile environments and involving risk assessments.

  • Broad and in depth experience in digital or broadcast news.

  • Proven track record managing direct reports.

  • Demonstrated deep command of a variety of video sources, including wire services, UGC, archival footage, motion graphics, and original footage.

Preferred Requirements:

  • Excellent writing, editing and communication skills.

  • Expert knowledge of current events with advanced-level experience covering breaking news stories in the U.S. and internationally. 

  • Experience working collaboratively with members of a multidisciplinary team.

  • Experience overseeing shoots and interviewing experts on camera.

  • Familiar with digital storytelling formats.

  • Understanding of mainstream and emerging social channels

  • Flexibility to work extended hours.

job.title: Senior Video Journalist, Live Video Production
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times is seeking an experienced video journalist to join the growing Daily News video team in New York and help lead the video response to breaking and developing news in newsroom live blogs and coverage. You will help support our live journalism, scaling new workflows and communicating schedules and production timelines.

You are passionate about breaking and developing news and have deep knowledge of visual digital journalism. Previous experience working on digital live coverage and with content management systems is a plus. You will bring a strong understanding of editorial priorities and collaborate with visual journalists on the team. You will be responsible for producing immediate updates with short video clips that take our audience to the scene for ongoing stories, brainstorming visual opportunities for the blog for tentpole news events and pitching relevant visual stories that complement our coverage.

You have strong organizational skills and are able to communicate requests in a clear and efficient manner. You can work under deadlines and thrive in a dynamic and fast-paced environment. We're looking for a candidate who will relentlessly find the best video for a news story and has a track record of working on multiple projects at any given time.

This is an in-office position based in New York City and includes regular attendance four days a week. There may be some flexibility per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Own and coordinate coverage plans for news video in live blogs and related programming work, including livestreams, videos for reporter updates and clips for carousels.
  • Collaborate with the Live news team to plan for upcoming news events and visual opportunities.
  • Monitor the news day across core areas of coverage.
  • Identify opportunities to improve workflow, project tracking and automated reminders for production updates.
  • Manage workflow and process documentation.
  • Pitch visually driven videos for live blogs.
  • Use news wire services such as AP and Reuters to acquire material.
  • Guide the work of others on the team by overseeing clips and assigning daily news targets
  • Experiment with different forms of vertical and mobile visual storytelling.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • This role reports to the Daily News Director on the video team based in New York.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of journalism, video storytelling or video production experience, preferably in a digital video newsroom
  • Significant and proven experience reporting in complex and breaking-news environments under tight deadline
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently and decisively, take initiative and carry out all aspects of production with limited guidance
  • Proficient in Adobe Premiere Pro, able to edit quickly and accurately.
  • Strong editorial news judgment and writing skills, with a passion for breaking news.
  • Demonstrated social media platform expertise
  • Experience setting priorities, managing multiple projects and guiding or coordinating the work of other video journalists

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Thorough knowledge of global current events and a track record of covering news across multiple subject areas or regions
  • A foundational knowledge of legal, ethical, copyright and usage issues for visuals.
  • Well-versed in the world of social and digital media, with a keen eye on what competitors are doing and what new tools are being used.
  • Willingness to work evenings and weekends as the news demands.
  • Collaborative team player with a positive attitude

job.title: Staff Photo Editor, Business
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

A Photo Editor for The New York Times has a creative eye and an innovative approach to formats and mobile-focused presentations. You should bring sharp technical skills and sound journalistic judgment to join a team creating visual journalism—still and video— for breaking news, features and enterprise stories for on- and off-platform publishing.

The primary duties of the job are to conceptualize and assign photography and video for the New York Times’ Business report, and to select and publish images and video for multiple platforms of The New York Times. You will assign and research a wide array of news and feature photographs and video, working productively with staff photographers, freelance photographers, wire services, agencies and all other sources of pictures, as well as editors, designers, and reporters in the newsroom. You will engage our staff and freelance photographers to identify and develop pitches with strong visual potential, producing strong photographic, video and multimedia displays with an eye toward innovative digital story forms and presentations.

You have a strong demonstrable passion for multimedia, journalism and photography of all kinds, and possess a broad knowledge of the current photographic, video, visual and social media landscape, including digitally innovative formats and mobile-first multimedia presentations. You must be a team player and a good communicator, and must initiate and develop ideas for photographs, short video clips and visual stories in different formats.

This is a hybrid position based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office 4 days each week.

Responsibilities:

  • Conceive of, pitch, develop, edit, pace and build powerful and innovative visual stories with attention to detail in a fast-paced newsroom
  • Maintain the highest standard of photography and multimedia assigning for feature, news and enterprise stories for all platforms including mobile, print and social
  • Identify, vet and onboard new contributing photojournalists as needed. Ensure that new contributors are versed and committed to ethical journalistic rigor, independence and integrity. Build relationships with the photographers you are directing through briefings, regular contact and feedback
  • Collaborate with writers, reporters, editors, visual editors and photographers to shape ideas into visual story opportunities
  • Demonstrate strong editorial judgment, working with Times editors and legal department for all vetting, copyright, legal and ethical questions
  • Focus on working with a diverse range of subjects and photographers, keeping our global and multigenerational audience in mind
  • Coordinate with Business desk editors and security team members to ensure the utmost preparation, training and safety of our photojournalists in the field
  • Maintain and meet your desk’s photo budget, process/approve invoices in a timely fashion
  • Attend photo department meetings to report and share your desk’s visual priorities
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world
  • This role reports to a Deputy Editor of Photography

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years experience in a newsroom or equivalent
  • Experience assigning and directing photojournalists in a variety of situations
  • Proven deep research skills
  • Expertise in handling electronic images, photographic usage and copyright issues
  • Strong technical skills, including proficiency in digital tools and programs, including content management systems, Photoshop, PhotoMechanic, video editing tools and social media platforms

Preferred Qualifications:

  • An enthusiasm for visual journalism and current events, coupled with keen news judgment and a firm sense of journalistic ethics
  • Strong organizational, communication and collaborative abilities.
  • Knowledge of Adobe Premiere is a plus
  • Experience prioritizing and managing multiple projects in fast-moving environments
  • The initiative to take on and learn new technologies and tasks.
  • Openness to working a flexible schedule as news demands.
  • Experience making quick decisions under deadlines in a high-pressure news environment

Please submit a portfolio with examples of work that you have assigned and/or edited along with your CV.

job.title: Video Journalist, Reporter Video
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times is an industry leader in visual journalism with reporting that includes extraordinary news coverage, investigations, and culture and lifestyle reporting. The Reporter Video team identifies compelling stories and brings the depth and breadth of our news report onto our site and other platforms through video that features the expertise of our world-class journalists.

This is a role for someone who wants to produce, edit and publish short-form vertical videos daily and is versatile enough to work on news, features, enterprise and investigative projects with colleagues across the newsroom. You have expertise in video storytelling, including video editing and writing creatively to visuals, as well as a sharp sense of the digital landscape. 

Your portfolio and work samples should reveal a strong grasp of modern mobile video storytelling, and it should show that you’re a quick learner with creative ideas and the ability to work on small or large teams. You are solid technically, ideas-oriented and have solid news judgment. Cinematography skills are an added asset. We’re looking for someone who excels on deadlines and has experience juggling multiple projects at any given time. 

This is an in-office position based in London and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Write, produce, edit and publish short-form vertical videos every day.
  • Help to identify breaking news and enterprise across our news report and create video that features the expertise of our journalists, whether working with reporters on camera or using voiceover or visual storytelling techniques including graphics and animation.
  • Write visually rich scripts with an emphasis on visual takeaways.
  • Experiment with various forms of short-form vertical video storytelling. 
  • Collaborate with visual editors to generate video formats that bring our best journalism to new audiences.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to a Senior Producer for Reporter Video in London.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Proven experience with video storytelling, video editing and production experience at a news organization.
  • Excellent news judgment and proven ability to work with colleagues and reporters to synthesize newsgathering and/or investigations into a tight, informative and engaging video.
  • Experience producing shoots and interviewing experts on camera.
  • Experience creating original videos that intelligently incorporate audio, video, still images and text.
  • Strong video editing skills with Adobe Premiere.
  • Facility in using photo, video, audio, graphics and animation in storytelling.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Thorough knowledge of global current events particularly in Europe, Africa and the Middle East.
  • Able to meet deadlines and adapt to change within an unpredictable news and production environment
  • Design and animation skills including experience with design and animation software (Figma, Illustrator, Photoshop and After Effects).
  • Experience working collaboratively with members of a multidisciplinary team.
  • Available to work a flexible schedule.

In your cover letter, include links to three videos from your work that best reflect the kind of reporter video work you could see The New York Times making. job.title: Lead Site Reliability Engineer
job.description:
Who We Are

UnitedMasters 

UnitedMasters is building a marketplace that connects artists, brands and fans - empowering artists to earn and grow. UnitedMasters has taken the bold step of building a music distribution service that, radically, puts artists first - disrupting the legacy music business by letting up-and-coming artists distribute their music directly to fans through streaming services while maintaining ownership of their master recording rights and up to 100% of royalties. Through the combination of UnitedMasters' music distribution platform and its deep ties to brands, UnitedMasters enables independent artists and change-makers to grow and earn unlike any other platform.

The UnitedMasters team is made up of musicians, marketers, engineers, and storytellers with backgrounds from YouTube, SoundCloud, Pandora, Facebook, Uber, Dropbox, Complex, VICE, and more. We work hand in hand with the award-winning creative teams that forge those innovative partnerships at Translation (our in-house creative advertising agency).

The Role

You'll partner with platform, data, QA, and product engineers across the organization, owning the intersection of reliability and security: the tooling, monitoring, alerting, emergency response, and systems design the whole org depends on.

A defining part of the role is building how we protect our systems going forward. We're investing in agentic, AI-driven security pipelines that continuously detect, triage, and help remediate vulnerabilities across our codebase and infrastructure — and you'll lead the design and stewardship of that capability.

Above all, though, this is a coaching and consulting role. We're looking for a strong listener, patient collaborator, thoughtful architect, and skilled builder — someone who identifies needs in reliability and security and empowers peer developers to improve them.

What You'll Do

  • Partner with platform, data, QA, and product teams to understand their automation, infrastructure, monitoring, and security needs.
  • Build tooling and processes that solve the problems those conversations surface.
  • Build and maintain an agentic vulnerability detection and mitigation pipeline that will scan, triage, and propose fixes, with human-in-the-loop guardrails.
  • Embed security into the development lifecycle, including threat modeling, supp ly-chain hygiene, secrets management, secure-by-default patterns.
  • Lead security and reliability incident response as first-class operational concerns.
  • Define company-level SLAs, SLOs, and Error Budgets, and help teams set their own.
  • Steer system design toward shared tooling and decisions that ensure reliability, scalability, security, and maintainability.
  • Join the on-call rotation as a peer to spot process gaps and coach on response.
  • Act as a senior escalation for infrastructure and security issues, helping resolve them while coaching teams to handle the next.
  • Own our AWS infrastructure and set the long-term strategy for our reliability and security posture, balancing scalability and cost.

Who You Are 

  • Senior-to-staff experience as an SRE, platform, or infrastructure engineer, owning production reliability at scale.
  • Hands-on application and/or infrastructure security experience; enough to lead the security conversation without a separate security team in the room.
  • Practical experience building with LLMs and agentic systems. You've shipped something real and understand their failure modes and where human oversight is non-negotiable.
  • Strong software engineering fundamentals. You build tools and systems, not just configure them.
  • A coaching instinct: you measure impact by how much you raise the teams around you.

Our Values

  • We Get on the Plane — Entrepreneurial spirit means fully committing to the journey not just having the idea.
  • We Expect Challenge + Respect — We constantly challenge each other and the work to reach excellence, always with respect.
  • We Are Defined by Our Resilience — We stay resourceful, fail fast, keep getting better, and never quit on our mission or our team.
  • We Pursue Answers Before the Question Has to Be Asked — We understand our customers so well that we anticipate what they need before they ask.
  • We Run Towards Darkness — We have the courage to work through uncertainty rather than settling for an easier, inferior plan.
  • We Know What We Don't Know — We bring confidence in what we do know, and honesty about what we don't.

Compensation

Salary Hiring Range: $195,000 - $240,000

Our salary ranges are designed to be competitive for companies of our size and within our industry and represent just one part of our overall rewards package. We also offer company-sponsored medical, dental, and vision plans, a 401(k) with company match, and, depending on the role and individual circumstances, additional compensation opportunities such as bonuses and stock options.

Individual pay rate decisions are based on a number of factors, including qualifications for the role, experience level, skillset, and balancing internal equity relative to peers at the company. We expect the majority of the candidates who are offered roles at our company to fall healthily throughout the range based on these factors.

The range above is for the expectations as laid out in the job description, however we are often open to a wide variety of profiles, and recognize that the person we hire may be less experienced (or more senior) than this job description as posted. If that ends up being the case, the updated salary range will be communicated with you as a candidate.

The salary range above is for NY/CA. As a company, we have a location-based strategy, which means the salary range could be lower or higher than this if the role is hired in another location.

UnitedMasters Inc. represents the creative solutions company, Translation, and the leading software and services platform for independent creators, UnitedMasters. UnitedMasters enables ownership, exposure, and new paths for financial return for independent creators, while Translation helps brands leverage the power of contemporary culture to achieve transformational growth. Combined, UnitedMasters, Inc. is the world's leading marketplace for cultural capital, connecting independent artists and brands to realize a future in which all creators own their future. job.title: Senior Enterprise Security Engineer
job.description:
SoundCloud empowers artists and fans to connect and share through music. Founded in 2007, SoundCloud is an artist-first platform empowering artists to build and grow their careers by providing them with the most progressive tools, services, and resources. With over 400+ million tracks from 40 million artists, the future of music is SoundCloud.

SoundCloud is looking for a Senior Enterprise Security Engineer to join our Security team. In this role, you will own the security of the infrastructure and cloud environments our employees rely on to build delightful experiences for creators and fans, spanning endpoint, identity, cloud, and third-party risk.

You will act as a key technical lead across our modern security stack: driving incident response, securing enterprise AI systems, hardening multi-cloud architecture, and automating threat detection. If you have a deep passion for security, a builder mindset, and a desire to shape a secure environment for a fast-scaling platform, this role is for you.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead security incident response: identifying, investigating, and remediating infrastructure incidents and endpoint anomalies
  • Own and evolve security for internal workplace, on-premises, and cloud environments (AWS, GCP)
  • Administer and harden Google Workspace and Context-Aware Access policies as a lead administrator
  • Manage and optimize our endpoint security stack, including SentinelOne EDR and device management via JAMF (macOS) and Intune (Windows/Linux)
  • Manage the security of our AI Inference, Agents, and Agentic Tooling
  • Drive our Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) program, working closely with Legal and Privacy to assess vendor security posture
  • Operate and tune Google SecOps (Chronicle SIEM) for threat detection, log correlation, and investigation workflows
  • Manage security awareness and phishing simulation programs
  • Partner with our IT team and NYC-based executives to ensure the security of our key employees.
  • Coordinate penetration testing and vulnerability assessments across infrastructure and applications
  • Promote security best practices through collaborative engagement with engineering and product teams
  • Identify and implement automation opportunities across security operations and integrations
  • Stay current with threat intelligence, security vendors, and evolving industry standards

Experience and Background:

  • 6+ years of hands-on experience in security engineering or a combined software engineering/security role
  • Broad understanding of the evolving cyber threat landscape, emerging attack vectors, and industry security trends
  • Deep proficiency with Google Workspace administration, including security settings, audit logging, and DLP controls
  • Practical experience with SentinelOne or equivalent EDR platforms
  • Hands-on experience with JAMF Pro (macOS fleet management) and Microsoft Intune (cross-platform MDM)
  • Working knowledge of Google SecOps / Chronicle SIEM — building parsers, detection rules, and dashboards
  • Experience running or contributing to a Third-Party Risk Management program
  • Strong cloud security background in AWS and/or GCP — IAM, security groups, audit trails, and config compliance
  • Familiarity with GitHub security features (GitHub Actions, secret scanning, dependency review, branch protections)
  • Proficiency in either Python, Ruby, or Go for security automation and tooling. Don’t worry, you’ll have an LLM to help with the others!
  • Experience with Terraform, containers, Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines, and secrets management in microservices architectures
  • Solid understanding of web application security, vulnerability assessment, and code review
  • Experience implementing Context-Aware Access policies and BeyondCorp / Zero Trust architecture is a strong plus
  • Hands-on experience with security awareness and phishing simulation platforms like KnowBe4 is highly preferred
  • Prior experience managing and securing Enterprise AI Platforms (such as Claude, OpenAI, and Cursor) is a distinct advantage
  • A degree in Computer Science or an equivalent demonstrable technical background is welcome, but not required
  • Passion for exploring new areas of security; security is in your DNA

The salary range for this role is $140,000- $170,000 annually. The final salary offered will be determined based on relative experience, skills, internal equity, and location. We also offer a generous total rewards program - read more about additional benefits and perks below! 

About us:

  • We are a multinational company with offices in the US (New York and Los Angeles), Germany (Berlin), and the UK (London)
  • We provide a flexible work culture that offers the opportunity to collaborate and connect in person at our offices as well as accommodating work from home
  • We are deeply committed to ensuring diversity, equity and inclusion at all levels of our organization and fostering a community where everyone’s voice, perspective and experience is respected and heard

  • Robust 401k program
  • Employee Equity Plan

  • 16 paid weeks for all parents (birthing and non-birthing), regardless of gender, to welcome newborns, adopted and foster children

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion at SoundCloud

SoundCloud is for everyone. Diversity and open expression are fundamental to our organization; they help us lead what’s next in music by understanding and empowering our creators and fans, no matter their identity. We acknowledge the challenges in the music industry, and strive to influence an inclusive culture where everyone can contribute respectfully and thrive, especially the historically marginalized communities that many of our creators, fans and SoundClouders identify with. job.description:
Title: Visuals Producer, Social Video

Schedule Format -Hybrid - San Francisco

Pay Information: $94,860 - $112,469



KQED is looking for a visuals producer who can make videos and graphics for our news social channels including Instagram, YouTube and TikTok. You’ll work directly with our social video producer and be part of the news department’s audience engagement team. You will also work with our award-winning photographers and reporters in the newsroom.

We’re looking for someone with a mix of experience in visual journalism, graphic design, and social media who can take our journalism and tell stories visually for Instagram, YouTube and TikTok. 

Show us how you can make the news informative and engaging, and how you think about bringing journalism and essential resources to new audiences on social media.

Visuals Producer, Social Video ADDENDUM

The Social Video-Visuals Producer is a visual journalist who has sharp skills creating videos on social platforms, such as Instagram, TikTok and YouTube Shorts. This producer thrives on turning news stories into memorable vertical videos, while working with journalists in a collaborative process. 

The Social Video-Visuals Producer creates videos from start to finish – ideating, scripting, shooting, editing and publishing – and is highly collaborative with newsroom colleagues in order to tell these stories. You love the Bay Area, enjoy telling our unique stories and are as enthusiastic about working in the field as you are of executing great edits. 

Journalism ethics is a must, so you must know how to gather news – both with reporters and on your own – and tell stories on social platforms in a fair and accurate manner. 
 

KQED envisions a public media organization with a culture that centers on human dignity, equity, and belonging. This will enable us to better serve and reflect the Bay Area through diverse and inclusive storytelling. 

We value the contributions of marginalized people in society — including Black, Indigenous, and all people of color,  people with disabilities, and LGBTQIA+ people — and we believe that these communities must be centered in the work we do, and we strongly encourage members of these communities to apply.

KQED Code of Ethics  https://www.kqed.org/about/code-ethics

The mission that drives us:

KQED provide citizens of Northern California with a community-supported alternative to commercial media.   We provide citizens with the knowledge they need to make informed decisions; convene community dialogue; bring the arts to everyone and engage audiences to share their stories. We help students and teachers thrive in 21st-century classrooms, and take people of all ages on journeys of exploration- exposing them to new people, places and ideas.

This role will work hybrid between working in KQED's newly renovated headquarters and working remotely. 

Essential functions: 
  • Planning and shooting video coverage of events in the Bay Area
  • Creating short form social videos on news and feature stories in the Bay Area
  • Strategizing new forms of visual content that will bring KQED reporting to a wider audience
  • Designing graphics for social platforms (such as Instagram, TikTok and YouTube) that provide valuable information and resources to communities in the Bay Area
  • Keeping aware of news photo shoots, posting photo carousels, and writing captions for Instagram
  • Work with reporters to create and execute a visual social strategy for their stories

Knowledge/Experience Required:
  • Excellent communication and writing skills; ability to write quickly and accurately, with an understanding of tone and style across platforms
  • Familiarity with graphic design, Canva, Photoshop, Premiere, Adobe, Google Drive, Slack
  • Experience editing photos for news publications.
  • Experience taking a story and writing succinct scripts for social media
  • Experience writing text and captions for social media posts
  • Some video editing experience
  • Advanced knowledge of YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok
  • Knowledge and interest in current events
  • Writes text with correct spelling, grammar and punctuation 
  • Ability to meet deadlines and goals while working under pressure
  • Ability to stay organized and prioritize tasks when working on multiple projects at once 
  • Interest and knowledge in Bay Area news with a focus on local communities 
  • Checks work before publication and maintains adherence to facts
  • Adherence to copyright laws; understanding of media licensing agreements 
  • Clear communication with colleagues 
  • Ability to stay focused, organized, communicative and proactive — you’ll be working with a number of journalists or staffers across the organization, potentially dealing with several different editors
  • Minimum of five years’ experience as Producer or Field Producer in media, preferably public media or through other informal institutions.
  • Published examples of digital video production and/or other forms of digital storytelling
  • Ability to work collaboratively and cooperatively with the KQED News team—strong interpersonal and communications skills preferred 
  • Proven ability to edit, with limited supervision, short format engagement videos or longer-form documentary style segments. Attention to detail and experience in fact checking preferred.
  • Proficient at utilizing the entire Adobe Creative Suite with an emphasis on Premiere Pro, After Effects, Audition, Photoshop and Illustrator
  • Ability to independently problem-solve and adapt quickly to news cycles, formats and styles. 
  • Experience troubleshooting edit issues, transcoding media, performing minor color correcting and media archiving.
  • Proven ability to engage in high-level writing, research, or production on original and creative topics for story development.  Ability to write or co-write short format texts with factual integrity that move, surprise, dazzle and engage. 
  • Proven ability to set up, light, record audio and shoot video for short format style segments in quick turnaround situations.
  • Experience with a wide range of cameras, lenses and related equipment.
  • Experience with social media and web distribution.
  • Knowledge of basic journalistic editorial principles, ethics and standards.
  • A passion for producing digital media and demonstrable experience covering the Bay Area.
  • Demonstrable collaboration skills and experience cultivating sources and partnerships.
  • Ability to represent KQED to the broader Bay Area community, other institutions, and the general public.

Knowledge/Experience Desired:
  • A compelling visual style and personal voice.
  • Expertise in making digital videos.
  • Expertise in social media.
  • Expertise as a still photographer.
  • Experienced with web publishing and CMS systems (WordPress preferred).
  • B.A./B.S. degree.

Recommended Skills:
  • Familiarity with After Effects
  • Experience creating infographics or data visualizations
  • Comfortable being on camera

job.title: Fill In Journalist (Anchor-Editor-Writer)
job.description:
Our company is committed to being trusted voices of light and truth reaching hundreds of millions of people worldwide.

Who We Are

At Bonneville International, our purpose is to build up, connect, inform, and celebrate communities and families in the markets we serve. As an integrated media company, we provide content, advertising, and digital marketing solutions across 19 radio stations in Denver, Phoenix, Sacramento, Salt Lake City, and Seattle, along with the NBC Affiliate TV station, KSL-TV 5, in Salt Lake. We are responsible for lifting and inspiring with respect and giving voice to all the communities and clients we serve.

We believe that empowering our employees to share their ideas and experiences will fuel creativity, innovation, and inspiration. A diverse and inclusive workforce is crucial to our ability to create and deliver exceptional content, products, and services that represent our communities. We’re proud of our history and we want talented people to join us as we continue to grow!

To learn more about Bonneville and how our local media matters, visit: https://bonneville.com/

Position Overview

The Fill In (On call) Journalist - Anchor / Editor / Writer position is a role that requires the ability to show an aptitude for broadcast delivery and news production of factual, well-written, contemporary news that is informative, compelling, and entertaining. This role will collaborate with news and talk show teams to produce and share stories that resonate on broadcast channels and digital spaces. Proficiency in multimedia delivery is essential, as is the ability to generate factual, articulate, and compelling news content. In this on-call capacity, the role involves contributing to talk shows, the news department, and maintaining a strong presence on MyNorthwest.com. The ideal candidate will be adept at working independently in a deadline-driven environment, excel at multitasking, and communicate effectively with team members, particularly in high-stress scenarios. 

This role will serve as a back up for the Anchor / Editor role, but must also be able to write for the website and report as needed.

Note:  Work configurations are subject to change based on business needs and at company discretion.

  • This position is an onsite role that requires the employee to work at our Seattle site.

What You Will Do:

Primary job duties will include, but are not limited to:

  • Produce accurate and engaging news content for both over-the-air and online. (including, but not limited to enterprise interviews and stories). 
  • Ensure a consistent and high level of accuracy in news reporting, while upholding the station’s branding. 
  • Find, record, edit, and mix audio promptly to meet deadlines. 
  • Write brief, factual, and compelling newscasts, updates, and traffic reports and deliver them live on air.
  • Work with speed and efficiency, responding decisively and aggressively to breaking news situations
  • Identify and secure interviews with guests and newsmakers; build a robust network of news sources and contacts. 
  • Maintain proficiency with technical systems relevant to multimedia broadcasting. 

Skills and Experience We Are Looking For:

  • Must have flexibility in schedule and be available for a variety of back up coverage when needed from 4AM to 7 PM. 
  • Story Development: Proficient in identifying, developing, and delivering engaging news stories and creating original content. 
  • Audio Proficiency: Skilled in recording and editing audio.
  • Able to orally deliver professional newscasts, reports and updates, both live and recorded 
  • News Writing: Able to write factual, captivating, concise, conversational, news and broadcast copy with the added ability to proficiently deliver the copy on-air
  • Web Writing: Exceptional news writing, editing, headline writing and grammar skills; Also able to ghostwrite or adopt another contributor’s style and tone.
  • Technical Savvy: Computer literate with technical skills/acumen necessary to operate studio equipment, ease of working with technology and learning new systems. 
  • Independent and Team Work: Ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a team. 
  • Organizational Skills: Highly organized with meticulous attention to detail and superior time management abilities. 
  • Journalistic Integrity: A profound understanding of journalistic standards, ethics, and expectations, with demonstrated history of news judgment. 
  • Multitasking and Communication: Proven multitasking skills and the ability to communicate clearly and calmly under pressure. 
  • Receptiveness to Feedback: Openness to direction and feedback, with the ability to integrate it into work. 
  • Education: A four-year degree in journalism or a related communications field, preferred. 
  • Experience: Three plus years in news editing/producing, anchoring, and reporting, preferred. 
  • Regional Knowledge: Familiarity with local issues and political dynamics, preferred. 

Physical Demands

  • Receive, process, and maintain information through oral and/or written communication effectively.
  • Manual dexterity and fine motor skills to operate computer keys and general office equipment. Ability to work on a computer for prolonged periods of time.
  • Valid driver’s license and clean driving record.

Compensation Range

$28.59 - $40 This comp range spans multiple levels for this role.

Hourly rate will be determined by an evaluation of the education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities of the applicant along with internal and external benchmarks. The pay range provided here spans multiple levels for this role.

What We Offer You: Check Out Our Bonneville Benefits!

Employees at Bonneville can enjoy a broad offering of benefits, including:

  • Paid sick leave accruals
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP) services
  • Access to an entire team of free financial planners
  • Continuous growth and development opportunities
  • Dynamic team culture that values teamwork, having fun, and collaboration

Bonneville is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other characteristic protected by law. Minority/female/disability PWDNET/veteran are encouraged to apply.

job.title: Production Support Specialist (36)- 2nd Shift
job.description:
FIND OUT WHAT IT IS LIKE TO BE A PART OF HALLMARK SUPPLY CHAIN

JOB OVERVIEW

You’ll be at the heart of our production center, helping millions of customers across the world enjoy Hallmark products. You will have a variety of duties that support the production process in numerous ways. You’ll be cross-trained across multiple departments by a support team of trainers and supervisors to help you learn every step of the way!


SALARY AND SHIFT DETAILS

  • Your starting pay will be between $19.80 - $22.65 depending on your shift.
  • This position is a full-time, 5-day work week position in the 2nd shift from 3:30pm - 11:30pm, Monday through Friday.
    Don’t see a shift that works for you? We still encourage you to apply! We’ll work with you to find a shift that fits your lifestyle and gives you the flexibility you need.

The Production Support Specialist in Lawrence has a variety of duties that support production in numerous ways.  Prepares greeting card stock for the Cutter to cut.  Jogs, skids and moves stock to the cutter.  Carries stock to skids and moves finished skids into the outgoing area.  Responsible for complete make-ready, run, monitoring and maintenance.  Removes die cut cards from full sheets either using a hammer or by using an Automatic Card Extractor (ACE).  Performs make-readies on the ACE and prepares rails/bars and press set-up.  Responsible for quality sampling and stacking cards onto skids according to register, blockouts, salvage and spoilage.  Determines when adhesive will be mixed and when test will be performed on the mixture.  Responsible for ensuring that the ingredients are in the area for mixing the adhesive.  Assists the Webtron press operator with press set up and changeover, make-readies, machine adjustments and routine preventative maintenance procedures.  Responsible for supporting the production areas by ordering the correct stock, moving components in and out of the areas, inputting information on the computer system, and maintaining a clean, safe, work environment. 

Positively participates in performance dialogues and other team problem-solving activities.  Sets up and operates a Gem/Cello machine, wholesale sealer, accumulator and shrink tunnel which shrinks poly film around wholesale unit of specialty items and/or operates a lift truck and keeps track of stock in the OAI.  Performs all paperwork assigned involved in moving stock, either into or out of the department.  Packs finished goods on a packaging line.  Identifies potential problems, and shows willingness to proactively work on problem resolution and alternative solutions to traditional methods of operation.  Flexibility is key as the incumbent will be expected to move to different work assignments as needed.

Important things to know:

  • Position may be in several departments and incumbent will be expected to learn and perform multiple assignments within this job classification.

  • In the production areas there is some noise. Hearing protection is provided by Hallmark.
  • Overtime is available and will be covered during the interview process.

In this position you will:

  • Perform make-ready duties on the Gem/Cello machines, ACE press and Webtron presses.  Set up wholesale sealer and pack product into shipping containers.  Mix adhesives and assure the proper ingredients and quantities are available in the area. 
  • Execute Quality System including preflight, sampling plan and the removal of salvage/spoilage.  Perform quality and/or adhesive test and report results in a timely manner.  Plan and maintain the workflow through the department in accordance with work schedule.  Order and deliver stock, cartons, and other components needed for production to the work area. 
  • Achieve and continually improve specified production including production goals, throughput, etc. during training.  Participate in performance dialogues and team problem-solving activities.  .
  • Complete regular press maintenance and cleaning, including TPM’s.  Move skids of stock into and away from the press, including completion of related paperwork.  Transport and handle hazardous waste material in accordance with all Federal, State, and Local regulations.  Be certified to operate power lift equipment and skid inverting machine. 
  • Demonstrate the flexibility and teamwork to positively influence how goals are accomplished within shorter periods of time.  Effectively communicate information to the next shift to ensure consistency and continuous operation. 
  • Utilize good safety practices.

 

YOUR AREAS OF KNOWLEDGE AND EXPERTISE

Basic Qualifications

  • You’re at least 18 years of age
  • You have the ability to grip and push/pull lifts of stock 2”-3.5” thick, 80-120 times per hour
  • You have the ability to lift 20-30 lb stacks of stock, 60-80 times per hour, with frequent lifting throughout the shift of 40-60 lbs.
  • You have the ability to constantly stand, walk, twist, bend, and reach above shoulder level
  • You have the ability to constantly use repetitive hand/wrist motion and perform fine motor skills

Preferred Qualifications

  • High school diploma, GED, or equivalent
  • Strong communication- and problem-solving skills

WHY YOU’LL LOVE WORKING AT HALLMARK

We want to help you be your best – at work and at home, now and in the future. It’s why providing benefits to support you and your family’s well-being is one of the most important investments Hallmark makes.

  • Your Health: Medical, vision, and dental plans; Specialized plan option for people with type 2 diabetes; Short-term and long-term disability coverage; Life and accident insurance
  • Your Well-Being: On-site registered nurses who provide health consultations and optional seasonal vaccinations. Health rewards program (earn up to $400 per year).
  • Your finances: A 401(k) with a 4% company match vested from day one. Health savings (HSA) or Flexible spending (FSA) accounts.
  • Your life: During your first year, you’ll receive 18 days (144 hours) of PTO and 10 paid holidays. Paid parental leave, adoption assistance, and comprehensive fertility benefits for eligible employees.
  • Your work environment: Climate-controlled and safety-first environment; On-site café that offers hot and cold meals; On-site Hallmark store where you can shop Hallmark products for 50%-75% off; Inclusive environment and a relaxed dress code, with a few safety rules to follow (close-toed shoes are required). Whether you have purple hair or express yourself through body art, we want you to bring your whole self to work.
  •  Your career: A career with Hallmark can take you anywhere. Our career paths are shaped by your talents and ambitions. Whether you want to take the next step up in a role you know and love or are looking to move into an entirely new area or location. We can help you do just that.

Now’s your chance to embrace a future with Hallmark—just follow the instructions below to apply. 

You must show how you meet the basic qualifications in a resume or document you upload, or by completing the work experience and education application fields. Accepted file types are DOCX and PDF.  

In compliance with the Immigration Reform and Control Act of 1986, Hallmark Cards, Inc. and its subsidiary companies will hire only individuals lawfully authorized to work in the United States. Hallmark does not generally provide sponsorship for employment. 

Employment by Hallmark is contingent upon the signing of the Employment Agreement, signing of an agreement to arbitrate in connection with the Hallmark Dispute Resolution Program, completing Form I-9 Employment Eligibility Verification, passing the urinalysis drug screen, education verification and satisfactory reference and background checks. 

Hallmark is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will be considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, pregnancy, national origin, physical or mental disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, or any other legally-protected status. Principals only please. 

HALLMARK – Because Connecting With Each Other Has Never Been More Important 

For more than a century, Hallmark has been bringing people together and improving the relationships that matter most. That’s why millions of people all over the world connect with the Hallmark brand. It has always been a mission so much bigger than any one of us who work here.

Today, we need empathetic learners, strategic thinkers, and enthusiastic visionaries with diverse experiences and skills to help us create the rest of Hallmark’s second century as we shift to a more digitally savvy, unified approach that combines the best of brick-and-mortar retail with the efficiency of dot-com spaces. Help us imagine what our next hundred years could look like! 

When you join Hallmark, we will go out of our way to make you feel like part of the team. In the day-to-day, we’ll make the best use of the skills and talents you already have. We’ll also give you leadership opportunities and show you multiple potential pathways to future success. 

Our culture of care for our consumers and for one another shows in the way we embrace different backgrounds, identities, and working styles, deliberately seeking out ways to be more inclusive both internally among our work groups and externally through the things we make and sell to our retail partners and consumers. We believe that a broadly inclusive, equitable approach is also our best path to future success. We’re seeking out those who can bring a fresh perspective to our business and would love your input as someone new to our team! We can only change and grow when we intentionally include new perspectives–like yours.

The Maintenance Mechanic position reports through the Maintenance Department within the Lawrence Production Center.  Individuals in this department provide the necessary skills to install and maintain the production equipment in support of manufacturing.    

 

The Maintenance Mechanic in Lawrence is full time 40 hours a week, Monday - Friday 7:30am - 3:30pm

  • Competitive hourly rate - $26-$38 based on experience

 

The Maintenance Mechanic demonstrates a broad range of mechanical and troubleshooting skills by having the ability to repair equipment that ranges from simplistic (i.e. batch counter) to complex (i.e. troubleshooting PLC/Ladder logic programming).  Specialists install machinery and equipment to be used in production or related process by assembling, leveling, and securing the equipment. Specialists are also responsible for making the necessary electrical, compressed air, gas, and water connections.  They dismantle machinery as required, transport, reassemble, and make new connections when either moving from one location to another or disposing of equipment.  Specialists repair and maintain machinery/equipment to keep in compliance with safety, blueprints, and manufacturer specifications. Maintenance Specialists install/troubleshoot/repair electrical wiring, replace belts, fabricate parts, read schematics, and troubleshoot Programmable Logic Controllers (PLC), etc.  They also may be asked to modify existing equipment or designs and build new machines to improve capacity, quality, safety, or cost.  Specialists instruct operators and Operations Supervisors in the operation of new or modified equipment and work with them until they can satisfactorily and safely operate the equipment.  They often transport and handle hazardous waste material in-accordance-with all Federal, State, and Local regulations. job.title: Customer Service Representative - Halls KC Concierge (On-call)
job.description:
WHO WE ARE:

Crown Center, one of the nation’s first mixed-use redevelopments, is an 85-acre complex that welcomes more than five million visitors each year. A subsidiary of Hallmark Cards, Crown Center is a ‘city within a city’ – combining hotel, office, retail, residential and entertainment land uses within its boundaries.

Halls KC provides the ultimate in trend-setting design, exclusive brands, and superior customer service. Our beautiful, 60,000 square foot store is located on the third level of the Crown Center shops in the heart of Kansas City. Halls KC offers shopping experiences in a fresh and exciting environment, taking an active role in Crown Center’s goal of creating a vibrant central city. 

 

WHAT WE DO AND HOW WE DO IT:

The On-call Customer Service Representative (Halls Concierge) is the first point of contact for Halls customers, delivering an exceptional shopping experience at Halls KC – a luxury retail store. This role requires a passion for customer satisfaction, strong communication skills, and the ability to manage multiple tasks with precision and professionalism. The On-call Customer Service Representative (Halls Concierge) is responsible for cash handling, gift wrapping, stocking supplies in Hall Concierge, and performs other responsibilities as required by management.

 

IN THIS ROLE YOU WILL:

Provide exceptional customer service with a focus on creating memorable experiences and ensuring customer satisfaction. Exhibit empathy, patience, and a positive attitude when addressing customer needs or concerns. Uphold Halls’ brand image and demonstrate a passion for our customers in every interaction. Answer incoming phone calls, transfer calls appropriately, and assist with inquiries in a courteous and professional manner.

Collaborate effectively with team members, demonstrating a positive team player attitude within the department and the entire store. Perform gift wrapping and gift boxing services to maintain Halls’ high standards of presentation. Multitask in a fast-paced environment while maintaining attention to detail. Cash management and cash handling accurately and responsibly. Maintain and stock supplies in the concierge area to ensure readiness and efficiency. Keep the customer service area clean, organized, and visually appealing.

job.title: Research Product Manager AP Intelligence
job.description:
The Associated Press is an independent global news organization dedicated to factual reporting. Founded in 1846, AP today remains the most trusted source of fast, accurate, unbiased news in all formats and the essential provider of the technology and services vital to the news business. More than half the world's population sees AP journalism every day.

 

About AP Intelligence 

The Associated Press is an independent global news organization dedicated to factual, accurate and nonpartisan reporting. 

 

AP Intelligence is building a new intelligence layer on top of AP’s global reporting—transforming verified journalism into structured facts, events, entities, relationships and signals that machines and people can use in real time. 

 

By combining AP’s firsthand reporting, editorial standards, historical depth and global reach with modern data and AI infrastructure, AP Intelligence creates machine-readable intelligence that can be integrated into models, applications and decision systems. 

 

We are expanding the product team responsible for determining what intelligence can be derived from AP reporting, how we know it is useful and reliable, and which capabilities should become scalable products. 

 

The Role 

We are seeking an intellectually curious, highly analytical Research Product Manager to lead research and product definition for emerging AP Intelligence capabilities. This is a 0→1 individual contributor role. Much of the work begins before there is a roadmap—and sometimes before the precise product problem is fully understood. 

 

You will turn broad questions into structured hypotheses, research plans and experiments; investigate them using data, customer conversations and lightweight prototypes; and translate what you learn into clear product decisions and requirements. 

 

Here, “research” means structured product investigation: framing unanswered questions, working directly with data and product outputs, testing hypotheses, evaluating results and learning from customers. 

 

This is not a traditional feature-delivery PM role. You will help discover the problems, define the products and establish the frameworks that allow engineering teams to build them. 

 

The role does not have direct reports at the outset, but offers significant ownership and visibility. As AP Intelligence grows, its scope may expand based on business needs and the individual’s strengths and interests, including deeper product leadership, domain ownership or people leadership. 

 

What You’ll Do 

Research, Prototype & Evaluate 

  • Lead research into ambiguous product questions across event intelligence, structured news data, knowledge graphs, real-time information and AI systems. 

  • Turn questions such as “What makes an event important?” or “How should we measure whether a signal is reliable and useful?” into hypotheses, experiments and evaluation frameworks. 

  • Work hands-on with AP datasets and product outputs, using tools such as SQL, Python, notebooks, LLMs and lightweight prototypes to test ideas. 

  • Design benchmarks and evaluation methods for dimensions such as accuracy, timeliness, confidence, relevance and usefulness. 

  • Identify patterns that can become scalable schemas, taxonomies, scoring systems and product capabilities. 

Define Products & Influence the Roadmap 

  • Translate research into clear product concepts, requirements and recommendations engineering teams can build. 

  • Define how concepts such as event importance, impact, velocity, provenance and confidence become useful AP Intelligence capabilities. 

  • Partner with engineering and applied AI teams to identify failure modes, improve product quality and move promising ideas from prototype to production. 

  • Use evidence to recommend which ideas should advance, change or stop and to inform AP Intelligence priorities. 

Learn With Customers & Lead Across Disciplines 

  • Work directly with prospective customers and design partners to understand workflows, test emerging concepts and determine where AP Intelligence creates meaningful value. 

  • Assess not only whether a capability is technically possible, but whether customers will integrate it, rely on it and pay for it. 

  • Partner closely with journalists, engineers, AI teams, commercial teams and senior leaders. 

  • Synthesize editorial, technical, customer and commercial perspectives into clear decisions and communicate complex ideas to technical and nontechnical audiences. 

 

Who You Are 

We expect strong candidates to bring many, but not necessarily all, of the following: 

  • 6+ years of relevant professional experience, including significant experience in product management, data products, AI/ML products, applied research, search/information systems or another highly analytical product environment. We care more about demonstrated 0→1 product ownership and judgment than a conventional career path. 

  • A strong track record of taking ambiguous problems and independently turning them into structured questions, experiments and product recommendations. 

  • Exceptional analytical and conceptual thinking, with an ability to find patterns in complex information and develop clear points of view from incomplete evidence. 

  • Strong technical and data fluency. You do not need to be a production engineer, but should be comfortable exploring datasets, interrogating outputs and building lightweight analyses or prototypes. 

  • Familiarity with structured or semi-structured data and areas such as APIs, taxonomies, ontologies, knowledge graphs, search, retrieval or related information systems. 

  • Working knowledge of modern AI systems and concepts, including LLMs, RAG, embeddings, information retrieval, structured outputs and model evaluation. 

  • Strong product and customer judgment, including the ability to distinguish an interesting research problem from a capability customers will use and value. 

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills and comfort working across engineering, AI, journalism, commercial teams and senior leadership. 

 

Experience with AI/ML products, knowledge graphs, search/retrieval, real-time or event-driven data, intelligence platforms, AI evaluation, financial/risk/geopolitical information products, or early-stage 0→1 environments is especially relevant, but not required. 

 

What Success Looks Like 

In your first year, you will have: 

  • Turned important unanswered AP Intelligence questions into rigorous product investigations and clear recommendations. 

  • Established benchmarks and evaluation frameworks for emerging capabilities. 

  • Helped define and validate new event, signal and intelligence capabilities from research through product definition. 

  • Influenced the AP Intelligence roadmap through evidence from data, customers and experimentation. 

 

Why This Role 

AP Intelligence sits at an unusual intersection of journalism, data infrastructure, artificial intelligence and real-world decision-making. 

 

AP has spent nearly two centuries building a global system for determining what happened, verifying it and communicating it accurately. AP Intelligence is exploring what becomes possible when that same reporting is structured for machines. 

 

For someone who enjoys ambiguous problems, data, emerging technology and building new products, this is an opportunity to help define a new category of product for AP. 

 

Location, Salary & Benefits 

This role may be based in New York, NY or remotely within the United States. 

 

The anticipated salary range is $140,000–$185,000, based on a candidate’s skills, qualifications and location. 

The Associated Press offers comprehensive benefits, including medical, dental and vision coverage; retirement benefits; company-paid life insurance; paid vacation and sick days; paid parental leave; and mental well-being resources. 

 

 

AP seeks to build an inclusive organization grounded in respect for differences. We support all aspects of diversity and provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, marital status, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, status as a veteran, or other characteristic protected by law.

job.description:

Sales Manager

#26-1336

Washington, District Of Columbia, United States

Apply

Business Unit

WTOP-AM/FM

Employee Classification

Full Time Regular

About Us

Hubbard DC, which includes WTOP, Federal News Network and 2060 Digital, is committed to reporting relevant news for our region. Through continuously evolving brands, we connect consumers with advertisers across a growing number of distribution platforms including radio, podcasts, social media, and websites. We do this with a commitment to our community...while growing our people and profits.

OUR VISION

To be an industry leader and set the standard for equality and inclusivity for all races, genders, ages, ethnicities, abilities, sexual orientations and religions by creating and fostering principles that integrate our core values.

OUR MISSION

To be proactive in providing a welcoming, professional environment; free of harassment, discrimination and marginalization with on-going habits that incorporate our unique experiences into the overall success and continuous evolution of this organization.

Job Overview

This position is responsible for leading the sales team to meet revenue goals and service client accounts.

Job Responsibilities

Develop and adapt short and long-term sales strategies to achieve revenue goals, improve client service, and respond to changes in the marketplace.

Recruit, develop, train, and motivate salespeople; build a collaborative culture with clear expectations and individual accountability.

Work alongside account managers to identify business needs and develop integrated marketing solutions.

Collaborate with the sales management team on sales procedures, pricing and programs that maximize revenue.

Help Account Managers Find, Renew and Grow revenue.

Join Account Managers on in person and video meetings with clients and prospective clients.

Provide regular coaching, constructive feedback, and training to improve prospecting, client discovery, presentations, closing, and account growth.

Use CRM and sales reporting systems consistently to manage account assignments.

Help Account Managers monitor budget performance and develop action plans when results fall short.

Lead client meetings and major presentations; build meaningful relationships with key customers and support new-business development.

Develop integrated marketing programs across our brands, connecting radio, digital, federal marketing and event capabilities to the client’s objectives and customer journey.

Participate in weekly sales meetings by sharing relevant product, community, audience, and market information with the sales team.

Identify and recruit talent to help grow the sales team.

Partner with Sales Management team on budgets, account distribution, compensation plans, and rate, inventory, and yield management within assigned responsibilities.

Coordinate with digital, creative, production, and client-service teams to support effective execution and strong client relationships.

Work with the sales and finance teams to address collections and maintain account payment performance in line with company expectations.

Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Minimum of six years of sales experience, including at least four years of sales management experience preferred.

Experience with digital and/or federal marketing is preferred.

Demonstrated success achieving revenue goals through a coordinated, organized, and effectively coached sales team.

Ability to create a strong sales culture, earn trust, communicate clearly, delegate effectively, and hold people accountable.

Proven ability to recruit, interview, train, coach, and motivate staff to reach their potential.

Strategic thinking and the ability to translate business priorities into practical sales plans, measurable goals, and consistent follow-through.

Experience developing client-focused, integrated marketing programs and applying digital and radio advertising capabilities to business objectives.

Ability to use audience and marketing research in consultative selling and train others in its use.

Strong client relationship, presentation, and collaboration skills; ability to establish positive working relationships with colleagues, vendors, and customers.

Ability to use sales systems and reporting to evaluate progress, prioritize opportunities, and adjust strategies in a changing marketplace.

Professional judgment and demeanor; ability to manage competing priorities, work collaboratively, and follow company policies and procedures.

A valid driver’s license and good driving record, subject to verification; ability to travel to client and business locations and work the established schedule and additional hours as needed.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

Ability to perform the essential functions of the role, including communicating with clients and colleagues, preparing and delivering presentations, and using a computer and standard office equipment. The Company may make reasonable accommodations to facilitate the ability to perform essential job functions.

WORKING ENVIRONMENT

Professional, collaborative office environment, with travel to client meetings and other business locations as needed.

Sales managers are expected to be either in office and/or on sales calls 75% of the week.

Additional Information

This position is subject to pre-employment driving record background check. A conviction, violation pending adjudication, or adverse driving record more than 3 years old or does not meet the major violation definition per company policy will not, on its own, disqualify an applicant. The company will use background check information in a confidential, non-discriminatory manner consistent with applicable federal, state and local law.

Compensation and Benefits

When extending an offer, the company considers a variety of factors such as (but not limited to) the candidate's work experience, education/training & key skills as well as internal peer equity and other market and business considerations.

Salary of $100,000, plus the majority of your compensation from override on all revenue.
