job.title: Account Executive
job.description:
About TEGNA

TEGNA Inc. helps people thrive in their local communities by providing the trusted local news and services that matter most. With 64 television stations in 51 U.S. markets, TEGNA reaches more than 100 million people monthly across the web, mobile apps, streaming, and linear television. Together, we are building a sustainable future for local news.

 

KENS-TV San Antonio, the TEGNA-owned CBS affiliate in San Antonio, is seeking a competitive, coachable and results-driven Account Executive to develop new business and grow a portfolio of advertising clients. This is an opportunity to build a career in media sales while gaining experience across broadcast television, streaming, connected TV and digital advertising.

You’ll sell one of the strongest portfolios in the market, combining the reach and trust of KENS broadcast television with the targeting and growth of streaming. On the linear side, you’ll connect advertisers with the large, engaged local audiences that turn to San Antonio’s trusted news and programming. On the streaming side, you’ll leverage Premion, TEGNA’s streaming and CTV advertising business, to reach cord-cutting audiences across a premium marketplace of 125+ OTT and connected-TV publishers. Together with digital video, display and content solutions, you’ll have a powerful cross-screen portfolio to help local businesses reach their customers and achieve their goals.

We provide the coaching, tools and support to help you build your skills and your business. You bring the drive to learn, compete and succeed.

Responsibilities

Develop new business. Build and maintain a strong pipeline through consistent prospecting. Research local businesses, identify key decision-makers and create opportunities across broadcast TV, Premion streaming/CTV and digital.

Manage the full sales process. Prospect, qualify, uncover client needs, present solutions, handle objections and close business while working toward established activity and revenue goals.

Sell consultatively. Learn each client’s business and marketing goals and recommend the right mix of broadcast television, Premion streaming/CTV and digital solutions to deliver measurable results.

Build compelling proposals. Develop data-informed presentations that demonstrate how broadcast reach and connected-TV targeting can work together to meet client objectives.

Grow client relationships. Build new accounts into long-term partnerships by delivering results, maintaining strong relationships and identifying opportunities for continued growth.

Manage your pipeline. Use CRM and prospecting tools to manage activity, maintain an accurate pipeline and keep opportunities moving. Partner with account, creative and product teams to deliver effective campaigns for clients.

Requirements

Competitive, self-motivated and goal-oriented with a genuine interest in building a career in sales.

Strong communication, presentation and relationship-building skills.

Coachable, curious and motivated to learn consultative media sales.

Strong organizational skills and follow-through, with the ability to manage multiple priorities.

Interest in broadcast television, streaming/CTV and digital advertising, with a willingness to learn and stay current on the evolving media landscape.

Sales, customer service, marketing or advertising experience preferred but not required. Internships, relevant coursework and transferable experience are welcome.

Bachelor’s degree preferred.

Comfort with Microsoft Office; familiarity with CRM or digital advertising tools is a plus.

Valid driver’s license and ability to travel locally to meet with clients as needed.

job.title: Senior Software Engineer
job.description:
Join the future of news

We’re on a mission to deliver riveting storytelling for all of America. At The Washington Post, you’ll help reinvent news. Our work is driven by a deep investigative spirit and enhanced by innovation to bring audiences closer to the stories that matter most.


About Our Team


The Washington Post is powered by the passion and talent of our people. It takes all of us to reinvent news. Beyond our award-winning News and Opinions teams, we work across many departments, including Brand & Events, Communications, Customer Care, Engineering & Product, Finance, Human Resources, Legal, Marketing & Advertising, Print Operations, and Sales.


Why This Role Matters

 

We are looking for a Senior Full Stack Engineer to join the Subscriptions team at The Washington Post. This role spans the full application stack with a strong emphasis on the cloud infrastructure, delivery systems, and operational practices that keep our subscription products reliable and scalable. As a senior engineer, you will take ownership of complex technical work, contribute to architectural decisions, and help improve how the team builds, deploys, and operates software.


The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in AWS, CI/CD, cloud infrastructure, and production operations, along with strong application development experience in Java - our primary backend language - and Node.js, and familiarity with React. We value autonomy, initiative, strong communication, and meaningful day-to-day use of AI-assisted engineering tools, including continually finding new ways to apply AI to development, automation, operations, and team effectiveness.


What Motivates You

  • Strong sense of ownership and accountability for both the software you build and the systems that run it.
  • Passionate about reliable, scalable systems and making software delivery faster, safer, and more repeatable.
  • Proactive and comfortable driving complex work with a high degree of autonomy.
  • Comfortable moving across application code, AWS infrastructure, CI/CD, developer tooling, and production operations.
  • Actively uses AI in day-to-day engineering and continually looks for ways to expand its impact on development, automation, operations, and productivity.
  • Enjoys collaborating across teams, mentoring others, and communicating technical decisions clearly upward and sideways.

How You'll Support the Mission

  • Design, build, test, deploy, and operate applications and services supporting our subscription products.
  • Own technical solutions throughout their lifecycle, from design and implementation through deployment, observability, production support, and continuous improvement.
  • Design and maintain scalable, reliable AWS infrastructure using services such as ECS, Lambda, S3, RDS, IAM, CloudWatch, and related technologies.
  • Build and evolve Infrastructure as Code, with experience using AWS CDK strongly valued.
  • Design, maintain, and continuously improve CI/CD pipelines, deployment automation, and developer workflows.
  • Configure, operate, troubleshoot, and improve self-hosted engineering platforms such as Jenkins, Airflow, and similar systems.
  • Develop backend services and APIs primarily using Java, with Node.js used across supporting services, automation, and tooling.
  • Contribute to frontend applications built with React and modern JavaScript/TypeScript when needed.
  • Build automation that reduces operational overhead and improves the reliability and repeatability of development and production processes.
  • Establish strong observability and diagnose complex issues spanning applications, infrastructure, deployment pipelines, and third-party integrations.
  • Participate in the team’s on-call rotation, taking ownership of incident diagnosis, mitigation, communication, and systemic follow-up.
  • Identify technical debt, operational bottlenecks, and opportunities for improvement and proactively drive solutions.
  • Communicate technical decisions, risks, tradeoffs, and progress clearly to engineering peers, leadership, product partners, and adjacent teams.
  • Mentor engineers and contribute to technical standards, architecture discussions, documentation, and engineering best practices.
  • Use AI extensively throughout the engineering lifecycle and identify opportunities to apply it to development, infrastructure, troubleshooting, automation, incident investigation, and operational workflows.

The Skills and Experience You Bring


Minimum Qualifications

  • BA/BS in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 5+ years of hands-on AWS experience, including designing, deploying, operating, and troubleshooting production workloads.
  • 4+ years of experience with CI/CD, deployment automation, and Infrastructure as Code in production environments.
  • 3+ years of backend development experience with Java, including building and operating production services and APIs. Java is the team’s primary backend language.
  • 2+ years of professional experience with Node.js, including services, automation, developer tooling, or infrastructure tooling.
  • Experience administering and operating self-hosted engineering platforms such as Jenkins, Airflow, or similar technologies in production environments.
  • Strong understanding of cloud architecture, networking, IAM, security, scalability, reliability, and operational best practices.
  • Experience building and maintaining Infrastructure as Code using AWS CDK, CloudFormation, Terraform, or comparable technologies.
  • Experience with containerized workloads and services such as Docker and ECS.
  • Strong production operations and observability experience, including logs, metrics, tracing, dashboards, alerting, and troubleshooting across applications and infrastructure.
  • Experience supporting business-critical systems through an on-call rotation, incident response, and post-incident remediation.
  • Strong software engineering fundamentals and the ability to contribute to application code when needed.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently identify, scope, and drive complex technical work with limited oversight.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate effectively upward and across organizational boundaries.
  • Significant hands-on use of AI-assisted engineering tools in day-to-day work. Candidates should be able to discuss concrete examples of applying AI to infrastructure, automation, software development, troubleshooting, incident investigation, documentation, or other engineering workflows.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 7+ years of hands-on AWS, DevOps, SRE, or cloud infrastructure experience, including ownership of highly available, scalable production environments.
  • 5+ years of experience designing and operating CI/CD, deployment automation, and Infrastructure as Code across multiple applications or teams.
  • 5+ years of backend development experience with Java and 3+ years with Node.js.
  • 2+ years of experience with React or a comparable modern frontend framework, with the ability to contribute to and support modern JavaScript/TypeScript applications when needed.
  • Deep experience with AWS CDK and building reusable infrastructure patterns, constructs, and deployment tooling.
  • Significant production experience administering and evolving Jenkins, Airflow, or comparable self-hosted engineering platforms.
  • Deep experience with AWS services such as ECS, Lambda, S3, RDS, IAM, CloudWatch, and related technologies.
  • Experience building reusable infrastructure, deployment patterns, automation, and developer tooling used across engineering teams.
  • Experience with observability platforms such as DataDog and AWS-native monitoring services.
  • Experience improving developer experience and engineering productivity through platform engineering, automation, and self-service tooling.
  • Experience mentoring engineers and influencing infrastructure, reliability, and operational practices across team boundaries.
  • Advanced use of AI-assisted engineering tools, including experience helping other engineers expand their effective use of AI across infrastructure, operations, automation, troubleshooting, and software development.

 

Collaboration makes us stronger. That’s why our offices are designed with open layouts, modern technology, and easy access to transportation. With certain exceptions for newsgathering and business travel, we work on-site five days a week.

Your story awaits. Apply today!

Learn more about The Post at careers.washingtonpost.com.

job.title: Fellow, A.I. Initiatives
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Join the 2027 New York Times Fellowship class as an A.I. Initiatives fellow in New York.

We are looking for a fellow who will bring a mix of machine-learning and journalism experience to newsroom reporting projects. You will work with journalists across departments to identify, develop and execute projects that use the power of artificial intelligence, machine learning and data science techniques to address investigative challenges. You will be part of the A.I. Initiatives team, which includes editors, engineers and a product designer.

This is an in-office position and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance. You may be required to work some nights, weekends and holidays as needed.

Responsibilities: 

  • Collaborate with investigative reporters to support projects that benefit from A.I., including large-scale research, transcription, translation, document search, language analysis and computer vision tasks
  • Identify opportunities and experiment with responsible A.I. tools to empower the newsroom
  • Participate in training and social programs designed for the fellowship
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Basic Qualifications:

  • No more than five years of full-time, professional experience in journalism and/or machine learning
  • Technical proficiency and experience analyzing data, developing applications and conducting research with machine-learning models
  • Editorial experience, such as interning in a newsroom or working on a college newspaper
  • Engineering skills and experience with APIs, front-end web applications and databases
  • Recent experience working with LLMs and other machine-learning models
  • Interest in the intersection of journalism and artificial intelligence
  • Understanding of ethical considerations surrounding the use of A.I. in journalism

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Record of multiple news or opinion journalism internships, or equivalent experience
  • Work demonstrating experience applying A.I. to real-world problems
  • Experience working with large datasets and cloud computing platforms
  • Experience working with Svelte or similar front-end frameworks

To apply, upload a résumé and cover letter. The application will prompt you when to upload materials. Applications that fail to include any of these materials or follow these instructions will not be considered.

You must be authorized to work in the United States. We will not sponsor work visas for the fellowship, but we will consider applicants with valid work authorization or a valid student visa that can be extended with Optional Practical Training.

You may apply to only one fellowship position per year. For instance, if you apply as an A.I. Initiatives fellow, you should not apply for any other positions in the fellowship. Duplicate applications will be discarded.

The application deadline is 5 p.m. Eastern Standard Time on Nov. 20. 

The Times Fellowship generates a high level of interest, so we cannot acknowledge the status of every application upon receipt or during the vetting process, which can take eight weeks or more. We cannot accept applications that are mailed or emailed to us. We will contact you for interviews as needed.

The fellowship program will begin on or about June 7, 2027, and end on May 26, 2028, subject to satisfactory performance. There is no guarantee of a full-time position upon completion of the program.

job.title: News producer
job.description:
Guardian Australia is part of Guardian News & Media (GNM), publisher of theguardian.com. As a leading global media organisation, we are renowned for our pioneering independent journalism and our award-winning digital products.

 

We are seeking for a news producer to be responsible for a full range of production tasks for Guardian Australia, including subediting and publishing stories, displaying them on the website and disseminating through social media.

 

This role is being offered on a full-time 12 month contract, working on a seven-day roster with early starts or late finishes, including one weekend day each week. This role is open to candidates in both 
Sydney and Melbourne.

 

In this role you will…

 

  • Edit copy for online content including articles, blogs, videos, galleries, interactives, podcasts and social media posts, correcting grammar and spelling, consistent with Guardian style
  • Ensure accuracy of what we publish
  • Write page furniture, assign tags
  • Add pictures and multimedia elements 
  • Write engaging and SEO-friendly web headlines
  • Add internal and external web links and cross-references
  • Create and/or edit picture galleries, polls and quizzes, video and audio pages
  • Display stories on the Guardian Australia website effectively and imaginatively 
  • Work on social media promotion of stories as required
  • Cover for the deputy production editor/production editor and news desk editors as required
  • Retrieve wire stories and use them to create articles
  • Liaise with reporters on story progress and to resolve any issues with filed stories
  • Liaise with lawyers, as needed, to resolve any outstanding issues before publication
     

You’ll bring….

 

Knowledge and experience

  • Subbing and production experience – ideally both online and print
  • Expertise in using web tools for editing and layout
  • Interest in and wide knowledge of the output of Guardian Australia
  • Demonstrable enthusiasm for and interest in web and print journalism
  • Understanding the editorial aims and values of the Guardian
  • Awareness of the needs and interests of the Guardian’s readers/audiences
  • Appreciation of Guardian history 
     

Skills and behaviours

  • Excellent writing and communication skills
  • Excellent production skills
  • Meticulous eye for detail, grammar and spelling
  • Ability to handle writers’ copy sensitively
  • Ability to learn and apply new skills quickly and thoroughly
  • Willingness to take responsibility for editing decisions, in collaboration with the news desk
  • Excellent planning and organisational skills 
  • Ability to edit copy quickly and accurately under pressure
  • Flair for writing headlines and other page furniture
  • Team player, enthusiastic with strong interpersonal skills
  • Logical, imaginative, adaptable and flexible
  • Ability to accept constructive criticism
  • A passion for independent journalism and an understanding of our editorial code and values


About working at Guardian Australia… 
 

  • Hybrid working 
  • Employee assistance program (EAP) to support employee wellbeing
  • Paid volunteer leave
  • Dedicated diversity and inclusion employee groups, action plans (including our Reconciliation Action Plan) and cultural competency training
  • Guardian digital subscription
     

For more information please view the full job description here.

 

This role is being offered on a full-time 12 month contract, working on a seven-day roster with early starts or late finishes, including one weekend day each week. This role is open to candidates in both 
Sydney and Melbourne.

GNM Australia Limited (Guardian Australia) is proud to be a fair and ethical employer. Australian editorial minimum rates of pay by band and grade are outlined in the Journalists (GNM Australia Pty Ltd) Enterprise Agreement 2024 for roles that fall under its coverage.

Annually, we host more than 160 million guests, promote more than 10,000 shows and present more than 22,000 events around the world. We are committed to innovation, artistry, and community, and leverage the power of our 300+ venues, leading sports franchises, marquee music brands, integrated entertainment districts, premier ticketing platform and global sponsorship activations, to create memorable moments that give the world reason to cheer.

Our business is interwoven with the human mind and heart, and we strive to build a diverse and inclusive company that reflects the artists, athletes, and fans that we host; reach beyond traditional boundaries to support the communities in which we operate; and minimize our impact on the environment by adopting sustainable practices throughout our business operations.

Job Summary

The Assistant General Manager is responsible for overseeing venue events and shows. Responsibilities include hiring and scheduling staff, monitoring venue maintenance and security, and managing onsite operations at each event. The Assistant General Manager will also oversee guest relations, customer experience, and assist the General Manager and Venue Manager with projects and duties as needed.

Essential Functions

  • Manage venue events and shows, ticketing, advance show needs (concerts and special events), show settlement; coordinate technical aspects including lighting, video and sound; parking and sponsorship.
  • Analyze event calendar and determine appropriate staffing levels. Create and maintain schedules based on part time employee availability and event schedule. Approve hours worked and time off requests for part time staff.
  • Oversee venue maintenance and security. Check for maintenance issues, project planning and coordinate with maintenance staff for resolution. Attend and direct security meetings during preshow and during the event, monitor staff levels, communicate with head of security on overall operations and troubleshoot security issues.
  • Manage day to day office operations. Oversee the ordering of supplies for both office and venue; monitor the maintenance of customer service email and holding of comp tickets for VIP guests.
  • Oversee guest relations and ensure customers have the best experience possible. Respond to escalated guest complaints and inquiries resolving in a timely manner.
  • Make recommendations to the General Manager on allocation of departmental budget, monthly reforecasting and reconciling of monthly financial statements.
  • Oversee all operations and make decisions in General Managers’ absence.

Required Qualifications

  • 6-8 years Of related work experience
  • Knowledge of accounting principles
  • Computer savvy and proficient in MS Word, Excel, and Outlook
  • Previous production experience, including scheduling, managing staff, and payroll

These businesses allow Live Nation Media & Sponsorship to create strategic music marketing programs that connect more than 1,200 sponsors with the 145 million fans that attend Live Nation Entertainment events each year. For additional information, visit www.livenationentertainment.com.

WHO ARE YOU?

Internship Summary:

The role involves administrative support based in the Live Nation Toronto office, production support at events across our owned and operated venues in Toronto, as well as at any partner-led proprietary events. You will also contribute to the efforts of Live Nation Canada’s sales & strategy team inclusive of our digital integration efforts. job.title: Client and Event Support Manager
job.description:
Job Summary:

JOB DESCRIPTION - CLIENT & EVENT SUPPORT MANAGER


Location: Brussels

Division: Global Support & Operations

Line Manager: Regional Operations Director

Contract Terms: Permanent, Full-Time 37.5 hours per week


THE TEAM


Global Support & Operations Organization has the mission to build a global support & operations center of excellence where all processes, tools & best practices are applied to all regions across the globe in order to achieve the highest levels of employee, fan & Client satisfaction.

EMEA Support & Operations team, a vertical of this organization, is accountable for supporting Clients in markets located under the EMEA Region (Europe, Middle East and Africa) and providing the ticketing service to the full life-cycle of their events (from onsale to entry).

Our Clients demand and value high service levels and we believe our people are the foundation to deliver great service. We are fortunate to have the most experienced and skilled operations experts on the field around the globe, regionally and locally, that have a deep understanding of our Clients’ needs. We then apply our own ticketing technology to help our Clients innovate in their offering and ticketing strategies.


THE JOB


As Client and Event Support Manager, you will lead and develop the Client and Event Support team in Belgium. You will be accountable for accurate, timely event programming across Ticketmaster’s Belgian client base and effective, proactive operational support for assigned top-tier clients. You will set clear priorities, plan team capacity and maintain agreed quality standards and service levels throughout the event lifecycle.


The role combines people leadership with practical operational involvement. You will coach the team, improve workflows and provide hands-on support for complex deliveries, peak periods and escalations. You will develop the team’s knowledge and judgement so that colleagues can manage their responsibilities confidently and resolve issues independently, involving specialists where needed.


You will help the team build trusted client relationships, anticipate requirements and support the adoption of relevant Ticketmaster tools and features. Working with Client Development and specialist teams, you will contribute to client retention and growth through reliable service, effective product use and practical improvements to clients’ ticketing operations.


WHAT YOU WILL BE DOING


Leadership and people development


  • Lead, coach and develop the Client and Event Support team, setting clear expectations for delivery, client service and collaboration.
  • Hold regular one-to-ones, provide constructive feedback and address performance concerns promptly. Agree development plans that build individual skills and support career progression.
  • Build team capability by facilitating training, knowledge sharing and cross-training, and by delegating work appropriately. Ensure sufficient expertise and cover across key responsibilities.

Event programming and service delivery


  • Oversee event programming across the Belgian client base, ensuring event setups and changes meet approved requirements, quality standards and agreed Event Management service levels.
  • Plan capacity, allocate work and maintain coverage for on-sales, event peaks and ongoing client support. Resolve competing priorities and escalate resource constraints or delivery risks early.
  • Maintain quality assurance and peer-review processes, ensure agreed procedures are followed and address the causes of programming errors and recurring delivery issues.
  • Provide hands-on operational support for complex deliveries, peak periods and escalations, while maintaining oversight of team priorities and performance.
  • Ensure event and support records in Salesforce are accurate and current, with clear ownership, status and next steps.

Client support and success


  • Build relationships with key contacts at assigned top-tier clients and ensure the team maintains regular dialogue and forward planning around their event calendars, priorities and service needs.
  • Act as the primary management escalation point for complex or high-impact client and event issues. Coordinate the response, involve relevant specialists and ensure clear ownership, timely communication and follow-through to resolution.
  • Oversee client onboarding, practical training and adoption of relevant Ticketmaster tools and features. Ensure the team follows up on difficulties and helps clients work confidently and independently.
  • Share client feedback, service risks and improvement opportunities with Client Development to support retention and growth. Coordinate agreed operational actions, while Client Development retains ownership of commercial agreements.

Process improvement and cross-functional coordination


  • Develop and maintain effective market-level workflows for Client Support and Event Management, adapting them to Belgian client needs while aligning with regional and global standards.
  • Monitor event accuracy, delivery timeliness, support responsiveness and resolution, recurring issues, client feedback and tool adoption. Use these measures to prioritise improvements, agree corrective actions and review their effectiveness.
  • Work with Client Development, Product Operations, Field Operations, Finance and Fan Support to coordinate service, clarify responsibilities and resolve issues that require input from multiple teams.
  • Represent Belgium in regional forums, sharing client needs, operational insights and successful practices. Coordinate local implementation of agreed product and process changes, ensuring procedures and team training remain current.

WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW


Languages: The ability to communicate effectively in at least one local language (French and/or Dutch) is required, in addition to fluency in English.


  • Proven experience leading and developing teams, ideally within operations, client services or event management, including setting expectations, coaching colleagues and managing performance.
  • Strong understanding of ticketing platforms, event configuration and client support processes, with the ability to guide others, assess operational risks and support complex issue resolution.
  • Experience planning workloads, managing capacity and prioritising competing requests in an environment with time-critical delivery and changing demands.
  • The ability to design effective workflows, interpret performance data and lead practical improvements to quality, efficiency and service.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the judgement to manage client escalations, explain operational decisions and coordinate colleagues across different functions.
  • Confidence using business systems, CRM platforms and Microsoft Office, particularly Excel. Experience with Ticketmaster platforms, TM1 tools and Salesforce is an advantage.
  • An understanding of live entertainment or sports operations, and flexibility to support occasional evenings, weekends, holidays and on-site activity as required and agreed.

YOU


  • You give clear direction, make considered decisions and hold yourself and others accountable for commitments.
  • You develop people through practical coaching, constructive feedback and delegation, creating an environment where colleagues ask questions and raise concerns early.

JOB DESCRIPTION - CLIENT SUPPORT SPECIALIST


Location: Brussels

Division: Global Support & Operations

Line Manager: Client and Event Support Manager

Contract Terms: Permanent, Full-Time 37.5 hours per week


THE TEAM


Global Support & Operations Organization has the mission to build a global support & operations center of excellence where all processes, tools & best practices are applied to all regions across the globe in order to achieve the highest levels of employee, fan & Client satisfaction.

EMEA Support & Operations team, a vertical of this organization, is accountable for supporting Clients in markets located under the EMEA Region (Europe, Middle East and Africa) and providing the ticketing service to the full life-cycle of their events (from onsale to entry).

Our Clients demand and value high service levels and we believe our people are the foundation to deliver great service. We are fortunate to have the most experienced and skilled operations experts on the field around the globe, regionally and locally, that have a deep understanding of our Clients’ needs. We then apply our own ticketing technology to help our Clients innovate in their offering and ticketing strategies.


THE JOB


As a Client and Event Support Specialist, you will deliver event programming across Ticketmaster’s full client base in Belgium and act as the day-to-day operational contact for assigned top-tier clients. For assigned top-tier clients, you will build a detailed understanding of their events, priorities and ways of working, using that knowledge to provide proactive guidance and ongoing support. You will help clients plan ahead, adopt relevant Ticketmaster tools and features, and improve their ticketing operations over time. You will coordinate the resolution of ticketing issues and keep clients informed throughout the event lifecycle.

Event programming and delivery


  • Build and maintain events in the ticketing platforms used in Belgium, following agreed procedures, quality standards and Event Management service levels.
  • Collect and review event submissions; clarify missing or conflicting information and translate approved requirements into accurate event setups, including dates, pricing, inventory, sales channels and on-sale timings.

Anticipate requirements, identify recurring challenges and coordinate practical improvements with clients and relevant teams.

  • Work with Client Development, Product Operations, Field Operations, Finance and Fan Support to provide coordinated service. Share client needs and improvement opportunities with Client Development, which retains ownership of commercial agreements.
  • Coordinate specialist help for access control, box office, hardware or reporting issues. Support events on site or outside normal hours as required and agreed.

Strong attention to detail, accurate data entry and a structured approach to quality assurance, documentation and standard operating procedures.

job.description:

Discover your purpose. Embrace innovation. Experience #LifeatRealChem.

Job Summary:

Real Chemistry is looking for a Senior Account Manager to join our growing team!

 

As a Senior Account Manager, you will act as the key day-to-day client contact, managing relationships and taking responsibility for the delivery of several medium to large projects. As a client account lead or captain (depending on the size of the account), you will be responsible for managing the execution of parallel ongoing projects and take an active role in coaching your junior team and ensuring projects are delivered effectively alongside the account lead and/or sponsor.

 

You should have a clear understanding of the programme as a whole (not just the projects you are working on) across your accounts, increasing your involvement in the strategic planning and financial management of your accounts and focusing on developing your leadership style to actively manage up and down, based on project needs.

 

 

What you’ll do:

Client delivery

  • Act as day-to-day client contact: provide regular status updates to your client (leading updates on more complex projects); anticipate client needs; respond to client queries and share recommendations (following discussion with your account lead); manage client expectations on timelines, scope of project, etc.; take client briefs and clearly communicate to team members, implementing realistic project plans

  • Confidently formulate objectives and strategies for new client work with support from your account lead, ensuring that programme strategy is pulled through

  • Lead large projects with less support from your account lead, being accountable for the whole project from start to finish

  • Provide counsel to the client throughout the project with confidence to challenge the client when required; manage challenging conversations with the client, as required

  • Provide support to your account lead in addressing programme and team challenges

  • Formulate solutions to client challenges such as last-minute requests

  • Have a clear understanding of the programme as a whole (not just the projects you are working on), including the client objectives, strategy and environment so that you are able to confidently lead internal meetings and client calls

  • Ensure momentum is maintained across the programme and contact with client continues whenever the account lead is absent

 

Business development

  • Identify areas for organic growth within existing accounts (evolving existing programmes and/or additional tactics) and confidently sell new ideas in to clients, with support from your account lead

  • Play a management role in the new business process (assisting in the production of credentials and pitch presentations, coordinating and managing team members and external suppliers), having a significant share of voice/visibility with the internal cross-functional team

 

Team management

  • Begin to develop your leadership style, instilling professional values and good working habits in your teams

  • Look for opportunities to inspire, motivate, and empower your team on a daily basis, leading by example and setting the standard for junior accounts team members

  • Provide coaching and mentoring to junior team members and manage their performance

  • Support interviewing for new AAs – SAAs

  • Line manage at least one accounts team member AAs – SAAs, providing day-to-day support and longer-term career development guidance

 

Financial management

  • Develop more complicated budgets for integrated client programmes and track resource use against available budget throughout the month

  • Coach others to develop accurate budgets for clients, reflecting back on previous projects and gathering cost quotes

  • Support your account lead with the financial management of your accounts, proactively getting involved in invoicing, forecasting and resourcing and attend month-end finance meetings

  • Complete your timesheets and expense claims accurately and on time and take an active role in reviewing timesheets across the majority of your projects

 

Agency environment

  • Participate in internal initiatives which contribute to the culture or development of the Medical Communications team, or Real Chemistry more broadly (e.g., compliance/socials/inspiration)

  • Keep abreast of award-winning work and insights from other industries, sharing as appropriate

 

 

This position is a perfect fit for you if:

  • ​Our Company values – Best Together, Impact-Obsessed, Excellence Expected, Evolve Always and Accountability with an “I” – really speak to you.

  • You are adaptable, resilient, and OK with adjusting your scope, responsibilities, and focus as we grow. When things change, so do we. We’re always evolving.

  • You are proactive, driven, and resourceful with strong prioritization skills and a desire to dive into the data.

  • You are highly organized self-starter, able to work independently and under tight deadlines.

 

 

What you should have:

  • Relevant degree in a scientific subject

  • Excellent business communication skills, including informal/formal presentation and writing skills

  • Excellent business communication skills

  • Informal/formal presentation and writing skills; including presenting to clients

  • Skilled in data communication

  • Experience with Microsoft Office tools (PowerPoint, Word, and Excel).

  • Edit junior staff writing and presentation material

  • Must have Medical Education experience; integrated experience preferred.

  • Skilled in data communication and able to develop final documents and presentations

  • Able to develop solutions to client needs and problems, with a strong work ethic and a track record of high-quality deliverables on schedule and on budget

  • Experience coaching and mentoring junior team members

  • High energy, able to effectively operate in a fast-paced, growing and evolving environment

job.title: Accounts Payable Assistant
job.description:
Opportunity

Brunswick is seeking an Accounts Payable Assistant to join our Finance team. Working across a complex, international and fast-paced business, you’ll play an important role in ensuring our financial operations run seamlessly, taking ownership of everything from invoices and payments to expenses, supplier relationships and day-to-day queries.

This role combines accuracy and pace with a genuinely people-focused approach. You’ll have the opportunity to build trusted relationships with colleagues across the firm and contribute beyond the core AP process through wider projects and analysis.

We’re looking for someone who takes pride in delivering work to a high standard, demonstrates sound judgement and attention to detail, and enjoys being part of a collaborative team where professionalism, responsiveness and strong relationships matter.

About the Role

Your main responsibilities will include:

  • Ensuring invoices are processed accurately and on time, with a minimum of 30 invoices posted per day
  • Responding to AP mailbox queries within 24 hours
  • Reviewing and posting pending items daily, ensuring they are cleared within 48 hours
  • Preparing BACS payments every two weeks
  • Managing, reviewing and posting staff expense claims
  • Setting up and verifying supplier and staff bank details in line with company policy
  • Uploading batch journals
  • Reconciling supplier statements
  • Preparing and setting up ad hoc payments in the bank on a weekly basis
  • Responding to ad hoc queries and carrying out analysis as required
  • Supporting and reviewing the apprentice’s workload and development

 

What We’re Looking For

Standout candidates will demonstrate:

  • Accounts Payable processing experience, ideally within a multi-currency, multi-entity environment
  • A minimum of 12 months’ experience working within a finance team
  • A highly personable and collaborative business partner who can build strong relationships with colleagues and stakeholders
  • Strong numerical skills and excellent attention to detail

 

Why Join Us

Whether you are joining a client facing team, a core services team, or starting out on your professional career journey, joining Brunswick unlocks a range of employee benefits to support your financial future, health and wellness, family and community and continuous professional development.

 

About Brunswick

Brunswick is a global advisory firm. We help companies tackle high-stakes issues, navigate complex stakeholder relationships, and deliver high-impact outcomes. 

Our clients value our ability to anticipate, shape, and respond to the key players and forces in the financial and investment arena, regulatory and geopolitical universe, NGO community, workforce and beyond. They rely on us for deep experience, fresh perspectives and original thinking. So, in Brunswick you will find an exceptional range of experience and talent with a rich mix of backgrounds. From the beginning, we have prioritized attracting, developing, and retaining the best professionals in the industry, united by a culture of inclusivity, excellence, and intellectual curiosity.

job.title: KSL HR Business Partner
job.description:
Our company is committed to being trusted voices of light and truth reaching hundreds of millions of people worldwide.

Who We Are

KSL is Utah’s leading local news source across digital and broadcast platforms, delivering trusted, award‑winning journalism through KSL.com and KSL‑TV. We provide in‑depth local reporting, investigative journalism, and up‑to‑the‑minute coverage that serves communities across the state. Committed to being a trusted voice of light and knowledge, KSL helps Utahns stay informed, connected, and engaged with the issues that matter most.

 

POSITION OVERVIEW 

 

The HR Business Partner supports the people who bring KSL’s mission to life. Working with employees, managers, and the broader HR team, you will provide practical guidance on employee relations, performance management, employee development, and day-to-day HR needs across our multiplatform media operation. 

 

Note: Work configurations are subject to change based on business needs and at company discretion.  

  • This position is a majority onsite role that requires the employee to work at our Salt Lake City site. Specific schedule will be determined based on business needs and evaluated by manager and senior management.  

 

What You Will Do: 

 

Primary job duties will include, but are not limited to:  

  • Build strong working relationships with employees and leaders across KSL’s business units. 
  • Learn departmental priorities and recommend people practices that support business needs and the employee experience. 
  • Serve as an approachable, responsive resource for employee questions and workplace concerns. 
  • Support performance review processes, onboarding, engagement initiatives, retention efforts, and organizational changes. 
  • Review workforce metrics such as turnover, retention, engagement, and employee relations trends. 
  • Use data alongside employee feedback and business context to recommend practical improvements. 
  • Help managers communicate expectations, deliver constructive feedback, and support employee development. 
  • Partner with recruiting, benefits, payroll, and other HR colleagues to provide coordinated employee support. 
  • Assess employee relations issues, gather relevant information, and recommend timely, fair, and consistent responses. 
  • Proactively support a workplace free from harassment, discrimination, and retaliation, including at offsite business activities and company-sponsored events. 
  • Actively support company EEO policies across recruitment, selection, evaluation, compensation, training, promotion, and termination. 
  • Support applicable employment-law requirements and broadcast-related EEO processes, including FCC EEO compliance, in partnership with HR leadership. 
  • Maintain accurate HR records and employee relations documentation. 
  • Handle sensitive employee and business information responsibly and otherwise conduct yourself in compliance with company policy and professional standards. 

 

 

Skills and Experience We Are Looking For: 

 

  • 1-2 years of experience in an HR Business Partner role 
  • Hands-on employee relations experience, demonstrating sound judgment in gathering information and making recommendations.  
  • Excellent interpersonal communication skills through active listening, clear guidance, and dependable follow-through 
  • Ability to understand and apply HR data and analytics in practical ways 
  • Proficiency with Excel or comparable spreadsheet tools and experience using an HR information system. 
  • Foundational knowledge of employment laws, HR practices, and workplace policies. 
  • Strong judgment, attention to detail, organizational skills, and the ability to manage competing priorities. 
  • Ability to work independently within your experience level while seeking guidance and escalating matters appropriately. 
  • Ability to work onsite in Salt Lake City for the majority of the workweek. 

 

Physical Demands

- Receive, process, and maintain information through oral and/or written communication effectively.

- Manual dexterity and fine motor skills to operate computer keys and general office equipment. Ability to work on a computer for prolonged periods of time.

- Sit and/or stand for extended periods of time.

- Lift, move, and carry up to 25 pounds on occasion.

 

Compensation

Salary rate to be determined by multiple factors including but not limited to evaluation of the education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities of the applicant along with internal equity and alignment with market data.

Employees at KSL can enjoy a broad offering of benefits, including:

  • Robust, affordable medical, dental and vision coverage with no wait period for enrollment
  • Paid leave for new parents under our Medical Maternity and Parental Leave policies
  • Opportunities to apply for tuition reimbursement
  • Paid time off for vacation and sick leave in addition to paid company holidays

  • Matches on contributions to charitable organizations after one year of service
  • Continuous growth and development opportunities
  • Dynamic team culture that values teamwork, having fun, and collaboration

 

KSL is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other characteristic protected by law. Your role

As Canada’s national public broadcaster, CBC/Radio-Canada is committed to reflecting Canada’s diversity in its workforce, as well as across all of its platforms. 


CBC Saskatchewan is looking for a creative, innovative, collaborative and independent-thinking journalist/producer for a unique role as associate producer for the content diversification and creator network unit. This is a full-time, permanent position based in Regina or Saskatoon (open to candidates in either location)


This position is different from any other in Saskatchewan’s newsroom. Reporting to a senior producer, you will work with independent video creators, producing strong original stories that will find audiences on multiple emerging platforms. This work will push the boundaries of our storytelling, focusing on new, diverse perspectives and experiences, told in innovative ways with the goal to draw in new audiences. While the majority of your time will be spent working with and developing video storytelling projects with emerging creators, your job will also include bringing those stories to the audience, on multiple emerging platforms, to reach the audience where they are. From pitch to publication, you’ll strive to find homes for these diverse perspectives and stories at CBC Saskatchewan and across CBC, while fostering a community of creators and continuing to build this network.


Your strengths are both in imaginative storytelling and developing relationships with potential freelance creators, sources and audience members to develop projects that are firmly rooted in this community but that are also surprising to our audience. You are able to encourage and build momentum with emerging storytellers, bringing in their unique perspectives, while communicating the need to balance this with journalistically rigorous storytelling. 


Strong journalism, storytelling and relationship-building skills are needed, as well as an ability to write and edit. Video skills are an asset, but an interest in learning new ways of video storytelling is more important, alongside a genuine interest in exploring digital storytelling tools. 


An interest in mentoring and interacting with those outside the CBC is key, as well as a strong ability to communicate and share your work internally. An independent-thinker who can juggle multiple projects on multiple timelines is essential. Knowledge of contracting and rights issues is an asset.


As the primary associate producer for this unit in Saskatchewan, you will also  pitch original ideas that connect with the community, seek diverse perspectives and new creators as well as innovative treatments that help stories resonate with new audiences. You will work collaboratively with a small team based in Alberta, Saskatchewan and Manitoba. You will assist in developing digital content including researching, writing, editing, organizing shoots and reviewing freelancer work as needed. You will balance your work managing creator’s projects with content diversification or first person stories, on different deadlines. Work must adhere to CBC journalistic and/or show policies, practices and standards, but initiative and independent judgment are required.


Key Tasks include:

  • Seek out, connect and build relationships with emerging independent creators and talent from diverse and digital communities, mentor and guide them from pitch to publication and create a sense of belonging for them within the CBC.
  • Throughout the process, provide creative feedback and notes while communicating CBC’s journalistic principles and business and rights practices, ensuring that bar is met before publication.
  • Assist in developing content including idea generating, chasing of voices, writing, researching, editing, preparing questioning, setting up shoots, fact-checking, developing the writing or ideas of others
  • Assist in packaging Creator Network stories for multiple platforms as they evolve, including writing web articles, radio and tv scripts, YouTube titles and thumbnails, and producing social media content, as well as managing internal communications around publication. 
  • Contribute ideas for content and suggestions for treatment of original, compelling, diverse and people-focussed content diversification stories in Saskatchewan.
  • Potential to gather audio-visual material including interviews, video and photographs to enhance digital, print, and social media platforms as required. 
  • Potential to plan and execute community outreach events or other engagement-focused happenings that enhance the creator community and CBC’s role in it, or that generally address gaps in our coverage. This could include hosting screenings, workshops, meet-and-greets, speaking at journalism and film schools/ programs, and representing CBC at local film events and festivals. 
  • Develop and maintain contacts in a range of diverse communities around the region.  
  • Manage multiple projects on different timelines.
  • Communicate and collaborate effectively across multiple departments and outside CBC.
  • Act as a CBC ambassador in Saskatchewan’s production and creative communities.
  • Adhere to the Journalistic Standards and Practices of the CBC, some familiarity with media agreements, Business & Rights, budgets.

We are looking for a candidate with the following: 

  • University degree or equivalent
  • Five years’ practical and relevant experience, including some experience with collaborating in creative partnerships and content production
  • An understanding of local journalism, and the tools needed to produce it
  • A deep understanding of how to work with creatives from all walks of life, effectively communicating journalism, business and rights and other storytelling needs, while collaborating on unique, diverse, surprising and creative finished products
  • A strong sense of journalistic storytelling with an awareness of contemporary political, economic, cultural and social issues of importance to  this community, paired with a good understanding of the needs of a diverse Saskatchewan audience
  • A deep understanding and appreciation of diversity of perspective, opinion and experience and the ability to tell stories  from those perspectives – whatever that looks like.  
  • Must have strong creative judgement, initiative and a high degree of responsibility for the quality of work throughout the complete production cycle as well as publication, as well as the ability to provide imaginative and effective solutions, suggestions and feedback.
  • Excellent interpersonal and organizational skills, along with the ability to work under tight deadlines with multiple priorities interacting with different teams across the organization.
  • Strong critical thinking skills (familiarity with CBC’s Journalistic Standards and Practices is essential).
  • Excellent writing, editing, video producing and other digital storytelling skills
  • Able to keep track of a number of simultaneous activities and projects and prioritize and plan, and to keep enthusiasm and momentum going on projects that can take months and evolve over time.
  • Ability to generate, pitch and pursue strong, creative and original people-focussed story ideas and treatments with the goal of reaching new audience
  • Ability to seek out new voices and freelancers and develop relationships with audience members and potential collaborators
  • Knowledge of the digital space and trends as well as social media
  • A demonstrated connection to diverse communities within the Saskatchewan area as well as a commitment to producing journalism for audiences that are often underserved and/or underrepresented.
  • Excellent communication, interpersonal and outreach skills, along with the ability to work under tight deadlines with multiple priorities interacting with different teams across the organization.

Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. We make connections between media content, systems, people and places. We are the space in between.

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada but around the world. The Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) AI Lab at CBC/Radio-Canada operates as an agile, high-performance innovation hub. Our mission is to prototype, experiment with and deploy artificial intelligence solutions for media production systems across the organization. We design customized functionalities and seamlessly integrate advanced AI technologies into our existing product ecosystem.

We are looking for an AI Analyst who is pragmatic, curious, ambitious and ready to kick-start their career in applied AI. Backed by senior experts, you will work in a highly experimental environment where your initiatives will have real, immediate impact.

Our team is supported on a day-to-day basis by next-generation coding assistants like Cursor and Claude to optimize ideation, development, debugging and documentation. Behind the scenes, but ahead of the curve: help us develop the next-generation public service media organization.

 

Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation’s technology and infrastructure. We are the people that make stuff work. We make connections between media content, systems, people and places. We are the space in between.

 

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada but around the world. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force, and we are the team making it happen.

 

This is a hybrid position with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

 

Your Role


We are looking for highly skilled and organized Enterprise Architect with deep subject matter expertise in media systems Architecture for one of our downtown Toronto, Ottawa or Montreal Office locations.

 

Reporting to the Director of Media Systems Architecture, you will be responsible for establishing an unified technological vision by understanding media production processes and translating business requirements into technical solutions that deliver business value.

 

As part of the Architecture and Strategic Development (ASD) Department you will leave your mark by driving the shift from hardware-centric infrastructure to software-centric media production architecture.

 

You will enjoy innovative work in a creative and dynamic work environment, working with leading technologies and opportunities for continued professional development.  

 

How will you make an impact?

 

As an Enterprise Architect, you will:

  • Define and promote a common vision of Enterprise Architecture and establish clear direction on roles, responsibilities and priorities with stakeholders.
  • Lead the evolution of the Enterprise Architecture practice and drive the shift from hardware-centric infrastructure to software-centric media production architecture.
  • Define the strategy to connect Production systems with data governance,risk management, information security to monitor its implementation and effectiveness.
  • Participate in designing, documenting and communicating the current and target state architectures for major initiatives and other vendor-driven system replacements.
  • Document the High Level Architecture that outlines the structure, components, and relationships between business processes, data, applications and technology infrastructure.
  • Ensure that enterprise investments align with business goals and objectives.
  • Ensure that architectural decisions align with organizational policies, industry best practices and regulatory requirements.
  • Help establish and enforce architecture governance processes and standards.
  • Drive innovation by identifying emerging technologies and evaluating their potential for the organization.
  • Coach and mentor other architects, product owners/managers and business stakeholders to instill architectural thinking.
  • Build and maintain relationships with business and technology stakeholders.

 

Perks you can look forward to:

  • Four weeks of vacation per year.
  • Work from home opportunities.
  • Competitive total rewards package.
  • Opportunities to work with cutting edge technology.
  • Opportunities for continued learning and professional development - including access to e-learning services, customized courses and certification opportunities.
  • Opportunities to become a member of our Employee Resource Groups.
  • A creative and dynamic work environment, where your ideas and contributions can be heard, valued and respected.
  • A supportive management team committed to upholding the highest standards of diversity and inclusivity.

 

What you bring to our team

 

Minimum Requirements

  • Minimum Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, or computer science,Professional Engineer a definite asset.
  • Five or more years of enterprise or systems architecture and/or business experience in strategic and operations planning.
  • Ten or more years of experience in solution or technical architecture and application development
  • Knowledge of production systems ecosystems such as Playout, editing systems, Cloud Platforms, On-prem and hybrid solutions.
  • Understanding of business models, operating models, financial models, cost-benefit analysis, budgeting and risk management.
  • Familiarity with enterprise architecture tools, related graphical models and frameworks.
  • Understanding of various operating models such as project-centric and product-centric.

Company Overview

Cumulus Media is an audio-first media company delivering premium content to a quarter billion people every month — wherever and whenever they want it. Cumulus Media engages listeners with high-quality local programming through 377 owned-and-operated radio stations across 84 markets; delivers nationally-syndicated sports, news, talk, and entertainment programming from iconic brands including the NFL, the NCAA, the Masters, US Soccer, and AP News, across more than 7,800 affiliated stations through Westwood One, a leading national audio network; and inspires listeners through the Cumulus Podcast Network, an established and influential platform for original podcasts that are smart, entertaining, and thought-provoking. Cumulus Media provides advertisers with personal connections, local impact and national reach through broadcast and on-demand digital, mobile, social, and voice-activated platforms, as well as integrated digital marketing services, powerful influencers, full-service audio solutions, industry-leading research and insights, and live event experiences. For more information visit www.cumulusmedia.com.


Position Overview

CUMULUS MEDIA | Dallas is offering a great opportunity for a  Full-Time Chief Technical Board Operator/Producer for WBAP and KLIF. Our ideal candidate should possess an extremely good work ethic, is a self-starter, reliable, and highly organized with the ability to work in a fast-paced office environment and be able to work closely with the program director to execute programming and be accessible to the sales department if needed. 


Key Responsibilities & Qualifications

Key Responsibilities:

 

  • Running the broadcast console in the radio control room with the purpose of putting content on the air seamlessly and ensuring all Station Policies and Procedures are followed and all FCC requirements are met on a daily basis. 
  • Ensuring that all commercial materials air as logged 
  • Audio editing, station or show production. 
  • Producing Mid-day and afternoon show on WBAP. 
  • Podcasting and station social media management 
  • Filling in on other shifts from time to time as needed
  • Help in supervising board operators. 

Qualifications:

  • 1-3 years radio experience either at the college or smaller market level 
  • Candidates must have a knowledge of news and know the hit stories of the day. 
  • Have a good understanding of all equipment in a radio control room including but not limited to the broadcast console and related digital audio systems, call screening, Vox Pro, EAS Systems, broadcast delay, and any remote delivery equipment 
  • Must be able to think quickly and make good decisions in a high pressure, fast paced environment 
  • Must be able to get along with and work closely with other employees 
  • Excellent communication skills are a must,  including writing and grammar 
  • Candidates must be reliable, responsible, and punctual and must be able to work weekends, weekend nights, overnights and holidays if needed

  • Competitive Pay

  • Paid Vacation, Sick & Holiday time off
  • Parental leave time off benefits, life insurance, disability insurance, wellness, and an employee referral bonus program

Part-Time On-Air Talent / Brand Ambassador

Are you passionate about connecting with people? Are you ready to get behind the mic and out into the community? Let's talk!

Midwest Communications, Inc is looking for energetic and confident individual to join our Fargo team as Part-Time On-Air Talent & Brand Ambassadors across three of the area's favorite radio brands: Y94 (Top 40), 101.9 Jack FM (Adult Hits), and Froggy 99.9 (Country).

This is your chance to do more than just talk on the radio. You'll connect with listeners, bring our brands to life at community events, and help create the experiences that keep people listening. We develop winners- many of our part-time on-air personalities have built successful careers right here within our stations.

job.title: Broadcast & Media Technology Project Manager
job.description:
OVERVIEW OF THE COMPANY

Fox News Media

FOX News Media operates the FOX News Channel (FNC), FOX Business Network (FBN), FOX News Digital, FOX News Audio, FOX News Books, the direct-to-consumer digital streaming services FOX Nation and FOX News International and the newly announced platform FOX Weather. Currently the number one network in all of cable, FNC has also been the most watched television news channel for 20 consecutive years, while FBN currently ranks among the top business channels on cable. Owned by FOX Corporation, FOX News Media reaches 200 million people each month.

JOB DESCRIPTION

FOX News Media is seeking an experienced Broadcast & Media Technology Project Manager to lead complex technology initiatives across studio operations, live broadcast production, contribution/transmission networks, Media Asset Management (MAM) pipelines, and fast-turnaround content creation/editing environments.

 

This role will manage projects from initial discovery and technical requirements gathering through solution delivery, systems integration, testing, commissioning, and transition to 24/7 broadcast operations. The successful candidate will collaborate closely across broadcast engineering, studio operations, control rooms, post-production, editorial, transmission, infrastructure, cybersecurity, and external systems integrators/vendors.

 

The ideal candidate combines disciplined project management practices with a strong technical understanding of how broadcast content moves from field capture/ingest through studio control rooms, non-linear editing (NLE) suites, central MAM repositories, master control/playout, and multi-path transmission.

 

A SNAPSHOT OF YOUR RESPONSIBILITES

Project Delivery and Governance

  • Lead the full project lifecycle, including discovery, scoping, technical design coordination, procurement, installation, integration, testing, commissioning, cutover, hypercare, and operational handover.
  • Develop and maintain integrated project plans covering work breakdown structures, milestones, critical paths, dependencies, hardware/software lead times, risks, issues, and capital/operating budgets.
  • Establish governance routines, engineering working sessions, steering committee reporting, and change-control decision forums.
  • Coordinate workstreams across broadcast engineering, studio tech, transmission/traffic, newsroom operations, editing/post-production, IT infrastructure, and third-party vendors/systems integrators.
  • Track delivery against broadcast milestones, schedule, budget, quality standards, and operational-readiness criteria.
  • Maintain rigorous project documentation, including functional specs, system schematics coordination, rack elevations, acceptance test plans (ATP), cutover runbooks, and handover documentation.

Broadcast & Media Technology Delivery

  • Lead initiatives involving production switchers, audio consoles, studio cameras, robotics, multi-viewers, tally/intercom systems (e.g., Riedel, RTS), broadcast graphics (e.g., Vizrt), and virtual/augmented reality studio tech.
  • Oversee deployments for field acquisition, bonded cellular (e.g., LiveU, Dejero), satellite/fiber contribution, IP contribution protocols (SRT, RIST, Zixi), and baseband/IP ingest pipelines.
  • Manage MAM implementations, metadata schema standardization, ingest automation, nearline/deep archive tiers, LTO/cloud storage lifecycles, and media supply chain orchestration.
  • Drive technical delivery for non-linear editing (NLE) platforms (Adobe Premiere, Avid Media Composer), shared production storage (SAN/NAS/Isilon/Avid NEXIS), fast-turnaround news editing, and transcode/QC workflows.
  • Coordinate projects for playout automation, routing matrices (SDI and IP), primary/backup transmission paths, satellite uplink/downlink, terrestrial fiber circuits, and disaster recovery (DR) facilities.
  • Facilitate technical integration between newsroom systems (e.g., iNEWS, ENPS), rundown automation, prompters, and playback servers.
  • Translate operational and editorial requirements into clear engineering workstreams and technical deliverables.
  • Support infrastructure modernization and technology refreshes, such as SDI-to-ST 2110 IP transitions, cloud-assisted production, and hybrid on-prem/cloud workflows.
  • Coordinate technical design reviews alongside Principal Engineers, Systems Architects, and Technical Leads.

Live Operations, Commissioning & Deployment Readiness

  • Plan and direct factory acceptance testing (FAT), site acceptance testing (SAT), end-to-end rehearsal workflows, operational shadow periods, cutovers, and rollback strategies.
  • Schedule and oversee maintenance windows and deployment sequencing to ensure zero disruption to on-air linear feeds and 24/7 live studio operations.
  • Partner with Broadcast Operations and Engineering teams to establish support escalation models, monitoring/telemetry dashboards, signal path redundancies, runbooks, and SOPs.
  • Coordinate comprehensive operational training and knowledge transfer for operators, directors, editors, engineers, and technicians prior to on-air cutover.

Technology Modernization & Continuous Improvement

  • Partner with engineering leads to evaluate emerging broadcast standards (SMPTE ST 2110, NMOS, NDI) and cloud/virtualized production platforms.
  • Identify workflow bottlenecks in the content creation and turnaround pipeline, introducing automation for ingest, transcode, QC, and archiving.
  • Promote standard operating procedures and best-practice deployment frameworks across all broadcast and studio facilities.

WHAT YOU WILL NEED

  • Bachelor’s degree in Broadcast Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Media Technology, Computer Science, or equivalent practical industry experience.
  • Technology project management experience, with experience directly managing broadcast engineering, studio facility, transmission, or media production technology projects.
  • Proven track record leading projects through technical scoping, RFP/vendor evaluation, rack/facility buildout, systems integration, commissioning, and on-air cutover.
  • Demonstrated working knowledge across core broadcast domains, including:
    • Studio production, PCR/TCR control rooms, routing, and intercom systems.
    • Live contribution (SRT, RIST, ASI, Satellite, Fiber) and transmission pipelines.
    • MAM systems, automated transcode engines, and shared editing storage (SAN/NAS).
    • Post-production and NLE workflows (Avid, Adobe, automated QC).
    • Newsroom Computer Systems (NRCS) and broadcast automation/playout.
  • Solid grasp of broadcast video/audio signals and protocols (Baseband SDI, SMPTE ST 2110, AES67, Dante, PTP timing, MPEG-TS).
  • Experience coordinating structured acceptance testing (FAT/SAT) and high-stakes, off-hours facility cutovers with tight change-window constraints.
  • Proficiency with project management tools (e.g., Jira, Confluence, Smartsheet, Microsoft Project, Visio/Lucidchart).
  • Exceptional communication, leadership, and conflict-resolution skills, with the ability to bridge conversations between on-air talent/editorial teams and deep technical engineering specialists.
  • Experience leading facility buildouts, studio relocations, or control room overhauls.
  • Practical knowledge of IP media network architecture (SMPTE ST 2110, ST 2022-6/7, NMOS IS-04/IS-05).
  • Experience with broadcast equipment vendors and platforms (e.g., Grass Valley, Evertz, Ross Video, Sony, Avid, Imagine Communications, Vizrt, Harmonic, Telestream).
  • Familiarity with hybrid/cloud-based media workflows in AWS, Azure, or GCP.
  • Experience managing external Systems Integrators (SIs) and broadcast equipment hardware vendors.
  • Relevant industry certifications: PMP, CAPM, or technical broadcast certifications (e.g., SBE - Society of Broadcast Engineers certifications).

About KMOV:

We operate a CBS + ABC duopoly in one of America's great news towns. That means more platforms for your work — First Alert 4 newscasts, new ABC 32 newscasts, and all-day streaming.

KMOV is the most watched television/digital news operation in Missouri and Southern Illinois with nationally-recognized and award-winning news, weather, and investigative content found both on-air and online. KMOV won the prestigious national Edward R. Murrow Award for Best Newscast in 2023. Based in suburban St. Louis County, KMOV’s home is a new multi-million-dollar state-of-the-art broadcasting and digital facility. Ranked as the #1 city in the nation in 2022 for new college graduates, St. Louis is now recognized for its low cost of living, convenient transportation, and robust arts and entertainment scene. Home to the world-famous Arch, St. Louis Cardinals baseball, City STL soccer, and Blues hockey, St. Louis is quickly becoming THE place to be.

Job Summary/Description:

We are hiring an MMJ to find the best moments in the St. Louis region.’ This MMJ will identify moments as they are happening and deliver them to the audience first.   If your instinct is to capture the moment that everyone will be talking about — the video, the sound, the development that makes our coverage the original source even when everyone in St. Louis is on the same story — keep reading.  

What Winning Looks Like Here:

In St. Louis, First Alert means something. It's a promise: when it matters, we alert first, we stay out front, and we don't wait for the 5 p.m. show to tell people what happened at 2 p.m.

As our Audience-First MMJ, you will:

• Hunt moments, not soundbites. Lead every story with the most memorable moment from the field — off the top, not buried at :45.
• Be the original source. On the day's biggest story, make our video, our detail, our reporting the one everyone else has to credit. How do you separate when it's 4 cameras on the same scene? Show us.
• Put audience over linear. Yes, your stories will air in our traditional newscasts on First Alert 4 and ABC 32. But first, you think audience: you shoot, you send, you collaborate live with our Digital Content Center to post with urgency — stream it, push it, publish it now.
• Live in the field. You hate sitting around in meetings. So do we — for this role. Your desk is your car. Your assignment is to be out, building, finding, breaking.

What You Do Every Day:

• Enterprise, break, and own hard news and breaking news in the St. Louis market
• Build and work sources aggressively — not just for today, but for the next big one
• Shoot, write, edit compelling, tight, moment-driven stories for broadcast, streaming, and digital
• Go live with confidence and clarity, especially when news is breaking and unscripted
• Communicate constantly with producers and the Digital Content Center: what's happening, what you have, what you need, what's next

You'll be coached, you'll be pushed, and you'll be given room to run if you earn it.

Qualifications/Requirements:

Who Thrives In This Role:

• 3+ years working in a TV newsroom as an MMJ/reporter — and you can prove you're different
• A reel that opens with moments, not standups. We should feel like we were there.
• Aggressive on breaking news, calm under chaos, relentless on follow-ups
• Strong photographer instincts: framing, natural sound, sequencing that tells the story without narration
• Digital-first habits: cut a vertical moment, write an urgent web alert and update it
• Source-builder: cops, courts, community, scanners, social — you have a system
• Team player who collaborates fast with photographers, producers, anchors, and digital producers

What We're Not Looking For:

• Someone who wants to anchor. This is not an anchor track.
• Someone who wants to wait for a 6 p.m. package to show their work.
• Someone who needs a meeting to decide to go after news.

How To Apply – Show Us You're Different

Don't send a generic cover letter. Send us:

1. Resume + link to reel (lead with your 3 best moments, not your 3 best packages)
2. In 150 words or less: Tell us about a time every station had the same story, and yours was different. What was the moment, how did you get it, and how fast did the audience see it?
