NBCUniversal’s Ad Sales One Platform Ad Products team builds and operates the systems that power NBCUniversal’s $10B+ advertising business, including core ad serving, programmatic, and activation capabilities across CTV and digital.

Within AP&S, the Programmatic Demand team is responsible for product strategy and development of demand-side capabilities across NBCU’s programmatic ecosystem.

We are seeking a Senior Product Manager, Programmatic Demand to drive the evolution of how programmatic demand is optimized, scaled, and productized across NBCU’s streaming footprint.

Role Overview

This role focuses on developing scalable products, systems, and workflows that improve programmatic demand performance across NBCU’s ad tech stack.

You will identify inefficiencies in auction dynamics, platform behavior, and partner integrations—and translate those insights into durable product solutions rather than one-off optimizations.

A key focus area will be live event monetization, where concurrency, DSP behavior, and system constraints introduce complex demand-side challenges that require structured, product-led solutions.

Key Responsibilities

Auction Performance & Optimization Systems

  • Design and build scalable solutions (tools, workflows, automation) to analyze and optimize auction performance across bid rate, win rate, fill, pacing, and timeouts
  • Translate performance insights into productized capabilities (e.g., automated optimization frameworks, configuration layers, or decisioning logic)
  • Partner with Engineering to implement systems that continuously improve demand efficiency and revenue outcomes

Live Event Monetization (CTV Focus)

  • Identify performance gaps and system constraints in live event auctions (e.g., scaling limits, DSP throttling, timeout behavior)
  • Drive development of product solutions to increase stability, scalability, and performance in high-concurrency environments
  • Partner cross-functionally and externally to ensure platform and partner readiness for tentpole events

Platform Configuration & Deal Strategy

  • Define product-driven approaches to deal structure, configuration standards, and optimization across PG and PMP
  • Improve how platform settings (e.g., in FreeWheel and partner DSPs) translate into predictable demand performance
  • Productize best practices to reduce inefficiencies and variability in deal execution

Partner Integrations & Performance

  • Identify systemic partner performance issues and drive long-term solutions (vs. one-off fixes)
  • Inform product strategy based on partner capabilities, limitations, and evolving DSP behavior

Additional Responsibilities

  • Product Development & Testing: Own requirements and validation for demand optimization features and experiments
  • Cross-Functional Leadership: Align Product, Engineering, Ad Ops, Sales, and Strategy on priorities and outcomes
  • Issue Resolution: Lead root cause analysis and improve systems/processes to prevent recurring issues
  • Documentation & Enablement: Translate product functionality into clear internal guidance and GTM alignment
  • Market Insights: Monitor industry trends and inform product direction

Qualifications

  • Strong understanding of programmatic advertising ecosystems, including digital ad serving, measurement frameworks, identity signals, and privacy controls—and how these components work together to enable scalable, addressable advertising across CTV and digital environments
  • Experience implementing and validating measurement and data pipelines, with a focus on ensuring consistency and accuracy across platforms (e.g., bid requests, attribution, viewability, IVT, and delivery metrics)
  • Solid working knowledge of privacy regulations and industry signals (e.g., CCPA, GDPR, GPP, ATT, COPPA), and their implications for data usage, identity resolution, targeting, and measurement in a programmatic context
  • Experience understanding identity and user signals (e.g., device IDs, platform identifiers, consent signals) to enable privacy-compliant audience targeting and optimization
  • Proven ability to translate complex technical, business, and regulatory requirements into scalable, productized solutions - particularly within programmatic demand, auction dynamics, or partner integrations
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with experience diagnosing performance gaps, data discrepancies, and system inefficiencies, and driving root-cause resolution in production environments
  • Experience developing or leveraging automation and/or AI-driven approaches to monitor, validate, and improve the stability, quality, and performance of demand systems and measurement capabilities
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to operate effectively across Product, Engineering, Ad Ops, Sales, Strategy, and external partners to drive aligned outcomes
  • Demonstrated ability to operate in high-scalability, high-concurrency environments (e.g., CTV and live events), with a product mindset focused on building durable, system-level solutions rather than one-off fixes
  • Minimum of 3+ years of product management experience, preferably within digital advertising, ad tech, or data-driven platforms; experience in CTV, streaming, or programmatic demand strongly preferred

job.description:
Storytelling is, and will always be, the heart of what we do at Skydance.
Our vision is to build a thriving entertainment ecosystem where stories and worlds are imagined, brought to life and experienced. Overview:

The Director of Creative Music, Paramount Pictures serves as a key creative partner across Paramount Pictures’ theatrical slate, supporting filmmakers and creative leadership in the development and execution of music for feature films. Operating as an in-house music supervisor, this role oversees all creative music elements from early development through final delivery, ensuring that each film’s musical vision enhances storytelling and supports the filmmaker’s intent.   This position works closely with directors, producers, composers, artists, and internal studio partners to deliver high-quality, filmmaker-driven music for Paramount Pictures’ theatrical releases. This position is based at the historic Paramount Lot in Los Angeles.  

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Partner with directors, producers, and Paramount Pictures creative executives to shape and execute the musical vision for assigned theatrical films.
  • Engage in projects early in development to provide creative guidance on score, source music, and overall music strategy.
  • Serve as a trusted creative collaborator to filmmakers and talent throughout pre-production, production, and post-production.
  • Advocate for the filmmaker’s creative vision while ensuring alignment with Paramount Pictures’ production goals and creative standards.
  • Act as the in-house music supervisor for assigned Paramount Pictures theatrical films.
  • Oversee all creative music elements including score, source music, needle drops, themes, and temp music.
  • Supervise spotting sessions, music reviews, and creative discussions with filmmakers and post-production teams.
  • Ensure music choices support narrative, tone, and emotional impact.
  • Identify, recommend, and help secure composers and music collaborators in partnership with filmmakers.
  • Guide composers creatively throughout the scoring process, maintaining clear communication between creative and post-production teams.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with composers, artists, music editors, and scoring partners.
  • Oversee music workflows through production and post-production, including scoring schedules, recording sessions, and final mixes.
  • Attend scoring sessions, dubbing sessions, and final mixes as appropriate.
  • Ensure all music is creatively approved, delivered on time, and ready for theatrical release.
  • Collaborate with internal Paramount Pictures teams including Production, Post-Production, Creative Affairs, Legal, Business Affairs, Finance, and Marketing.
  • Partner with music clearance and licensing teams to balance creative ambition with budgetary and legal requirements.
  • Support soundtrack, marketing, publicity, and awards initiatives tied to Paramount Pictures’ theatrical releases.

 

Basic Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of experience in music supervision, film or series music, or creative music roles within theatrical film or television in a studio/network environment.
  • Proven experience supervising music for feature films or series from development through post-production.
  • Prior in-house experience at a major theatrical/TV studio or network
  • Experience working directly with high-profile filmmakers, creative executives and talent.
  • Established relationships with composers, filmmakers, artists, and music industry partners.

Additional Qualifications:

  • Strong creative instincts with deep knowledge of film scoring and source music.
  • Excellent communication, collaboration, and organizational skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple films simultaneously across a theatrical slate.
  • Working knowledge of music licensing, clearance, and music budgeting.
  • Filmmaker-first mindset
  • Collaborative and solution-oriented
  • Strong creative judgment and taste
  • Passion for theatrical storytelling and music

Two years. Three rotations. One launchpad to lead.

 

The Finance Leadership Development Program turns ambitious, innovative Analysts into Skydance’s next generation of Finance leaders. Starting summer 2027, you’ll join as a full-time employee for a two-year program, rotating through three eight-month assignments across our Finance organization — learning the business from the inside, building real financial and leadership skills, and pitching your own capstone project directly to company leadership. A dedicated mentor is with you every step of the way.

 

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Financial Modeling & Forecasting 

    • Craft and maintain complex financial models that shape real budgeting, forecasting, and expense optimization across the business

    • Turn data into direction — translate KPIs and core business metrics into analyses leadership will use to drive decisions

  • Capstone Innovation Project

  • Identify a real business problem, build a solution, and pitch it directly to company leadership — a chance most analysts don’t get until years into their career

  • On-the-Job Training & Leadership Development

  • Own real, high-impact work from day one — guided by your manager and a dedicated mentor invested in your growth

  • Receive comprehensive AI training, including in-depth sessions on how and when to use finance and other enterprise-wide tools

  • Sharpen your leadership edge through recurring feedback, a day shadowing an executive, and dedicated leadership training

  • Reporting & Close

  • Own critical pieces of the monthly and quarterly close — accruals, reconciliation, and variance analysis that keep the business accurate

  • Dive into the general ledger and turn raw numbers into clear, actionable reports

  • Run the quarterly payment process end-to-end

  • Business Partnership

  • Partner directly with finance, accounting, and business leaders — your insight helps shape how the business plans ahead

  • Take on ad hoc, high-visibility requests that put your problem-solving in front of the people who matter

  • Build a cross-functional network of relationships that will follow you for the rest of your career

 

LEADERSHIP TRAINING | INNOVATION | CAPSTONE PROJECT | DIRECT EXECUTIVE ACCESS

  • Proper work authorization is required to be employed within the United States for the full length of the program (July 2027-July 2029).

  • Experience in finance or accounting

  • Ability to work in a fast paced, high-pressure environment

job.title: Account Executive
job.description:
Title: Account Executive

Join The Alton Telegraph to help deliver impactful media campaigns for our customers, leveraging our rich history, extensive audience reach, best-in-class advertising solutions, and the power of cutting-edge AI tools!

Role Overview:  Hearst Newspapers is investing in its sales force, and we want you to be a part of it! We are looking for a digitally savvy, highly motivated Account Executive to join our advertising team at The Alton Telegraph. As an Account Executive, you will be responsible for developing and managing a sales pipeline and building new business relationships with local advertisers throughout the Alton area. You will work with your customers to promote compelling solutions that best fit their marketing needs. As an advocate for the customer within the Alton Telegraph, the role works in cooperation with other departments to ensure we can meet and exceed customer expectations both in performance and process. Hearst Newspapers operates on a hybrid work week schedule. 

The Alton Telegraph?

Our people make the difference! Our diverse team is filled with passionate individuals who want to win. We offer an upbeat and collaborative working environment where challenging the norm is encouraged. With ample opportunities to learn new skills and advance within the organization, our team members are given the tools to learn and grow their careers.

Leverage Advanced AI for Maximum Efficiency and Earnings
Imagine having a personal assistant that never sleeps. Our state-of-the-art AI tools, including ChatGPT Enterprise and Gong.io, streamline your workflow, enabling you to close deals faster and manage your pipeline more effectively. 

This means more time to focus on what you love and a direct boost to your earnings potential.

Exclusive Partnership with OpenAI
Through our strategic content partnership with OpenAI and our exclusive ChatGPT Enterprise license, we have unparalleled access to the latest advancements in AI technology. 

This partnership provides us—and you—with a massive competitive edge in the market, ensuring you have the most powerful tools at your disposal to drive sales and exceed targets.

Personalized AI Tutors for Seamless Onboarding
Your success starts from day one. With our personalized AI tutors, every question you have, and every training need you encounter is met with instant, tailored support. 

These AI-driven mentors ensure you learn and sell as quickly and efficiently as possible, empowering you to hit the ground running and achieve your goals faster.

What will you do?

  • Drive Success with Innovative Tools: Utilize our AI-powered software to enhance every stage of the sales cycle, from prospecting and planning to presenting and closing deals.

  • Lead Generation: Call on local small to medium sized businesses to show the value of our suite of digital media advertising products from social media, display, video, programmatic, SEO/SEM to traditional advertisements. You will generate new leads through cold calling, networking, and prospecting, as well as staying aware of any new businesses opening in the area. You will own the sales cycle and will have the support of your local account management team to aid in continued support after the sale!

  • Product Expertise: Become an expert on our digital and print products/services. The first three weeks of hire, you will be provided with both global and local training to be fully educated before even going out on your own! You will also have full support throughout your career which includes continual learning and training to grow and achieve success as an Account Executive. 

  • Execute sales tactics: Implementing marketing strategies, delivering effective sales presentations with passion to consistently earn, retain and increase revenue.

  • Advertising Solutions: Create engaging advertising solutions to solve clients’ business needs.

  • Client Solutions: Recommend new products and promotional opportunities to current clients and handle objections efficiently. Be a large part of the local business community and boosting your clients’ businesses through multiple digital media channels.

  • Forecasting: Manage client pipeline and monthly revenue forecast in Salesforce.com.

 

What will it take to be successful?

  • Purposeful: You are direct and get things done quickly, with confidence, integrity, and determination.

  • Adaptable: You react and adjust to changing conditions and come up with practical ideas to deal with them.

  • Driven: You have self-assurance and competitive drive, delivering high-quality, organized, and repeatable results.

  • Communicator: You are a lively and intelligent person with a stimulating influence on others.

  • Trend-Savvy: you will keep informed of industry developments to ensure our digital advertising strategies remain cutting-edge and effective.

 

What we’re looking for:

  • Education: BA/BS degree in Advertising, Marketing, or Communications a plus or equivalent experience.

  • Experience: 2+ years of business-to-business outside sales in advertising or media, with a proven success in new business acquisition and exceeding revenue goals.

  • Skills: Superior presentation, interpersonal, and communication skills. Technically savvy with experience in Salesforce, Excel, and PowerPoint.

  • Mindset: Goal-oriented, competitive, and forward-thinking with strong business and financial acumen.

 

What we offer:

  • Dynamic Environment: A great work environment where it's never boring.

  • Comprehensive Training: Paid in-depth sales and product training.

  • Competitive Compensation: Competitive base salary with uncapped commissions for unlimited earning potential.

  • Collaborative Culture: Ideas and input are always welcome.

  • Learn more about Hearst Newspapers at www.joinhnp.com

 

Our Benefits: At Hearst Newspapers we not only support our employees through personal and professional development, but we also believe in promoting each individual’s physical, financial and emotional wellbeing (and that of their family).  Our industry-leading benefits include:

  • Physical Wellbeing: Medical, Dental, and Vision coverage to keep you and your family healthy.

  • Invest for the Future: Competitive retirement plan with matching program in most markets.

  • Generous Paid Time Off: Recharge with ample time off, including holidays and vacation.

  • Paid Parental Leave: Support for growing families, with paid leave for new parents.

  • Monthly Child & Dependent Care Reimbursement: Financial support for the care of your loved ones.

  • Emotional Wellbeing: Be your best self with our mental wellness benefits.

  • LGBTQ+ & Inclusive Health Services: Inclusive healthcare designed for every individual’s unique needs.

  • Fertility Coverage & Menopause Support: Helping you along every step of your family journey.

  • Pet Wellness Reimbursement & Rover Credits: We care about your pets, too – helping you keep them happy and healthy.

  • And more, click here for additional benefits and details.

Compensation: In accordance with applicable law, Hearst is required to include a reasonable estimate of the compensation for this role if hired in Connecticut. The reasonable estimate, if hired in Connecticut, is $35,000 - $40,000 base plus commissions based on individual performance, commissions are uncapped for unlimited earning potential. A final decision on the successful candidate’s starting salary will be based on a number of permissible, non-discriminatory factors, including but not limited to skills and experience, training, certifications, and education.

Benefits: Eligible employees enjoy Health, dental, vision coverage, Health savings and/or flexible spending accounts, short & long-term disability insurance, 401k with company match, paid time off for vacation, sick days, company holidays and floating holidays. 

About Hearst Newspapers:

With 2,500 employees across the nation, HNP represents a network of 24 daily and 52 weekly publications, including the San Francisco Chronicle, Houston Chronicle, San Antonio Express-News and Albany Times Union, several top digital-only news and lifestyle sites, marketing services businesses, and entertainment businesses such as King Features Syndicate. At HNP, we are investing in new and innovative ways to tell stories–growing newsrooms, diversifying tools, evolving platforms–to support the millions of people who trust us each month to help them make decisions, take action and be inspired. 

Be a part of something bigger–Your Headline Awaits

job.title: CRM Executive
job.description:
Join our team at the Guardian and be a part of a diverse and inclusive global organisation that delivers fearless, investigative journalism, and holds power to account. Our team of award-winning journalists, cutting-edge commercial professionals, and industry-leading digital experts are committed to making a difference and represent a wide range of backgrounds and perspectives. We offer a challenging and exciting environment for career development, with a focus on training, growth and fostering an inclusive culture.

 

We are now looking for a CRM Executive to join the team. The CRM Executive will be planning and implementing multi-channel CRM activity across the reader lifecycle.

 

About the role

  • Plan, develop and implement multi-channel campaigns such as but not limited to; acquisition, in-life, upsell/cross-sell, renewal, winback
  • Deliver multi-channel and measurable customer campaigns and journeys
  • Presenting plans and activity performance to a broad range of stakeholders, taking part in team and cross functional meetings 

 

About you

  • Experience of building campaigns using a CRM tool (ideally Braze but not essential)
  • Experience of marketing performance tracking, analysis and reporting
  • Experience in audience-centric, data-driven marketing
  • Experience of executing activity across email, but other channels would be a bonus

 We actively encourage applications from groups traditionally underrepresented in the UK media 

We operate in a hybrid environment working 3 days a week from our offices in Kings Cross and 2 days a week remotely. 

 

We value and respect all differences (seen and unseen) in all people. We aspire to have inclusive working experiences and an environment that reflects the audience we serve, where our people have equal access to career development opportunities, their voices are heard and can contribute to our future. We actively encourage applications from people of all backgrounds. Many of our staff work flexibly and we will consider all requests for flexible working arrangements.

 

Please find a copy of the job description here.

 

How to apply

To apply, please upload your latest CV and cover letter which answers the following questions:

 

  1. Why are you interested in working on CRM specifically within a reader-funded, publisher environment like The Guardian compared to traditional e-commerce?

  2. Give one example of a revenue-focused or conversion campaign you have worked on. Briefly, what was the goal, channels used and key metric/business impact achieved?

 

We appreciate the time taken to prepare each application we receive. We do not use AI-assisted technology to review applications; every application is reviewed by a member of our recruitment team. Thank you for bearing with us during the screening process.

 

The closing date for applications is 6pm, Friday 30th October 2026.

 

Guardian News and Media is proud to be a London Living wage employer. The minimum salary for any full-time role within the organisation is £30,000 per annum. Salary ranges are dependent on skills and experience. 

 

All roles at the Guardian are open for everybody to apply. It is important to us that you feel supported and comfortable throughout your recruitment process, in order to perform your best. Please let us know if there are any changes we could make to help your application, this includes providing documents in accessible formats or personalising the process to better support your needs. Please contact Karen Walter on karen.walter@theguardian.com to discuss further so we can work with you to support you through your application.

 

Benefits at the Guardian

You'll have 30 days of annual leave per year (plus bank holidays) with the option to purchase an additional 5 days. Our pension scheme is generous; if you contribute 5% then we will contribute 8-12% (depending on your age). We believe in giving back, which is why employees are given 2 volunteering days annually and the option of payroll giving. Season ticket loans are also available.

You are entitled to private healthcare, life cover, income protection, and eye tests. You can also opt in to dental insurance.

We have enhanced maternity, paternity, adoption and shared parental leave policies in place. We also support our employees by offering an IVF, menopause, baby loss, and trans equality policy.

 

Culture and wellbeing

We want everyone to feel like they belong at the Guardian and we champion diversity of thought. Our various employee forums provide a platform to use their voice to foster an inclusive workplace. We became the first major media organisation to achieve B Corp status.

We offer tools to help you prioritise your wellbeing including access to our employee benefits platform which provides tailored support for health and wellbeing. In addition, we also offer free yoga and Pilates classes. These run alongside our corporate gym membership and cycle to work scheme. Our canteen has views overlooking the Regents Canal and caters for breakfast, lunch and dinner.

 

Learning and development

We encourage personal and professional growth. Employees have access to a broad range of tools and solutions, and we are happy to support the pursuit of professional qualifications through vocational courses and apprenticeships.

job.title: Senior Data Analyst – Paid Media
job.description:
Company Information

AEG brings music, sports, and live entertainment together to create moments people remember around the world. Each year, more than 100 million fans experience live events across five continents—from global touring, concerts, and festivals to iconic sports and entertainment destinations.

Through our music division, AEG Presents, one of the world’s leading operators of tours, concerts, and music festivals, we help shape the sound of now. We work with artists at every stage of their careers to bring live music to life, connecting artists with fans on stages around the world.

Headquartered in Los Angeles, AEG Presents is driven by creativity, innovation, and purpose, and powered by people who want their work to show up in the real world.

If you’re ready to help create moments that matter, there’s a place for you here. Because it happens here.

 

The Senior Data Analyst – Paid Media sits on the Data Analytics, Reporting & Strategy team and serves as the analytical partner and lead for the Paid Media team. Paid Media drives company-wide digital media strategy, campaign management, and consultative support across AEG divisions, including AEG Presents, Global Touring, Festivals, Goldenvoice, Bowery Presents, and Global Partnerships. Campaigns run across a broad mix of channels, including Meta, Google Ads, TikTok, and other social, search, and programmatic platforms.

This role is responsible for pulling, transforming, and modeling campaign data from those ad platforms and joining it with other data sources to build a unified view of performance. The analyst will design scalable data models and automated reporting that measure campaign effectiveness and surface opportunities to optimize budget allocation, audience targeting, creative, and customer acquisition. The role also turns findings into clear, practical recommendations that drive ticket sales, event awareness, and brand initiatives.

The Senior Data Analyst will work closely with the Paid Media, Product, and Data Engineering teams on cross-functional projects covering paid media data ingestion, aggregation, mastering, measurement, and visualization. The position will lead the work to make sure tracking and tagging (pixels, conversion APIs, UTMs) capture accurate marketing data. It will also develop and maintain attribution models and set performance benchmarks for key metrics such as CPA, ROAS, CTR, and conversion rate.

Essential Functions

 

  • Provide analytical support to Paid Media and Marketing teams, compiling performance marketing reports across digital channels using internal BI tools, Google Analytics, native advertising platforms. Communicate results to stakeholders, working with media and strategy teams to demonstrate clear actionable insights for media plans, budget forecasting, targeting/audiences, and creative.
  • Build and maintain comprehensive measurement plans to evaluate paid media performance, calculate benchmarks based on objectives, develop + maintain attribution models to identify trends, testing opportunities, and insights by channel, audience, festival/tour/regional show, and business unit.
  • Partner with Data, Product, Engineering teams to manage data pipelines + ingestion for channel metrics, define data collection requirements and enforce optimal taxonomy for reporting implementations, continual data hygiene + integrity across ad buying and internal platforms.
  • Collaborate with media, marketing, and data teams to inform audience and targeting strategies. Develop tests to evaluate new campaign strategies, ad products, optimization tactics, and targeting features.
  • Manage and lead paid media projects involving data aggregation and measurement tools such as Datorama, Google Analytics / GA4, Tag Manager, DOMO, BigQuery, LiveRamp, server-server integrations with media partners. Ensure appropriate site tracking is in place to capture relevant data points to measure marketing effectiveness.
  • Work closely with data team to develop and maintain reporting dashboards for internal and external use, while providing support for ad hot reporting requests.

 

Required Qualifications

  • BA/BS degree (4-year) in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Business, Marketing, or a related quantitative field
  • 4–6 years of experience in data analytics, business intelligence, or a similar role, with exposure to paid media or digital marketing data on the client, publisher, or agency side; e-commerce experience preferred
  • Advanced SQL skills and experience pulling, transforming, and analyzing large, complex datasets
  • Strong ability to build data models, data flows, and ETL/ELT pipelines using SQL and/or Python, bringing together data from multiple media channels into a scalable, automated insights reporting structure
  • Proficiency in BI and data visualization tools such as DOMO, Looker Studio, Tableau, or similar, with strong dashboard design and data storytelling skills
  • Experience with Salesforce Marketing Cloud Intelligence (formerly Datorama) or similar marketing data integration platforms is a strong plus
  • Working knowledge of paid media data and performance metrics, including impressions, CTR, CPC, CPA, conversion rate, and ROAS, across platforms such as Meta, Google Ads, and TikTok
  • Familiarity with tracking infrastructure such as GA4, Google Tag Manager, pixels, Conversions API, UTMs, and server-side tracking
  • Experience applying statistical methods to performance benchmarking, attribution modeling, and media mix modeling (MMM)
  • Understanding of the ad tech and Martech landscape (programmatic buying, DSP/SSP, audience management, ad serving, social buying platforms), and of privacy regulations’ impact on measurement, including cookie-less tracking and multi-touch customer journeys
  • Ability to clearly communicate insights and recommendations to technical and non-technical stakeholders, and manage multiple cross-functional projects at once

Payscale: $82,158.00 -$125,000.00

Bonus:  This position is not eligible for a bonus under the current bonus plan requirements.

Benefits: Full-time: We offer a comprehensive benefits package that includes: medical, dental and vision insurance, paid holidays, vacation and sick time, company paid basic life insurance, voluntary life insurance, parental leave, 401k Plan (with a current employer match of 3%), flexible spending and health savings account options, and wellness offerings.

AEG reserves the right to change or modify the employee’s job description whether orally or in writing, at any time during the employment relationship.  AEG may require an employee to perform duties outside their normal description.

AEG's policy is to hire the most qualified applicants, and we comply with all applicable federal, state and local employment laws in making hiring and employee decisions.  We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate against applicants or employees on the basis of race, color, marital status, disability, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, genetic information, veteran status, or any other legally protected status recognized by applicable federal, state or local law.

 

Employer does not offer work visa sponsorship for this position.

job.title: Sr. Accountant - Southwest
job.description:
For more than 20 years, AEG has played a pivotal role in transforming sports and live entertainment. Annually, we host more than 160 million guests, promote more than 10,000 shows and present more than 22,000 events around the world. We are committed to innovation, artistry, and community, and leverage the power of our 300+ venues, leading sports franchises, marquee music brands, integrated entertainment districts, premier ticketing platform and global sponsorship activations, to create memorable moments that give the world reason to cheer.

Our business is interwoven with the human mind and heart, and we strive to build a diverse and inclusive company that reflects the artists, athletes, and fans that we host; reach beyond traditional boundaries to support the communities in which we operate; and minimize our impact on the environment by adopting sustainable practices throughout our business operations.

If you want to be challenged to up your game and make a difference, then join us in giving the world reason to cheer!

Job Summary

The Sr. Accountant is responsible for financial reporting, including the reconciliation of the balance sheet and the monthly reforecasting. The Sr. Accountant enters, codes, and approves invoices, road checks and expenses and will also be responsible for preparing the monthly closing, journal entries, balance sheet analysis, expense coding, maintaining show files, settling shows and miscellaneous accounting projects as assigned. The Sr. Accountant is accountable for monthly accounting entries in the general ledger including invoices, petty cash, T&E, corporate credit cards, royalties and insurance. This position works in conjunction with Accounting Manager or Director of Accounting and is a contributing member of the finance team that oversees all financials for venue/region.

Essential Functions

  • Review and reconciliation of balance sheet, general ledger, accounts receivables and accounts payables.
  • Review and coding of invoices, road checks, cash receipts, p-card transactions and expenses. Create and code invoices for outstanding receivables. Obtain proper approval and code to specific events. Audits show file for tour and co-promotion settlements.
  • Responsible for monthly accounting entries in general ledger including invoicing rental clients, 3rd party processing, petty cash, T&E, corporate credit cards, royalties, and insurance.
  • Enter cash receipts and road checks for region into JDE and code to appropriate department. Review event settlements for accuracy and process road checks and cash receipts through AP.
  • Works in conjunction with Accounting Manager or Director of Accounting for department/venue to prepare annual budgeting and reforecasting based on monthly and annual projected sales. Complete the month end close and show and tour reconciliation.
  • Management of audits, including compilation of data for appropriate inquiries. Organize payroll audits for regional venues and offices.
  • Liaison with CAPs and part-time employees. Ensuring that staff needs are met and payroll conflicts are resolved in a timely manner to reduce compliance liability - check requests, rate discrepancies, and payroll audits.
  • Analyzes cost data to determine return on investment on partnership deals and renewals.
  • Annual management of building permits and renewals.
  • May assist in show settlement as necessary for unassigned shows or tours.

Required Qualifications

  • BA/BS Degree (4-year) In Finance/Accounting
  • 4-6 years Of related work experience
  • Experience with JDE, ImageNow, and Concur
  • Knowledge of basic accounting principles
  • Ability to multi-task and detail-orientated
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Word and Outlook; Strong Microsoft Excel skills-specifically working in pivot tables
  • Strong financial analytical skills with prior experience in finance reporting systems
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Able to work independently and as part of a team to accomplish the goals of finance department
  • Strong time management and interpersonal skills
  • Music Industry knowledge and concert operation experience

job.description:
Job Summary:

WHO ARE WE?

Live Nation Entertainment is the world’s leading live entertainment company, comprised of global market leaders: Ticketmaster, Live Nation Concerts, and Live Nation Media & Sponsorship. Ticketmaster is the global leader in event ticketing with over 620 million tickets sold annually and approximately 10,000 clients worldwide.  Live Nation Concerts is the largest provider of live entertainment in the world promoting more than 50,000 events annually for nearly 7,000 artists in 40+ countries. These businesses allow Live Nation Media & Sponsorship to create strategic music marketing programs that connect more than 1,200 sponsors with the 145 million fans that attend Live Nation Entertainment events each year. For additional information, visit www.livenationentertainment.com.

 

WHO ARE YOU?

Passionate and motivated. Driven, with an entrepreneurial spirit. Resourceful, innovative, forward thinking and committed. At Live Nation Entertainment, our people embrace these qualities, so if this sounds like you then please read on! 

 

THE JOB

The New York City Production Department is looking for a Production Manager who oversees the execution, management, and administration of production operations for all Live Nation-operated and third-party venues, including amphitheaters, arenas and stadiums in the region. Collaborating with the operations, talent management, and finance teams, the department plays a crucial role in liaising with clients, event planners, performing talent, venues, technical and site vendors, labor unions, and other key stakeholders to ensure the success of all events, both front and back of house.

 

The ideal Production Manager will have the ability to handle multiple projects and adapt to fast-paced, changing environments while maintaining quality and demonstrating exemplary leadership and teamwork. The candidate will be directly responsible for managing 75+ shows annually, and some travel within the region will be required.

 

WHAT THIS ROLE WILL DO

  • Oversee all on-stage, backstage, technical, and site planning aspects of events.
  • Advance and obtain key technical information, including venue specs, production needs, rider requirements, staging, and capacity changes.
  • Develop and maintain production documents such as site drawings, on-sale layouts, timelines, schedules, and artist riders.
  • Settlement of shows would be high priorty
  • Produce events across a range of venue sizes—from clubs and theaters to amphitheaters arenas and stadiums.
  • Manage technical production elements (e.g., stage, sound, video, lighting, backline, broadcast, labor crews).
  • Support site operations (e.g., power, heavy equipment, traffic flow, crowd control, sanitation, permitting, and engineering).
  • Track and assist with budget management for assigned responsibilities.
  • •         Lead multiple projects from planning through execution, including on-site presence from load-in to load-out.
  • •         Maintain consistent communication with stakeholders and senior leadership through meetings, calls, and emails.
  • •         Facilitate interdepartmental coordination and follow up on action items from internal and external meetings.
  • •         Foster a positive, collaborative environment for planning teams.
  • •         Contribute to event debriefs, including financial settlement notes and recommendations for future improvements.
  • •         Perform additional duties as assigned.

 

WHAT THIS PERSON WILL BRING

•         5+ years of production management experience across varied venue types and event scales

•         Proven project management and planning expertise, with the ability to manage multiple events simultaneously

•         Strong leadership and decision-making skills, especially under pressure and with limited information

•         Proficiency in both Windows and Mac OS applications (Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint, OneNote, SharePoint)

•         Exceptional organizational and communication skills—written, verbal, and interpersonal

•         Ability to prioritize tasks, meet deadlines, and maintain composure in fast-paced environments

•         Experience procuring vendors (e.g., staging, audio, lighting, video) and managing staff, services, and budgets

•         Flexible schedule with availability for nights, weekends, holidays, and regional travel as needed

•         Skilled in diplomatic communication with clients, vendors, and artist representatives

•         Adaptability to new technologies, workflows, and evolving event environments

 

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting live events, entertainment, music, production, hospitality, or another project-based industry.
  • Familiarity with QuickBooks, PEX, DocuSign, Dropbox, and spreadsheet-based tracking tools.
  • Experience with accounts payable, vendor onboarding, payroll coordination, contractor agreements, or expense reconciliation.
  • Experience coordinating meetings, calendars, staffing details, and cross-functional project follow-up.
  • Familiarity with event budgets, project codes, cost allocations, or post-event closeout processes.
  • Comfort working in a collaborative environment where priorities can change quickly.

HEALTH: Medical, vision, dental and mental health benefits for you and your family, with access to a health care concierge, and Flexible or Health Savings Accounts (FSA or HSA)

ABOUT THE ROLE

Working in close collaboration with the promoter and production teams, the Operations Accountant ensures accurate and timely night-of-show settlements. The role covers full-cycle accounting for each show: recording the income statement and balance sheet entries that capture the settlement, reviewing and approving transactions, and reconciling payables and receivables through to month-end close.

 

WHAT THIS ROLE WILL DO

This position owns the accounting for each show, from pre-settlement through month-end reporting, including:

  • Assist with pre-settlement and night-of-show artist settlements, working directly with promoters, artist representatives and production staff.
  • Act as the primary accounting point of contact for the talent department, artist representatives and production staff.
  • Enter show settlements into the accounting systems and distribute settlement reports to stakeholders.
  • Review all show settlements to confirm proper documentation and backup are on file for audit purposes.
  • Prepare and code artist final settlement wires per contract ensuring withholding taxes, charity and album bundles are correctly recognized.
  • Settle venue expenses, shared ancillary revenues and co-promotion deals.
  • Finalize the profit and loss statement for each show.
  • Code, approve and distribute show invoices and cheques for Accounts Payable input.
  • Prepare and upload show entries, along with accounts receivable and accounts payable settlements.
  • Reconcile revenues, project costs and accruals, resolving variances promptly.
  • Reconcile accounts receivable, review balances for accuracy and follow up to ensure timely collection.
  • Complete the month-end close and report per-show contribution margin.
  • Maintain and adhere to internal controls
  • Travel and provide on-site support for large shows and festival properties as required.
  • Take on ad hoc projects as assigned by management.

 

 

WHAT THIS PERSON WILL BRING

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or equivalent; progress toward or completion of a CPA designation
  • 3–5 years of accounting experience, with demonstrated strength in reconciliation (accounts payable, accounts receivable, accruals and cash).
  • Strong Oracle and/or Salesforce capability; advanced Excel
  • Practical use of Claude, AI platforms, BI and automation tooling to reduce manual work
  • Experience in live entertainment, events or another high-volume, deadline-driven transactional environment is an asset.
  • Strong organizational and time management skills, with the ability to complete multiple time-sensitive settlements and close activities on schedule.
  • Highly detail-oriented, with a strong ability to multi-task and maintain accuracy under tight night-of-show timelines.
  • Strong written and verbal communication and excellent interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with promoters, artist representatives, production staff and colleagues across the organization.
  • Proficiency applications, especially Microsoft Excel.
  • Flexibility to work evenings and weekends around show schedules, and to travel for large shows and festivals.

job.title: Engineering Lead – ERP Services
job.description:
About Us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Together, we help audiences stay better informed and deepen their understanding of the world around them.

Our Product & Tech teams drive us forward in an ever-evolving digital landscape, delivering cutting-edge products to over one million digital subscribers daily. Our growth relies on a diverse, dedicated and dynamic group of product, tech, delivery and data specialists.

With a supportive culture, entrepreneurial spirit and opportunities at every turn, there are no limits to where your FT career can take you.

Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

Our commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion

We believe everyone should have a fair opportunity to contribute, succeed, and reach their full potential. That means ensuring everyone is heard, respected, and valued, while identifying and removing barriers that may get in the way. Our commitment is to be an employer role model, grounded in inclusion and fairness for all.We want every application to receive fair and thoughtful consideration; therefore, all applications are reviewed by a member of our recruitment team, not by AI.

About you

You are an experienced engineering leader with strong knowledge of ERP or similarly complex enterprise platforms and a track record of leading teams responsible for business-critical technology.

You combine people leadership with credible technical judgement. You are comfortable setting direction, making engineering decisions and working with your team on complex technical problems, while creating the ownership and autonomy for engineers to succeed.

You understand that enterprise platform engineering goes beyond implementing configuration or coordinating vendors. You think about the entire technology capability: the core platform, integrations, data flows, extensions, operational processes, security, resilience and how the platform evolves over time.

You are comfortable working closely with Finance and other business stakeholders, translating priorities and requirements into sustainable technology solutions and constructively challenging approaches that create unnecessary complexity or risk.

You are also interested in building capability. You can identify gaps in skills and knowledge, develop engineers and create a team that understands and genuinely owns its technology rather than relying disproportionately on individual specialists or external partners.

About the team

ERP Services sits within Corporate Technology, part of Internal Products, and owns the engineering capabilities supporting critical Finance and enterprise business processes across the FT.

The team is responsible for the engineering, operation and continuous evolution of our ERP technology estate, including Oracle Fusion and the integrations, data flows and supporting capabilities that connect it to the wider FT technology landscape.

ERP Services works closely with Finance, Product, Architecture, Integration & Engineering Services, Security and other Corporate Technology teams to ensure these critical enterprise capabilities remain reliable and can evolve as the needs of the organisation change.

We are strengthening the engineering leadership and platform expertise within ERP Services as part of a wider evolution of the Corporate Technology operating model. The Engineering Lead will establish clear platform and team ownership, reporting to the Principal Engineer – Corporate Technology.

What you’ll work on

As Engineering Lead – ERP Services, you will own the engineering, operation and continuous evolution of the FT’s ERP technology capability.

You will lead the ERP engineering team, providing people leadership, technical direction and clear accountability for the health and performance of the platforms and services the team owns.

A key part of the role will be strengthening our internal ERP engineering capability. You will develop the technical knowledge of the team, establish clear ownership of platforms and services and ensure we have the skills and understanding required to operate and evolve our ERP estate effectively.

You will work closely with Product and Finance stakeholders to understand business priorities and translate them into engineering plans, balancing new capabilities and business change with platform health, technical debt and operational investment.

You will also work with the Principal Engineer and Architecture to ensure decisions within ERP Services support the longer-term direction of Corporate Technology and the wider FT technology estate.

Your responsibilities will include

Engineering & Platform Ownership

  • Owning the engineering, operation and continuous evolution of the ERP technology capability.
  • Providing clear technical direction for the platforms, integrations and supporting services owned by ERP Services.
  • Ensuring ERP platforms remain secure, resilient, scalable, maintainable and appropriately supported.
  • Establishing clear ownership across the team for systems, integrations and technical capabilities.
  • Ensuring engineering decisions consider reliability, security, operability, maintainability, cost and long-term sustainability.
  • Maintaining visibility of platform health, technical debt, lifecycle risks and significant dependencies.
  • Working with the Principal Engineer and Architecture on material technical decisions and longer-term platform direction.
  • Ensuring the team maintains sufficient technical understanding of its platforms to make informed decisions and challenge external recommendations.

People & Engineering Leadership

  • Leading, supporting and developing the engineers within ERP Services.
  • Setting clear expectations and providing regular coaching, feedback and career development.
  • Building a team culture based on ownership, accountability, collaboration and constructive technical challenge.
  • Developing ERP and enterprise platform expertise across the team rather than allowing critical knowledge to remain concentrated in individuals.
  • Identifying capability and skills gaps and developing plans to address them through development, recruitment or appropriate external expertise.
  • Creating opportunities for engineers to take greater technical ownership and develop their leadership capability.
  • Supporting recruitment and building a resilient team with the skills required for the future ERP technology landscape.
  • Ensuring appropriate succession and knowledge sharing across critical areas.

Delivery & Planning

  • Working with Product to translate business priorities and technology strategy into clear engineering plans and deliverable outcomes.
  • Owning engineering planning and resource allocation within ERP Services.
  • Ensuring engineering capacity appropriately balances business change, platform improvement, operational work and technical debt.
  • Identifying technical dependencies, risks and constraints early and ensuring these are visible in planning and prioritisation.
  • Ensuring delivery commitments are realistic and supported by appropriate technical understanding.
  • Working across teams where initiatives involve multiple platforms, integrations or engineering capabilities.
  • Providing clear visibility of engineering progress, risks and trade-offs to Product, technology leadership and relevant stakeholders.

ERP Platform Evolution

  • Developing a clear understanding of the current ERP estate and identifying opportunities to simplify, modernise and improve it.
  • Working with Product, Architecture and the Principal Engineer to shape the longer-term evolution of ERP technology.
  • Evaluating platform capabilities and determining when requirements should be addressed through standard functionality, configuration, integration or other engineering approaches.
  • Challenging unnecessary customisation and complexity where more sustainable solutions are available.
  • Ensuring platform upgrades, new capabilities and significant changes are introduced safely and sustainably.
  • Understanding vendor roadmaps and assessing their implications for the FT's technology direction and investment decisions.
  • Ensuring technical debt and lifecycle concerns are actively managed rather than accumulating through incremental business change.

Integration & Enterprise Technology

  • Ensuring the team understands and owns the integrations and data flows connecting ERP with the wider FT technology estate.
  • Working closely with Integration & Engineering Services and other platform teams to establish clear ownership of cross-system capabilities.
  • Ensuring integrations follow appropriate FT engineering and architectural standards.
  • Identifying opportunities to simplify interfaces, reduce duplication and improve reliability.
  • Supporting technical decisions that span ERP, Tax, People and other Corporate Technology capabilities.
  • Ensuring changes within ERP appropriately consider downstream and upstream impacts.

Operational Excellence & Risk

  • Owning the operational performance of ERP Services and ensuring critical services are appropriately monitored and supported.
  • Establishing effective approaches to observability, incident management, problem management, change management and operational readiness.
  • Ensuring recurring incidents and operational problems are investigated to their underlying causes and addressed sustainably.
  • Maintaining appropriate approaches to resilience, disaster recovery and business continuity.
  • Ensuring relevant security, data governance, compliance and technology standards are met.
  • Maintaining visibility of material operational and technical risks and ensuring appropriate mitigation plans are in place.
  • Using operational insight to inform engineering priorities and platform investment.

Vendors & Technology Partners

  • Managing the technical relationship with ERP vendors, implementation partners and specialist service providers.
  • Ensuring external partners are used effectively while maintaining clear internal engineering ownership.
  • Providing informed technical challenge to vendor recommendations and proposed solutions.

We provide a broad range of essential services, including news, comment, data, and analysis, to a growing audience of internationally minded business people.

Here at the FT, gold-standard journalism is just the beginning. Our 500-people-strong Product & Tech team keeps us ahead of the ever-changing digital landscape by delivering cutting-edge products to over one million digital subscribers every day. Our plans for growth rely on a diverse, dedicated, and dynamic group of product, tech, delivery, and data specialists – everyone’s welcome in this friendly, forward-thinking team.

 

Our commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion

We believe everyone should have a fair opportunity to contribute, succeed, and reach their full potential. That means ensuring everyone is heard, respected, and valued, while identifying and removing barriers that may get in the way. Our commitment is to be an employer role model, grounded in inclusion and fairness for all.We want every application to receive fair and thoughtful consideration; therefore, all applications are reviewed by a member of our recruitment team, not by AI.  

Storyfinding team

The Storyfinding team sits at the heart of innovation between the FT’s newsroom and technology. We collaborate closely with the Computational Journalism team to uncover and scale new ways of finding stories hidden in complex or unstructured data.

Our mission is to turn bespoke investigations into reusable tools and data products that empower more journalists to tell stories that otherwise would be untold. This is where engineering meets journalism — you can see the direct impact of your work on the FT’s homepage.

Since the team was formed, Storyfinding has helped uncover more than 10 exclusive stories, including Europe builds for war as arms factories expand at triple speed and Prices for used Teslas drop in US and Britain.

We are a cross-functional team of Software Engineers, Data Engineers, ML Ops Engineers, and Product Managers. We balance strong engineering practices with the fast-moving needs of the newsroom, delivering quickly while keeping our systems reliable, secure, and easy to evolve.

About the Role

Overview

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer 1 to play a key role in designing, building, and operating the backend systems and services that power Storyfinding’s investigative and editorial work.

This is a hands-on senior individual contributor role with a primary focus on backend software engineering. You will be responsible for designing and building robust backend systems and services, while also maintaining that data engineering is a key component of the work. You will contribute to and maintain critical data pipelines and data products, helping to establish patterns and standards that enable the team to scale its impact.

What You’ll Work On

Some example projects include:

  • Designing and operating data pipelines that ingest, clean, enrich, and model complex datasets for investigative reporting.
  • Building resilient, observable data workflows to support high-traffic and time-critical newsroom events such as elections or major economic announcements.
  • Developing shared data infrastructure and tooling that turns one-off investigations into reusable capabilities for the wider newsroom.
  • Working with unstructured and semi-structured data sources (documents, filings, scraped content, APIs) to create high-quality, queryable datasets.
  • Collaborating with journalists, product managers, and engineers to translate editorial questions into scalable data solutions.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and maintain scalable and resilient backend services, APIs, and infrastructure.
  • Ensure high standards of software quality through testing, documentation, observability, and security across all systems.
  • Design, build, and maintain scalable, reliable data pipelines and datasets in a cloud environment.
  • Work across OLTP and OLAP data stores to support both application-driven and analytical use cases.
  • Partner closely with journalists and other technical colleagues to shape data solutions that directly support storytelling.
  • Lead by example in engineering best practices, including code review, documentation, and pragmatic architectural decision-making.
  • Support and mentor more junior engineers through pairing, feedback, and knowledge sharing.
  • Identify areas where AI and new technologies can help in the newsroom and be able to propose ideas.
  • Actively participate in the process of requirements gathering and have the desire to have regular catch-ups with editors and journalists if that’s needed.

About You

We’re looking for someone curious, pragmatic, and motivated by impact. You enjoy working with messy real-world data, care deeply about reliability and clarity, and are comfortable operating in an environment where priorities can shift quickly around editorial deadlines.

Essential Skills

  • Strong experience as a backend engineer designing and building production-grade distributed systems and APIs in a cloud environment.
  • Excellent Python skills for developing backend services, system integration, and data processing.
  • Solid experience as a data engineer with a vital skill set in maintaining production data pipelines and using workflow orchestration tools like Apache Airflow.
  • Experience working with cloud platforms, particularly AWS.
  • Familiarity with modern engineering practices including version control, CI/CD, and automated testing.
  • The ability to communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Interest in exploring new technologies and approaches related to AI and Agentic AI.
  • An interest in journalism, investigations, or using data to answer real-world questions.
  • Data Science (DS) experience or education is highly valuable for this role, as we leverage AI heavily for many of our use cases.

Desirable Skills

  • Strong SQL skills and experience designing and working with relational and analytical databases.
  • Experience with databases such as BigQuery, Redshift, PostgreSQL, SingleStore, or MongoDB.
  • Experience working with unstructured or semi-structured data at scale.
  • A solid understanding of data modelling, data architecture, and trade-offs between different storage and processing approaches.
  • Comfort contributing to backend software engineering tasks beyond pure data pipelines.
  • Exposure to building internal tools or lightweight user-facing applications.
  • Experience with building simple user interfaces or/and the desire to do so (e.g., using frameworks like Streamlit).

Characteristics We Value

  • Inquisitive and analytical, with strong problem-solving skills.
  • Pragmatic and delivery-focused, able to balance technical quality with newsroom deadlines.
  • Collaborative and generous with your knowledge.
  • Comfortable working with ambiguity and evolving requirements.
  • A systems-level thinker who can see how individual pipelines and tools fit into a broader platform.
  • Motivated by learning and continuous improvement.
  • A collaborative team member who thrives in cross-functional environments and values collective success.

Our Technology

We don’t expect you to be an expert in everything. Our current stack includes:

  • Languages: Python, SQL
  • Cloud & Infrastructure: AWS
  • Data Pipelines & Orchestration: Apache Airflow, AWS ECS
  • Databases: BigQuery, Redshift, PostgreSQL, SingleStore, MongoDB
  • Version Control & CI/CD: GitHub, CircleCI
  • Frontend (small part of the role): Streamlit

This is a unique opportunity to use your technical skills to contribute to data journalism. You’ll be making content for the FT’s readership, using data to make news accessible, understandable, and impactful.

If this sounds like a role that aligns with your expertise and ambitions, we’d love to hear from you!

 

In Return, We Can Offer You

While flexible working requests will be considered, not all patterns are suitable for all roles.
